title: Tua Tagovailoa, A.J. Terrell Jr. and other Falcons speak to the media post-joint practice with Colts
text: Hey, how did it go out there today? >> Well, I think it went good uh with our first uh team, second team, third team series. Um you know, we we had some things that, you know, we wanted back and there's some things that uh we can look to clean up as well. But I think overall it went pretty well. Outside of that, we had our move the ball series in which, you know, some things happened. Can't can't can't turn the ball over. That's step number one. And uh you know from there just got to be on the same page with the receiver. >> Did he just have a good break on that or what? It looked like a good break from >> Yeah, he I mean he he had a good break. Um but I think the ball didn't help either. Just throwing it to his outside shoulder instead of his inside shoulder. >> Is that kind of the main coaching point on a play like that where it is a very quick route? You're you're kind of like seeing throwing before to beat the defender. Like what is the takeaway to improve there? >> Yeah, that that that's that's exactly it. Just ball placement. Yeah. Do you think this offense is close or do you think y'all are you glad you still got three weeks to go to get some stuff cleaned up? >> Well, I think regardless of how close or how far we think we are, the work still needs to be put in >> at the end of the day. And so if we have three more weeks, four more weeks, five more weeks, you know, it I mean it all correlates to us getting better, continuing to be on the same page before the real games start and before you know they start counting. >> I would imagine there are levels of comfort with a new offensive system. What stage of that are you in do you think now? >> Well, continuing to gain confidence with the guys, continuing to uh, you know, build confidence with the plays, uh, the scheme, things like that. So, it's a it's a daily thing that, uh, you continue to work on. The more reps you can get, the more comfortable you feel with it, and you move from there. >> Is this familiar to you? Is this close to what you've done in the past, or is this kind of new, the stuff that Kevin? >> Uh, ju well, I I would say just the the words are are different. Um, you know, uh, some words are the same as as other years, as I've said prior interviews, um, to where it's like I got to get some of those past concepts out of my head and bring in the new concepts for ones that were called, uh, that were similar in Miami. But outside of that, it's just repetition. >> How much do you believe you've kind of grown in the offense the last handful of weeks here in camp? >> Well, I think we're continuing to grow, right? figuring out the guys that run routes certain ways or how they run their routes, how they're coming out of it, things like that. The level of comfort in which guys thrive on certain routes. >> So things like that, >> the deliver the ability to deliver and receive feedback I'd imagine is really important throughout the course of the season. By now in training camp, what have you learned about Tommy Ree, Tanner, Kevin, the way they provide feedback, and how have you worked with them in that area? >> Yeah, I think they've been very helpful. um there's no holding back. They they'll tell you what it is and you move forward from that. I think as a player, as a professional football player, that's all you can ask for, right? Is constructive criticism and being able to take that and apply that moving forward, you know, is what they want to see and is what you you kind of want to see in yourself. You take that coaching point, you learn from it, you move forward with that. Um but it it's not just with the coaches. I would say it's also with the players getting them to communicate to me. um you know, and not kind of going to their coach like, "Hey, let's let's talk to each other. That's how we're going to, you know, go out there and be able to feel comfortable to see whatever route it is. If you're breaking this way or this way, like I got to know that, not not the coaches as as much as as we got to be on the same page." >> So, Tu, how do those conversations, you know, take place off off the field? >> Well, I would say after a play, I I just go up to the guys and talk to them like, "Hey, talk to me. Like, what did you think on that? What are you feeling? Did you like it? did you not like it? Things like that. And then their level of comfort with the play. Like if they don't they don't feel comfortable running that route. I don't want to waste my time trying to time that up with them. You know, if if they don't feel comfortable with that, then I'll tell Tommy or, you know, hey, like let's try to run more of these routes with with this guy or or whatnot. Um, and that's I I would say that's sort of the communication that that the guys give. And then, you know, it's vice versa. Vice versa, too. Do you believe you have enough time between now and week one, I guess, to reach the level you want to operate at in the offense? >> Well, I don't think you have a choice at the end of the day. You know, when when it's game time, it's game time. You better be ready. >> Where do you think you need to maybe improve, you know, between now and then the most? >> I think I need to improve every day. Um, I'm not looking at at a set goal of when I need to be improved by. I'm just looking to improve every day within this offense. Grow within the scheme. um grow within feeling comfortable in it enough to where man I can see everything. I can see where guys are going to be, what what he's calling if if uh the headset goes out, things like that. >> But you are like happy with the part of the process you're at right now like in your eyes you feel? >> Yeah, I I mean I would say there there's no other way to look at it. Um like you you got to be where you are right now and you know we'll learn from what what happened in practice today. We'll take the good as well as the bad. We'll move forward and we'll continue to grow that way. >> One of the uh one of the good I think it's fair to say Drake London legitimately, you know, moss a quarterback today. How how much faith does that give you as a quarterback to have a receiver who can do things like that out there on the field? >> Yeah. Well, you know, I've said it earlier in OTAA's like Drake, Kyle, couple of these other guys. I mean, they're they're bigger bodies, right? And so, you just throw it within the vicinity of them. They're going to go up and make a play for you. So, just your overall takeaways on on today, the first joint practice and how it went out there. >> No, it was good. Um, always, you know, getting a chance to go against another team. Um, it's good for the team and we just want to come out here and compete. Try to see where we at. Start fast, see where our communication at so we can line up and compete. >> And you know Kenny Moore fairly well, right? Because he was at your he's been at your house and stuff. Yeah. Uh, so has he over the years just has kind of helped have you learned anything about these these Colts players, the receivers like through that relationship? >> Um, no, not really. I haven't really, you know, asked him about none of that. But, you know, I definitely follow his game a lot. You know, he's been dominant over the over the last few years and um, just a key player in the NFL and I always be watching his game trying, you know, when I do see him, we do pick each other brain on, you know, techniques and things like that. And I know we've asked you a lot about your younger brother, but another young player who I've I've noticed a lot this training camp is Clark Phillips. How have you seen him grow and develop since you've known him? >> No, he a competitor, man. We got a lot of a lot of competitors on the team. Clark is one of them. Uh year in year out, he always >> uh you know, step to the table with the task of coming out here competing and um you that's what he do. He make plays uh you know they you know he he undersides and things like that, but he play big. So you know that's what we love on the outside. what what is kind of left for you to work on throughout the rest of training camp and and where are you in your process of getting ready for for the season? >> Yeah, just just competing and straining. That's the main thing for me. Just taking all my reps um and just maximizing them, you know, just trying to find ways to get the ball uh you know, communicate with my brothers at a high level so we could play slow the game down and play fast. >> Are you feeling the year 2eness of being in this system so far in training camp? >> Yeah. Yeah, it's it's good. It's always good to have uh the same DC, you know, coming into the next year so you can pick up on the little details, things that we weren't so sure on last year, just coming in this year, having rules for it and playing faster. Um, it's it's a plus. >> What were you happiest about today as far as the defensive performance and what are some things that you identified throughout this practice that you're going to want to work on? >> The energy. >> Yeah, >> I feel like we had a a good energy switch. Just being able to go against somebody else. Um, all the guys got to compete and, you know, just show new talent that we got. >> Yeah. Just let me get one real quick. Hey, how was it today? I know you probably already answered that. How was the act? >> No, it's it was good just being able to go against a new team. Um, and guys got to compete, you know, that's that's always a plus. Just being able to go against a new team instead of going against each other like we do all camp and just see where everybody at. looked like in the individual drills that offensive line had a pretty a pretty good day. What was your assessment of your group's kind of work out there today as well? >> Uh I think well I think it was great. Uh our intent was fantastic and guys came out ready to work today and uh you know it's a new environment you never been in and sometimes it's tough when you come out here but um I'm really thankful too. The Colts guys um it was just we were here to work today. There was no nonsense and like it was so great and guys didn't take things personal. There was no chippiness. Like it was really just a clean good workday to see a different look and for myself like against Grover Stewart and DeForest Buckner. Like those are two of the best starters in the NFL. And so to get work against them uh my love these days. >> I think you know in my personal mind dictionary iron sharpens iron. It's now you and Deforex Buckner as like the picture because that was incredible. Like what are some of the takeaways of working against him and getting better? Yeah, you see it on tape like you see the clips from the year and it's always funny like week one and week 17 are always tough for anxiety because you see a guy's whole year highlight film and so um ready to go today knowing that DeForest brings you know he's tall and long and so he can bring a speed to power with a long arm you know he's got the twitch to up and under and he can spin back um and he got me like it was fun we the first one he jumped offside showing that he was going inside on me and so I set that he was going inside after the reset that and he went out and then so the second time it was fun that I knew he thought he was going to do the first one so a little bit of a back and forth there and it was fun. It was just like what you like about these days in >> the game. >> Yeah. >> Uh seemed like the run game was working too and in some of the team periods. How are you feeling about the the run scheme and the plan and everything? >> Uh really good understanding of what we want as an offense and then to go out there and NLE did a great job communicating and so when he sets the table um it's really simple. I'm either going to who he's saying or one pass. So, he did a great job setting the table and echoing that communication across the board. >> How do you feel like it's going in your ramp up and getting kind of reactivated? >> Uh, it's going really well, man. Um, I have a great great uh plan around me. Uh, you know, just listening to the front office, what things they want me to do each day and, uh, just working in the weight room, working on the field to get myself back to like exactly where I want to be. >> What exactly happened to you? >> Um, had a knee surgery back in March. Um, just a clean up, nothing crazy. Um and just been, you know, just getting myself back to 100. Just kind of rehabbing throughout the offseason, but feeling a lot better now. >> Triceps is good. >> Yeah, tricep 100%. Um been healthy. It took about 12 weeks to heal and after that I was right back benching, doing everything else. So, it's it's good. >> How tough was it watching as Kent was getting started and you wanted to get out there and make an impression with your new squad? >> It's always really tough, you know, seeing your brothers out there playing ball and you know, you just on the sideline kind of rehabbing. But, um, you know, I just kept coming in, keeping my head down, working every day, and, uh, had a great, you know, great team, great group around me. So, uh, it just kept me, kept me motivated, and, uh, you know, just glad to be back out here. >> Like today against the Colts, >> it was a lot of fun. You know, they have a great defense, a lot of great players. Um, and it was a definitely a good challenge and we just got had fun out here competing. >> How difficult is it? Um, just overcoming physically, mentally in the rehab process, just, you know, getting back to full speed. Um it's it's it's really not difficult mentally if you if you come in with the right mindset every day just attack each day you know and uh just get better 1% better every day and uh that's what I do. Um and it's it's nothing new to me. I've had knee surgery before um in my time in my last team and you know same thing just attack each day try to get better and you know that's what I did. >> We've asked about the left quarterbacks a lot but you're the one that it's going to impact the most. Is that anything that you think about? >> Um yeah from time to time at the end of the day it's just ball. You know I just got to go out there and just do my job and uh help the team in every way I can.

title: Dewey Wingard Press Conference 8.18.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: A lot of ups and downs with Jacksonville over the years. From the 28 losing streak to the division title twice. What kind of locker room does it take to build that and are you seeing shades of that here? >> I am. I mean in the locker room it just takes ball players and that's all you can focus on and I've I've loved every second of since I've stepped on this building and in this locker room. I haven't seen a single ego. There's no divas. It's like all these guys are such good guys and good people and um that was one of our things in Jacksonville that got us over the top was we just had dudes that cared about each other and were good people and go to work every day and grind. So, I've seen nothing but great things from all these guys since I stepped in the building and they've welcomed me in and it's felt great. So. >> You're known for your relentless approach to practice during [clears throat] games. How is it practicing alongside a guy like Budda Baker? Does he match your energy? >> Hell yeah. It's so fun. Like he's just a grinder. He reminds me a lot of a guy I was with in Jacksonville. I was with Rashaan Jenkins and they're just vets that are still grinding. Like they're not the vet that's like oh you know I don't have to work hard anymore. I'm me. Look at me. Blah blah blah. Like Budda's one of the coolest guys I've met and he's he's just out there grinding every day. He's with you. And when you're out there with him you feel like you're with a guy who's in his first year who wants it just as bad as everyone else and I think that's one of the coolest things about him so far. >> We've seen in different practices you and Trey McBride you know going at it. Obviously friendly competition, but how has practicing against him made you better in your job? >> 100%. That actually goes back. Me and Trey go back pretty far. That goes There there's most of the bad blood is gone, but we go back pretty far. CSU Wyoming and you know, even last year playing in the game against him. I know he was mic'd up and all the all the people in the video room got heard a lot of things that I said, so thankfully it wasn't broadcasted publicly, but Trey's a stud, absolute stud. I'm thankful honestly to line up every day, you know, we're playing man and I'm man on two and there's Trey. So I'm like, all right, I I can go out there and cover anybody because you know, he's he's a special special player, truly is deserving of all the accolades and stuff and again kind of like Buddha, like Trey is about his business and he's a competitor. He's not he's you could ask him he's he's he would say I haven't made it. So all these guys just continue to grind so hard and I think you know, Sundays are going to happen we're either going to win or we're going to lose, but these guys work their ass off and it's not a you know, doom and gloom, you know, we suck like there's no like it's not like that like these guys are professionals and this is a professional locker room and you know, I I really like what we got, especially Trey. >> How did it start with Trey in college and how how intense did it get back then? >> It started when I was an you know, absolute demon that that I was at Wyoming and he spears me in the back when I'm laying on the ground after I make a tackle. So there were yeah, there was some bad there was some bad blood there. And then Trey would tell you he's like, well, he was their best player. I was trying to you know, I was trying to get him out of there, but he he was a freshman when I was a senior, so I only got to play against him one time, but I remembered it. No, but it was awesome and then like I said playing against him last year, he's just a like he's a competitor and you can see how hard these guys compete whether it's on the field or in ping pong or in golf and I know Mike has belabored the point about you know, competition, but that's true. Like I you know, Buddha plays ping pong and they're all just competitors. They they they want to win, they want to compete and I think that's going to be one of the things this year that we might look at and say that's what gave us an edge. >> So, what was that moment like when you first saw Tram when you got here? >> It was It was kind of like the Step Brothers moment where it was like Okay, I'm over it. Sort of thing. So, and it was funny cuz he was like the first guy I saw when I came in and signed my contract, and it was just like All right, man. Yeah, I'm over it. I'm over it. So, we're cool now. >> In in your career, obviously you've had a couple years where you started quite a bit, but you had a number of years where you didn't. Um it looks like you're in that position right now. You obviously did it last year. Was there a time where you were getting frustrated that that wasn't happening for you, or is it just that that was your timeline? >> For sure. That there's I mean, I've always seen myself as a starter and a baller and a starting safety in the NFL. I mean, when I was in college, I didn't even play special teams. Like I started all four years as a true freshman through senior year. So, when I first got in the league undrafted, it was kind of like Okay, like I I was going to play special teams, whatever, but always in the back of my mind I'd always been going like this. Like when I get my chance, I'm going to go. And then I got it, and you know However uh front office sees you and a coaching staff sees you, whatever, you just, you know, be a pro and do your stuff, but I see myself as a dog, and I just go play my game, and you know, I've been on winning teams as a starter, and I can go do it, and I can be a guy, and that's how I see myself. So, that's how I'm going to be here. Um whether I keep the job, don't keep the job, play special teams, I'm going to go 100%, but I'm going for it. So. >> If you all can get creative with the defense, where are you picking up on where those are most beneficial for you guys? >> Yeah, I mean, he's really a good coach. Like he's really a good coach. Same with Christian Garcia, my my secondary coach. Those two guys are really, really good young coaches and they're really smart and I think they're just starting to come into their own, but to your question, he just schemes things up for us so well with every single call, there's hey, this is how we're going to disguise and then this is how we're going to shift and then they're not going to count you in the box and then you're going to be a free hitter on the ball and that's all the things that he does with us in terms of disguise and how to manipulate the offense and then show one look, give another look and confuse them and make the quarterback, you know, bat the ball and then he's sacked. So, I think that's what he's been doing with us um and I think it's really helped and I think you guys will see it on Sundays. >> Andrew, even as an established pro, like how much do you look around the league at guys at your position and kind of, you know, observe, uh keep tabs on, whatever you do to maybe, you know, help you with your craft? >> Absolutely. I mean, you that's what you do. You try to find, you know, the Second the season ends, coaches are watching other teams' schemes and trying to learn things and players are doing the same thing, watching other guys, seeing how they're doing things and um you know, I like To be honest with you, I was watching a lot of Arizona Cardinals film this past off season. It's kind of funny. Just watching Buddha and watching uh Tom Jaylen Thompson was who when he was here, Rabbit. Just how they did things. I liked how they played. So, and it was kind of funny. I got the call from them like a week after I was watching Cardinals film, but yeah, you definitely you study. That's what you got to do. >> What do you like about Rabbit's game and then maybe and and added on to that about a guy like Keim Crawford, too? >> I This whole secondary room is awesome. Like awesome. Like everyone's bought into the culture. Everyone, there's a style of play with these DBs, how we play. Like it's been the most fun. Honestly, some of the most fun I've ever had in the NFL so far, but Rabbit, he's awesome. Like he's He kind of reminds me of a younger me. Like he's just a grinder. Like he doesn't care. He's not worried about outside noise, this or that. Even with me and him, we're like call it a battle, training camp battle, whatever you want. No one's focused on that. Everyone's focused on going out to practice and getting better at football. And however the chips fall, they fall. But there's no no egos, no nothing. And Rabbit's a guy who just goes out and grinds, and he's a great player. And I think he's one of those guys who when Sundays come, I think he's the type of guy that like really like shows his stuff on game day. And then Bug is just a psycho. Like Bug is like like I'd be scared of Bug. Like and he's just violent. Like violent, bad intentions, and >> [clears throat] >> sky's the limit for him. Sky's the limit for every guy in that secondary, but both of them young guys that they got the sauce, and they'll keep getting better, and they make me better. Hopefully I make them better, and it's just the whole room is just awesome. >> Dennis Gardeck was loved here, and Zaven was going to his other day maybe with the hair and the helmet on. Uh getting confused maybe at first. Have people called you Dennis when you first got here? Like a little confused with the hair flowing out of the helmet? >> Yeah, I mean a little bit. Dennis looked obviously, you know, he's got the like sharp teeth and Viking stuff. So I I hope I don't look like that, but just kidding, Dennis. I love you. But Dennis Yeah, no, Dennis was awesome. The long hair, like I just love a good psycho white guy. Like and you need one of those guys on your team, and that's what Dennis was in Jack- Jacksonville, and I think I can be that guy here, for sure. >> How have you and Buddha gotten about building a rapport off the field? Cuz obviously you guys have to play off each other so much. >> Yeah. >> How do you guys How How have you done that over the last few months? >> Well, I don't have enough status yet to be on the Cardinals tour to get into their their foursome to play golf. So that would be my main rapport building exercise. But so not for now, I just I mean we just chatted up. Like he's like I said, he's one of the coolest dudes I've met. I feel like I have become like close, close friends with all these guys like super fast. And Buddha being one of them just like I can literally chop it up. Talk about anything, life, this or that. Me and you know, me and Buddha were talking when we were at the Wigwam about how we met our, you know, fiancées and all that sort of stuff. So that that's just kind of I think that is how you build rapport the most is just like truly showing yourself to someone. And I think that's like I said back what I said earlier about this locker room like everyone is so open to each other and so cool and so raw. It's honestly one of the coolest locker rooms I've ever been in. Like everyone is just so cool. Like truly like cool as hell. Like all the guys are real, authentic. So I think that's been the biggest thing. And when you're that close with people, it makes playing with each other a lot more fun. And I've been on teams where you go out on Sunday and you feel like you're out there by yourself. And that's not fun. And that doesn't make you feel good, nor does it make you play good. And some of the best teams I've been on have been the coolest dudes I've been with. And you're like out there and you feel like you're in college again cuz you you know, you you grind with these guys, you talk to these guys, you care about these guys. And when we go out there practice, it's fun because we care about each other. And it's fun to play with guys you care about. And that only just feeds into the beast even more. So yeah. >> Sometimes it can be hard for a first year head coach to really command the respective of a locker room. But what's your guys' been uh in so far as buying with Mike Vrabel so far? >> there's been he's been awesome. It's been the complete op like he first day of OTAs, he commands it. And it's not the sort of like you know, he walks in and it's the drill sergeant sort of command. Like he's cool. He's relaxed. Like he's just a good dude. Like I said, a good dude again. But he commands it just and he's funny. Like he's a funny dude. And guys buy into that. But he you can tell he has command on the side, so and obviously his his track record speaks for itself. You know, he's had nothing but success wherever he's been, and he's freaking smart. You know, we get into these walkthroughs, and he'll pause the pause the drill and start talking to the offense, and and I'm just like, "Damn. Like, damn." This guy knows his Excuse me. This guy knows his stuff. Bleep that out. Um but he he's impressive, and you know, they kicked the crap out of us last year in London, 35 to 6. So, you know, he doesn't ever hesitate to, you know, make sure I remember that. I He knows his stuff, so. But he's super impressive, and I I think he'll do wonders for all these guys on offense, for sure.

title: HC Mike LaFleur Press conference 8.18.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: You would mention when you break camp out at the stadium that one of the things you guys had to do is kind of maneuver through the heat a little bit. I know it's only been a few days, but how is that been going for you and the team? >> Uh learning experience for sure. Um you know, so we obviously this will be the the third practice of a four-day block. Um went out there in the morning the other day. Uh what I learned was, you know, just it's the amount of time out there, right? And so stretching, doing our walk-through, stuff like that cuz it didn't feel bad and our guys were good, but just the amount of time we were out there. So, we'll adjust today. Obviously, it's a 9:00 a.m. practice, but we'll start uh in the bubble and what I like to call the tent. So, if I refer to this as a tent, um that's what it is, but we'll do our walk-through, we'll do our stretch, we'll do some routes and air and stuff like that, and then we'll transition to get our team out there cuz we have to, you know, I told the guys like, I get it. Um you know, week one inside, week two inside, but week three's up at Levi's. And I said, "Hey, we're going to leave our feet for a second, but but we do have an obligation and understand why we're practicing outside." Um one cuz we can't practice on the turf every single day cuz of of the knees and all those kind of things, but two we we do play outside. And back in 2024, I believe it was the hottest recorded game ever at Levi's Stadium, and it was it was at like 99 or something like that, but like anyone that stood on that sideline at Levi's in September, it might as well be like 150 um for for the the visiting team. Um I get I'm exaggerating right there, but you understand what I'm saying. So, there is a reason not just we're going to go do it to do it. >> We saw Trey Benson back out there yesterday. Is is he ready to start participating in 11-on-11s >> Not not quite yet, but he is uh he's progressing well. >> When he does get back on the field over these next 12 days here, what are you looking to see from him? >> Yeah, it's it was one of those disappointing things because um one, it was he was happy to get out there. Uh you talk about, you know, a guy like Star the other day and and you know, I mean, there's a human element to this thing and and everyone's is going to feel different to people. Uh Trey was just happy to get to to be out there. Um since I got here in February, he's putting in a lot of work behind the scenes that people haven't seen. And he's just every single day like it's I didn't I didn't work out too much in the morning, but anytime I did in the off season, he was always in there every single day. And uh so he's putting in a lot of work and then I thought, you know, like I said, I I think I was quoted a few weeks ago, one of his first runs he fell. And that's very kind He hadn't played football in forever and then all of a sudden like you're a quick learner. And then the next time he got the ball, a little bit better then he ends up hitting one off the left side, blocked well, but he hit it where it needed to go and you could see the explosiveness. And so you're like it was just good to see and I thought he stacked a few days where he was just uh continuing to prove and then all of a sudden we get a little swelling out of nowhere and uh and it sucked. Um but again, he just went right back to work to to, you know, uh with our staff to to make sure that that goes down to get back on the field. So, to answer your question, what are you trying to see? What he did the first time where he just got a little bit better every single rep, every single snap, um every single day, you know, cuz that's all he can do. That's all he can control is just going out there and uh you know, putting his best foot. >> What's your plan for the quarterbacks in the first team on Saturday? >> Um I'm going to hold that till Thursday. I promise I'll let you guys know Thursday cuz uh our guys will know on Thursday. They kind of know. I mean, it's not like I but I just I just haven't announced it to the team yet. So, um >> You've seen a lot of rotation between Cody Simon and Jack Gibbons at the inside linebacker spot next to Mac Wilson. How do you think their um skill sets going to complement each other? What do you like out of that battle so far? >> Yeah, I think they're just steady players, you know, I think they understand what's going on. Ball matters to them. Um playing uh you know, like I think those two obviously they've done a good job when Max in there, but there's times that, you know, Max not going to be in there. Um and so uh you know, just those guys working in unison together. Um again, they take a lot of pride in that whether the green dot or not. Again, steady players that just are understand football, understand scheme. Still room to improve for both those guys, but pleased with where they're at. >> Is that a position where you need to I feel like you need to have like one guy who is the starter and is always out there next to Mack or can you have a platoon at that I guess I feel like it's not a spot >> It's a it's a great It's a great question and I don't think there's a I don't think there's a a right or wrong answer to that. You know, I think you could say I mean it's just like a starting five in basketball. Like some weeks it just makes sense to go with a little bit more length or some weeks it may make more sense to have the shooters out there just depending on the team. So, I think those are those are going to be good problems to to discuss going into each week. So, but >> you think that's typically a position where teams have a you know, guys who play Well, I guess that second guy wouldn't play 100% of snaps, but pretty close to it. >> Yeah, well, I can't say you're you're dating me back a little bit. I >> I mean, do you like do you see a wide receiver or running back >> You're saying they don't? >> Feel like an inside linebacker I feel like most teams kind of pick their two guys and and those guys >> I I I agree with you. I 100% agree with you and I I guess I don't totally know that you know, it's working in unison with somebody, all right? You just you you you feel people. Like I go back to Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw, right? Two guys that have have played really good ball together and they just they they work off each other. They can feel the space. They can feel when someone's maybe out of out of position and they cover for it and it's just like this athletic intuition that these guys have. So, I'd say that's probably the you know, the most accurate answer. The easy answer is well, one's just better than the other guy and it just makes sense to have him out there. And so, again, I think with with those two that we're talking about, they both have a unique skill set that I think can complement Mack in this defense. And then, you know, we'll kind of see where we're going to go going into week one, but this is a good question. >> You mentioned uh I obviously you're going to have a plan for the quarterbacks whatever. You have a plan for everybody. I'm curious big picture like for you in your time in the NFL and watching how coaches have dealt with who plays in the preseason and how much, has your philosophy changed over the years? Does it like do you think the league's philosophy has changed over the years on how all this is kind of gone and and how much of this is like sports science and how much of this is kind of feel? >> It's uh yes, it has changed drastically. uh in Atlanta played four preseason games and you that third game for the league was like the mock game. You went out, you played a whole half of football with your starters, offense, defense, and then actually came out in the second half and at least, you know, what it felt like to go back inside, make some adjustments, and then get your body and mind right to go play that third quarter. And that was just kind of the league and some teams did it for for two games. Um in terms of playing over over a half. Um I'm not going to mention those teams. I think we can probably all kind of visualize who those teams were. We always would play our guys for for, you know, um two games, the second game and the third game and not the first and the fourth. you know, I was thinking back to 2019 with with rookie Deebo Samuel. I mean, he played all four and we played him into the fourth quarter in some games. Um and then it just over time it it just is kind of dwindled a little bit. And some teams are still doing a little bit more than others. Um you know, 2023 I get to LA and and you know, we played our starters in New York in 2023 get to LA and Sean uh historically has not played them. But when he get first got there, they did. Like Goff and all those guys played in when they when he first got there. All those guys, Robert Woods, um uh Cooks wasn't there yet. Uh Sammy Watkins, uh Todd Gurley, all those guys played. And then just through time and being in that system and in the you know, the roster being somewhat consistently the same, he started to the to take those guys out and then in in '23, albeit he was a fifth round pick, but we knew he was going to be our starting Z, Puka Nacua played a half of football for us, you know, and we saw it for a half and thought to ourselves, I think we've seen enough. And he didn't play again, you know, and so um yeah, it's it's the league has evolved with it. Um I still don't know if there's a right and wrong answer to it all. I I I do think rookies uh need to feel what it's like to go out there and and play in the speed. Um and uh you know, and some guys think they even need more than that in terms of the vets. So. >> Why do you think that training has evolved this way that it is to where it is now? >> Uh cuz cuz the games don't count, but they do matter, you know, and and and so it's like guys don't want to lose them for the regular season. I I I don't even want to get into some of the the the data. I'm sure you guys can probably get it somehow, but the um we did the the the owners' meetings, they talked about joint practices versus playing in the preseason versus not playing in the preseason. And I I I can't quote it cuz I don't know the numbers exact off the head, but it was like, you know, if you get two joint practices in, that's the equivalent of playing the two preseason because it is a height it is an amped-up environment. Um you're not tackling, but it's just it's the amped-up uh environment that you get that can that for some reason the data says if you end up having those joint practices, you have a less injury risk going into the first 4 weeks of the season. Is that by coincidence? I don't know. I'm just going off of what smarter people are telling us. Um and then if you're not doing the joint practice, okay, you're doing one, then maybe they should play in one game. If not doing any joint practices, which basically no one does anymore, then they need to play a certain amount if you want to, you know, follow this this model. So, um again, everyone's going to take their own, you know, deal with it and go from there. >> Just to confirm on Jeremiah, the plan is not for him to undergo surgery, right? >> Yeah, there's no surgery. >> No. >> Would you consider doing two joint practices next year? >> Yeah, uh I would love to do two joint practices. I'd love to do three joint practices. Uh what I learned uh when I got here in February is a lot of those coaches that were already hired already had their joint practices Yeah, I did it happens fast. Literally, I'm like the day I was hired, I was already getting calls about joint practices. It which you know, that's one of those I mean, it's it's funny, but it's it's like, "Okay, now I got it." Like the moment the season's done, call the people that you know, and and get get going with it. The thing I did learn is um people don't want to come here and joint practice. It's too it's too hot, you know, so that's why they've never had it here. So, no, it it we will always have to go on the road to do it. Then you say, "Well, why can't you do it at Glendale?" Well, a joint practice there's two teams, so there's 180 guys out there, but there's only one field. So, we're never going to be able to host a joint practice here in in Arizona, but that doesn't mean that we can't go do it other places. And that is something that we will be doing moving forward. >> We talked to Marvin Harrison >> He's trying to do. You still got to get an agreement with the other teams. >> I was saying I got to get Marvin Harrison Jr. to blocking in the run game earlier in training camp. You said that blocking is mandatory for your receivers. Is it hard at all to get those guys to buy in as opposed to other positions? And I guess the second question is what's it mean for your star receiver and Marvin Harrison Jr. to be so bonded that maybe some of the other guys can take into that. >> Um I'll answer your second one. No, it doesn't mean much that he's bought into blocking. That's just what we do. So, um him all the way down to the 90th guy, if you are an eligible on the perimeter, you better learn how to block. Um uh and and no, it's never it's never an issue. Like again, you get what you emphasize, and it's it's you know, we make it pretty clear right away. Because it's not just because we're we're tough and we're going to do it's No, that's how you that's how you run the football. Like you can't just rely on the five guys and a running back to go run the football. If If want to effectively run the football, it takes all 11. It takes the quarterback getting us in the right play and carrying out his fakes. It takes obviously the offensive line and tight ends executing. It takes the backs being disciplined. And then again, after you know, after that going and being who they are. It takes the you know, the receivers on the perimeter getting it done, getting sticky, and getting physical. >> With Josh Sweat's long hair, it appears he's building right now with you guys. >> Oh, yeah. Had a great talk with him about a cool restaurant in Arcadia today. It was sweet. >> You were saying that you can tell that Marvin seems happier playing right now. Like there's someone who doesn't trash talk, is is pretty in the zone when he's on the field. Where can you see that with Marvin? >> You know, I I I would I haven't been here with him, right? And so I I've seen the same Marvin. I've seen a guy that just comes in and he's he's steady every single day. He's super intelligent, super smart. Probably gets bored in our meetings cuz it it just makes sense to him. Like, you know, like when to cut a split, when to open a split a little bit, all those kind of things. And so, that's all I've seen. Just a guy that I enjoy and and we enjoy as coaches working with. And and a guy that I see interacts with his teammates who they like working with him and and being teammates. So, that's all I've seen and and a guy that every single day is trying to get better. And you know, we talked about the ball get off. That that that was first and foremost for us in terms of the pass game. Obviously, the run game. I'm glad that he's talking about that with you guys. But now, it's he's been a joy to work with and you know, we'll continue to try to point that arrow up. >> You treat him like the first smart player you've had in your career. When you have guys at that level mentally, how do you How do you How do you handle them? How do you like keep them and kind of make sure that they are not getting bored and kind of being engaged in learning? >> Yeah, I mean, it's part of our job. I mean, is to give them a reason to want to come in every single day, too. Like, yeah, it is their job, but like you want to come in here and have the urgency and and the want to like I can't wait to get to work. And and so, part of that's just, you know, how we you know, instruct our and construct our meetings and who's speaking and making sure it's not always the same person and delivering the message but in different ways, you know, it's got to be similar but it can be different, you know, in terms of how these guys are taking in that message. So, you know, my biggest not issue, but my biggest thing with some of the guys that just understand ball at extremely high levels don't overthink it, either. Not saying Marvin does, I'm just talking about smart players in general is hey, it's still ball at the end of the day. There's 22 variables, there's officials. It's like this is this is, you know, the structure of what we're trying to get done, but when that ball snapped, you got to go play, man. Like you got to go play. It's people that think that this game is going to be black and white, it's not. There you got to be able to be comfortable living in the gray. We're going to try to provide as much clarity to these guys for every single thing that we do with the understanding that man, that ball snapped, a lot of things can happen, you know. So, that's that's typically when you got someone as smart as as Marvin and some of those other guys, that's what kind of what you look for. Are they are they over analyzing? Are they overthinking? Is it paralysis by analysis? And then, you know, and then kind of take it from there.

title: Jalen Brooks Press Conference 8.18.26 | Az Cardinals
text: when you get to this time of year, I mean, obviously you're in a different position than maybe some other receivers, a Marvin or a Mike, like how do you go into preseason games? How do you look at them? How do you approach them >> for you? >> Yeah. So, uh I mean, this is year four. Uh came from Dallas, uh had three preseasons over there. And you know, just the guys that I've been around in that room. Uh you know, you guys got like CD Lamb, Brandon Cooks at the time, Michael Gallop, Jaylen Tolbert, and then uh George Pickkins and everything. Uh just seeing guys like that and being around that for so long. um you you start to play free, you know, and then uh just being over here is, you know, um in a different room, but I still got guys that are still attacking each and every day uh with a competitive mindset and everything. But I mean, I I think it just goes along with the years and the experience and everything. So, I I I feel like that's how it is, just the time and the the work that's put in. Are you the type of guy that might put more pressure on yourself going into these preseason games knowing that the opportunities in the regular season might not always be there, but in the preseason you know you're going to get yours. >> Uh I'm more of the type like shoot I have an expectation for myself. I wouldn't say like the pressure, but uh you know, I mean, some would say like pressure is a privilege. And it's just been uh very nice, you know, the the amount of targets that I get. You know, it's just it's it just feels more rewarding than, you know, more pressure cuz I know I've I've worked my tail off to put myself in this position and everything. And I just know throughout the years and everything that uh I've always been wanting to be in this position. And you know, like I said, like I I mean, I came from CD getting 15, you know, something targets a game. It's just like how does he how does he go about that and how does he handle that throughout practice, whether that be through a game and everything? So, just taking stuff like that from his game and other receivers that's over there. Do >> you ever find yourself doing the math like, all right, these guys will make the team, these guys might make the team, where do I fit in all this? Like, >> uh, no, I don't really start to count numbers. Uh, I mean, obviously last year, I mean, we we had a pretty stacked room in Dallas. Uh, I mean, it was just like more shoot, I'm going to just go out there, ball out, you know what I mean? Uh, but I have the most up confidence that, and I told this to receivers, uh, when it was my time to talk to them, like I have the confidence I could go in any room in the NFL and I will earn a spot there. Um, and I feel like this game is 80% confidence, man. As long as you have the right mindset, I feel like the sky can be the limit for you. And like I said, I mean, I was around great people and everything. They helped craft my game and everything. So, it's been good, you know, to learn from other people. I mean, it's been a hell of an experience to learn from Mike and Marv and everything. KB. Um, just the way Mike goes about his game and everything. Just like I'll come in to try and sub in for him during two minute, but he's like he's trying to push himself each and every day. He was like, "Nah, no, I'm good." So, just seeing that, you know, me and him same draft class, you know? You know what I mean? So, um, just being able to see that and his grind and everything and I I love Mike. I I respect his game. I told him that the first time I came over here, like, man, I love your game, you know? So, uh, just being able to go off of other people's stuff. >> What is your what is your kind of your your experience and background in in special teams? Because obviously when you start getting down the depth chart a little bit, that's something that's going to be important. Like, how do you kind of approach that? What have you done? >> Yeah. So, I've always been a four-phaser and that's help that actually helped me get drafted to the Cowboys actually. Uh, you know, I had a had a pretty good year at South Carolina, but it was more special teams wise. So, uh, in Dallas, I done started at Gunner. I done started uh front line on KO. Uh, I done started at almost every spot in on kickoff. I do plum return and I even came off the edge on um on pat block. So, uh, I had John Fossil and then Nick Soren up in Dallas. And John Fossil, if y'all know him, aka Bones and, uh, Steu, Coach Stew, man, they they just instilled that special teams, but I knew how important that was. My, uh, my final year, well, really once I got to the SEC, uh, because, you know, some people make a living off of special teams. And I had a great mentor, CJ Goodwin, that just retired over there in Dallas. Uh, you know, just being able to compete over there. We had a very very good special teams unit over there. You know, we had uh Kavonte Turpin back there returning. So, it was all about getting that getting the uh getting the return started and everything. Uh and then just bring that over here, you know. Uh now we got Goi and I mean he's a huge special teams co uh coach and everything. So, just trying to exhaust all of my abilities on that on all types of teams, whatever that that may be. for two [snorts] games and camp in general, what do you feel like you've shown this staff that you're capable of? >> Uh just being able to be versatile, uh you know, line up in a line up in a slide, line up outside, line up in a boundary. Uh and then just being able to stretch the field. Uh just uh just trying to instill that confidence, you know, that they have faith in me. And um like I have nothing but respect for the way that they try and give me the ball and everything. Uh so it's really just building that confidence. I know essentially that will come down to what it's really about is who they have the most confidence and and the most trust. >> Explosive down the left sideline in the Hall of Fame game. You take that hit. Probably the hardest you've ever been hit and take us through that hold on to that ball. >> Uh yeah, so I'm happy Carson brought me in a little bit because that actually was able to uh give eyes to that safety which made a hell of a play cuz he came from the whole opposite half. So, shout out to number 22 cuz he he flew over there. Uh, but yeah, so Carson bringing me in a little bit on that throw actually gave me the ability to get vision on him and I was like, man, I'm going to just catch this and just shield it. And I that was the that's what I was so excited. Like I was just so grateful I was able to shield my body for sure cuz if I wasn't able to shield my body, I don't know how that would have I probably would have been laying there for a little minute. But uh yeah, man. I was able to shield my body, man. Uh I mean it's it's football. you got to know how to take a hit and everything and I'm just happy I was able to do that. >> How's it been building [snorts] that chemistry with Carson and just what's been standing out to his game. >> Yeah. So, uh, no, it's been really good, man. Carson, uh, he knows a lot of ball. Uh, it was even some things that was in OTAAS. Um, I had a crossing route and he threw me like a back shoulder which was very elite and high level, but I wasn't expecting that from him at first, but he was like, "Hey, you see?" I was like, "Yeah, I see it for sure." But I didn't know you was going to be on that type of time, you know what I mean? So, uh, just getting those reps in and everything. So, now I could go into a game like, "Hey, you remember that rep that we had?" Boom. You know, uh, so just building that, uh, chemistry with him. I mean, it's been really good, man. Uh, he's been very coachable, you know? Uh, I mean, obviously it's rookie, but like he's very experienced and everything. He's been in the moment. He's very calm in the huddle. Uh, during a Hall of Fame game, like it was no panic at all. Uh, so I got I got much respect for him, man. >> You've been around [snorts] for a minute. When you see a guy like him coming in, six years of college, where do you see that experience kind of translate this early? >> Yeah. So, I think it it's just some people it takes them two, three, four years to get it. You know what I mean? You know what I mean? Like really be calm in the huddle. But him having that experience in college, he's just so confident in himself and he's just so easy. like if say like there's chaos in huddle, he can calm down the huddle. He can elevate everybody's game and everything. So, I just I think that helps him get to that that spark of what where he the coaches may need him to be at a little bit earlier instead of having to wait those two, three, four years.

title: Dennis Allen: 'Success breeds success' | Press Conference
text: Yeah, listen. Fire away. What you got for me? >> Coach, >> yesterday you guys were in diamond. You had you were in diamond. You had Dylan and Jaylen out there and then you had respectfully four guys that were not intended to be front line guys for I know man. I know you certainly not going to make excuses, but does it become challenging to just build the unit with all the treatment you guys are dealing with right now? Yeah, look, I mean, it it it's a challenge to to build that uh you know, unit together. Um and yet, as I've said before, it's a great opportunity for some of these guys that might not have gotten that that chance uh to be out there with the ones and and see what they can do. Look, I you know, there was a point in time where we didn't think we were going to be counting on Nan Wright last year. um and because of the injury situation, he got a lot of opportunities. He continued to take advantage of those opportunities and got better and really ended up being a starting corner for us. Um so, um it's it's not the recipe that we intended to cook the meal with and yet um you know, we've got to we've got to deal with what we have and and uh try to get the guys that are out there. We got to we got to get them better. yesterday practice tomorrow. You guys are going against Burrow, Chase Higgins, some pretty good players, pretty good offense. What are you looking for out there from your guys? >> Yeah, look, I mean, I think it's going to be a a heck of a test for us. Um, you know, u they've got a really good offense, um, MVP caliber quarterback, um, offensive player of the year, MVP caliber wide receiver. T Higgins is a heck of a player. Uh, Brown's a hell of a running back, you know, Gaseki at the tight end position. And so they've got a lot of weapons and a lot of things that they can do on offense. U all five of their uh offensive linemen are returning. So, um it'll be a it'll be a great test for us and I'm just looking for us to go out there and compete uh and see where we stack up against, you know, what I think is probably going to be one of the better offenses in our league. Yesterday, Press Taylor was talking about how for the joint practice, he wants to see how like the left tackle, for instance, does one-on-one, and he's not going to give him help just so he could kind of gauge it knowing the quarterback can't get hit. What are you specifically going to look for on defense in the joint practice? >> Yeah. Well, I I think our ability to line up and cover elite receivers in our league um and and see where we're at in terms of being able to do that. you know, we're we we play some talented uh receiving cores in our own division. So, uh, this will be a great test for us again, like I said, and an opportunity for us to, you know, step up and, uh, and see where we're at and gives us gives us a chance to evaluate where we're at as a defense, what we can do well, what we need to, you know, potentially look to as we get into game planning thoughts, you know, how we're going to be as a defense and and and how we're going to scheme. Dennis, are you hopeful Kyler will be good to go week one? Um, >> confidence there? >> Yeah, listen, I just know he's going through the rehab process. Um, really quite honestly, I I haven't that that's something that I can't really put a lot of thought into right now. You know, I've got to focus on the guys that we have. Um, you know, I'm I'm I'm hopeful that we'll be able to get him back sooner rather than later. And yet, that's not anything that I control. So, my pure focus has been on uh the guys that are out there and and uh and what we're doing with those guys. >> Outside of his rehab process, what has his role been in the offices and meetings? >> All all the meetings. Um you know, he he's involved in everything uh that we're doing from a meeting process uh standpoint, but uh has not been involved in anything physically uh with the team. Yeah, I apologize if you've been asked this, but Ben seemed excited after Saturday's game about Chroma's growth showing up in a game setting. Yeah. >> What's been notable to you about watching his arc? I >> I I think this I think um you know, he he's really taken to uh the coaching and and the way that we're trying to teach, which is a little bit different than what we were doing last year. Um we're trying to be a little bit more uh attacking and a little bit more aggressive. uh you know, attack the line of scrimmage a little bit more. And so there's some key coaching points in being able to do that. Uh and I think he's one of the guys that um has really just stuck with it and really tried to focus on doing those things exactly how we're we're coaching it. Um and him along with you know a few others when you see it and and and they see the results of man when you do it exactly right um you have success and so that therefore success breeds success. So, um, I I I've been really impressed with with what I've seen and, you know, hopefully throughout the course of these joint practices, we'll we'll get a little bit more look at him, uh, you know, maybe even maybe working, you know, with the ones and and see, you know, as you start to increase the level of competition. What does it look like? Does it look the same? You know, so uh, excited to see that. >> Coach, I know Tyreek has been out for a few days now, but what was your evaluation of him through this point in camp? And when do you maybe expect to get him back? Um, in terms of when to get him back, I don't know that answer. That's that's a medical question. I'm sure, uh, you know, Ben would be able to give you a little bit better information on that. Um, I I do think that he's, uh, I think he's he's improving. Um, and, uh, you know, I I try not to get into all these like, you know, evaluations of exactly where a guy's at or what he's doing. Um, you know, I really focus on what do we do each and every day. I've seen the guy get better. Um, obviously we need him out here so he can continue to improve. Um, and u, you know, when he when he is um, we'll get him back out there and get him going. >> I guess a better question to that I'm sorry, Larry. I guess a better question to that might be, do you feel like he's responded well to the things you all challenged him on? >> I think so. Yeah, I I I think so. I think so. And and listen, as with a lot of guys, it's always a work in progress. You know, we have to stay on it. he has to stay on it himself. We have to stay on it, you know, in terms of coaches. Um, and uh, and I think he's done a better job of that. >> Malik Muhammed's growth and what do you want to see from him in Cincinnati, especially in the game? >> Uh, I I think just I mean, it's cliche and it's simple, but, you know, just continue to get a little bit better each and every day. Um, I think he's got the right mindset. Um, I think he's I think he's got some confidence. I think he's aggressive in coverage. Um, you know, and again, this will be a great test to go up against these receivers and see see where we're at. >> Dennis, uh, uh, Benny said earlier that he want to make sure his offense is up to the level to test the defense. Uh, he wasn't satisfied before. Have you seen that improvement and what have you seen and Caleb's growth? What areas have you seen him grow compared to last year or earlier this camp? Well, look, I I mean, I think offensively we're we're night and day above where we were at this point in time in training camp last year. Um, and I think we're probably ahead of where we were at the end of the season last year from an offensive standpoint. Um, I think Caleb's understanding of the offense, command of the huddle, his communication, you've seen all of that improve. Um, and then, you know, to go along with that, you see him getting through progressions and getting to the right spots, you know, and, uh, I think Ben said this, you know, last year, but, you know, growth is not a linear process. It's kind of like the stock market a little bit. There's going to be some ups and downs, but, you know, hopefully it continues to grow, uh, you know, as you go along. And, and I've seen I've seen a lot of growth out of him. um you know and and and uh I'm looking forward to you know seeing what he can do in these joint practices. I'm looking forward to seeing what he's going to do this season. >> What do you think makes important? >> Um I know he knows your stuff. >> Yeah. Yeah. Listen um we drafted him in New Orleans. U he he's always been a disruptive player. Um, you know, you can put on a lot of tape and see him in the back field creating a lot of disruption. Uh, I don't know, you know, everybody talks about the, uh, production. Uh, there's a lot of hidden production at that in that he creates a lot of opportunities for other people. Um, he understands, uh, the mentality and the mindset of how, you know, we want to play defense. Um, and I think he's I think he's a good fit. I mean, obviously the biggest thing for for Marcus and and it's been that way throughout his career is his ability to uh be healthy and and and maintain his health, but when he's out there, he's a he's a disruptive force. >> But you haven't gotten a chance to really see Jaylen Johnson at his healthiest or at his best coming into this training camp. What are you hoping to see from him tomorrow against competition the likes of Jamar and T? >> Again, look, same thing that we've talked about with really all these guys. I mean, this is a hell of a challenge for all of our defensive backs to have to go up against, you know, this set of receivers and these skilled players. Um, and so, um, look, I want to see him go out there and and compete and, you know, can we play man coverage against these guys? You know, can we run with these guys? I mean, I'm I'm talking about everybody. I'm not just talking about Jaylen specifically. Um, I've I've seen improvement out of Jaylen. I I've seen some some flashes that say, man, he's he's he's looking, you know, a little bit more like what you expected him to look, you know, um and yet there's still a lot of growth. You know, the system that we're in is a lot different than what, you know, he was in before. And so I think uh we're still we're still growing. We're still learning. Uh but I've seen him uh I' I've seen him take to what we're trying to get done. Uh, and I've seen him improve. >> Dennis, uh, you have so many moving pieces, uh, in the secondary. Does that impair your ability to get a true evaluation of whether the pass rush has improved? >> Um, no. Um, it really doesn't. I think the pass rush has been better. Um, and and it still needs to improve. Um, we'll have great opportunity this week against uh, Cincinnati. um both in the joint practices and or the joint practice and and in the game. Uh but uh I I I think the I think the pass rushes uh has improved uh and I think it'll continue to improve. >> Paten this week of some joint practices that maybe get a little out of control and some fighting and all of that. As a coaching staff, what do you tell your guys in terms of one physical there's probably a line you don't want to cross? >> Yeah. Well, I mean, it's not a lot different than what we do here. I mean, you know, we've had a lot of physical practices. Um uh and yet it's maintained u relative order for the most part, you know, and and and that's the same thing that we want to do when we go up to uh or down to Cincinnati. I mean, we want to we want to go and we want to compete and have good productive physical practices and yet um nobody gets better when we're wallowing around fighting, you know. So, let's just let's compete. Let's practice uh and let's let's play physical between the whistles and then, you know, when the play's over, let's move on to the next one. Uh so we can be productive. And I think, you know, um, Ben and Zach, you know, are on the same page in terms of what's what's expected and and, uh, uh, that's been clearly, uh, communicated to the players. >> You talked some last year about how Harris's ability to coach with an understanding of what his guys see through the helmet. From your experience, why does his methodology sort of land with these guys the way it seemingly does? Well, I I mean, I just think this like um you know, you you you see a guy that's uh played the game and played the game at a high level, was very successful in doing it. Um, and so there's it's it's it's it's not a whole lot different than the veteran player. When the young player comes in and there's a veteran player that's in the room that's been very productive and done it the right way, you know, that can be very beneficial to a young player. And it's the same way, you know, with a coach, you know, um, when he says something in terms of what he sees, um, you know, he's been there. he's done that and I think u uh I think that's beneficial and and I think for him as a coach uh being able to see the game not only through the coach's lens and perspective but also through the lens of the player I think that's valuable for us as a staff because some things that may make sense to us as coaches at times when as he would say when you look through the helmet uh maybe it doesn't maybe it doesn't register as well. And I think sometimes, you know, communication uh with a guy that's played, you can take something that's maybe seems complex and you can break it down to its simplest form and make it make sense to the player. >> Yeah. All right. Thanks guys.

title: Rome Odunze, Montez Sweat discuss Bears' speed on both sides of ball | Press Conference
text: Rome, one of the things that Press and Ben mentioned was going to be more in the offense is giving you more of those contested catch opportunities. How did that come about and what do you what do you make of that? >> I love it. You know, I think that's definitely something especially like on the outside, you know, those opportunities um just to stretch the defense. I feel like, you know, when it's one-on-one opportunity out there and um you know, we got safety leverage or something like that, then you know, one-on-one kind of 50-50 ball um is one of my expertise. So, something I'm excited about, something we've definitely worked on in camp. [snorts] It's been a few fluid few weeks for the offense and trying to figure out what each receiver does best. How do you feel that process is sharpening here as we get about the midway point? >> I think it's doing you know it's it's coming along for sure. I mean obviously um you know everybody has their role to play in this offense and um you know it takes reps and and and practices to get that and get that honed in and tuned in on what that's going to look like. So, um, I think, uh, Ben and the staff have been doing a great job of, you know, putting ourselves, um, in positions to be successful for each and everybody's specific talents and, um, yeah, I think that's going to carry well into the season. >> What do you look forward to when you get to Cincinnati? >> Man, looking forward to going against somebody else. You know, I've been going against our defense for for a while now, so it'll be exciting to go against a different opponent and, you know, fan of Jamar and T and that receiver core over there as well. So, looking to see their their reps and and our DBs get after them. as you say, can you watch those guys a little bit up close or or in practice film later? How do you try to steal from some receivers around the league? >> Yeah, absolutely. I mean, there's so many good receivers in the league, you know, today. I feel like, you know, it's very, very talented across the board. So, um, I try and steal a few things here and there. I admire, you know, different talents that different guys, you know, have in their game and obviously with T and Chase, they they got a dynamic, you know, duo, but there's some other, you know, receivers Tinsley over there that, you know, made some plays, um, as well. So, um, yeah, I I'll definitely be trying to peek, you know, a few when they're on the field, trying to see, you know, what they're getting into. >> Man, I feel like T just moves so well for for, you know, his his height, you know, he's fluid in and out of his his routes and then he, you know, he has tremendous catch point, you know, radius, you know, going up contested catch. I feel like Jamar is, you know, just like incredible after the catch as well. some of the catches that he makes over the middle as well as his uh go ball um chemistry with um Joe, you know, something I'm looking to get, you know, and display with Caleb as well. So, um both those guys, you know, have great talents for sure. >> For you, for you, what does how does it compare what you can get out of a joint practice against a team versus saying playing in a game against them? >> I mean, it's different obviously. Um but I mean, it it can be even more beneficial honestly, you know, in a in a joint practice because you can get specific looks, you know, get specific things. um you know rep specific plays that you know you want to get going into it you know very planned out in that way knowing um you know it doesn't necessarily mean anything you know on the scoreboard. So um obviously there there's pride and you know ego on the field out there want to go play our best ball but um I feel like you can get into some of the specifics maybe try a few things out knowing it's not the real thing just yet. >> Rome Joe Tuni plays a totally different position but he's one of your captains. What have you gotten from your experience with him? man, just the consistency. I think, you know, Joe's the same guy every single day. He comes into the building. Um, he leads, you know, with joy. He plays the game with joy. Um, he works hard even in the, you know, I don't know what year he's on, 12, 11. Okay. Yeah. You know, even in his 11th year, plays with a lot of, you know, power. Um, you know, a lot of passion as well. So, um, you know, seeing him come in and work day in and day out, you know, um, being on his stuff. I go watch the one-on-one with the lineman sometimes just to see him and Grady go at it two vets. Um, just to see that competition. So, um, he's been tremendous for us in the locker room since. And obviously, his play is second to none. >> Does he say much as a captain? >> Uh, I mean, he definitely when it when it's his time to, you know, lead and and and say something within the team, he'll definitely say something for sure and encourage the guys, you know, whenever he he breaks us down or said something like that. You know, I'm not necessarily with the own, but every time we go in the huddle for a team period, he's giving everybody dab, encouraging everybody. So, yeah, I definitely think he he he speaks up when he needs to. >> Who do you guys miss most uh in practice when you have Luther out there? What do we miss most? Oh man, shoot. Probably him spinning the ball after the first down or the excitement that he brings to the game, you know, trying to choke people out. Um, all that all that, you know, definitely miss Lou out there. You know, I know his recovery uh is going well, so excited to get him back out there. >> With the with Coloulston, how how rare is his skill set? Like just watching him move and all the different things he does. >> Yeah, rare. Real, you know, rare. you know, a diamond, you know, it's uh it's impressive just to see his his wide, you know, route running ability um you know, is incredible. And then you get him down there blocking, you know, on a six stack or something and he and he's doing, you know, holding his own like he's a tackle. So, um you know, his versatility is is truly incredible. I'm super glad that he's on the crew and um you know, I learned learn a lot from him as well just for from his movement and his fluidity in and out of his routes. >> Can you see how defenses have to adjust for him and then how that could also maybe help 100% 100%. When you have that much of a threat inside, you know, the hashes on certain plays, you know, it creates creates a lot of opportunity outside the numbers, you know, for me and other wide receivers. So, he draws a lot of attention and and that's, you know, goes for the weapons all across our offense, you know, puts a lot of stress on the defense, not knowing where the ball's going to go, knowing we have so many playmakers out there. >> Rome, you had one of the highest yards per catch uh in the league last season. What are you looking to add to your game or refine? What's your next step, [snorts] >> man? wide receiver play in general. I honestly just want to fine-tune every every single one of those things. Obviously want to be better at the catch point this year. Um make a lot more contested catches. Um you know, m make some uh tough catches over the middle. Um as well as route running, I feel like, you know, my route running is is up there, but I have a few, you know, nicks and knacks that I can clear up and um make even better yards as a catch. You know, run after catch is definitely something I'm looking to improve on as well. You know, I'm watching Luther Safe looking at how he's making defenders miss trying to do some of that as well as Swift. So, um, all around I feel like I can improve and just, you know, be one of the best in the league. >> On the other side of the ball, how do you notice Dylan's speed? >> Man, I I I see his speed out there every single day. Every time you get the ball, every time he's out there, look, he's running to the ball and then you come outside and you see his name on the board, 22 miles per hour, 21 miles per hour, 22 miles per hour, day in and day out. So, um, you feel it as well. You know, the game is is slowing down for him as well. um and he made a play early on in camp um where he came down on a inb breaking route and kind of broke up the play and you know something that it takes a little bit of savviness a little bit of knowing what's happening seeing the field to to accomplish. So um I think it's coming you know very very um the game is is slowing down for him a good bit and he he's seeing things a lot quicker but obviously you know um he he's still learning and and still getting after it but he's been impressive so far for sure. about three weeks into camp. How's the foot? >> Man, I don't think about it. Honestly, I really don't really think about it. Um, like I said, you know, earlier, my my team here, the training staff here, as well as my team in the offseason, we put in a lot of work to get those right. So, I had my routine to stay on top of it. Um, other than like being in cleat soreness from being on the field, running around, being explosive. Um, that I think every guy kind of feels there's not much more to it. >> Press said the other day that kind of if you didn't know, you wouldn't know like that that you look back to. >> Yeah. Yeah. No, for sure. I mean, I don't feel it, you know. I I feel like, yeah, I have the same kind of perspective as everybody out there. I don't really, you know, think about it. Um, not something I really um think about. Like I said, I just kind of go out there and play. It feels good. >> That speed board, do guys pay a lot of attention to that? Does that get a lot of conversation in the room at all or >> Oh, for sure. For sure. Yeah, absolutely. Yeah, the guys are talking smack over that for sure. You know, um, and Dylan's, you know, like I said, been at the top of it a few times. You know, KD, uh, has also been at the top of it. He's got a long stride, um, as well. you know, I I've I'm I'm on there. You know what I'm saying? I'm on there. I don't want to, you know, say I'm not on there. No, I I've got up to speed a few times. Jade, you know, some other guys that are um prolifically on there, but yeah. No, it's definitely a topic of conversation in the locker room trying to have a lot of speed across the board. >> Is anyone consistently number one? >> Consistently number one, man. If I had to guess, I would say I'll probably say Kaden Davis. He he been since he came in, he been he been up there. And then I'll probably say Dylan. Those are the two and Jade. Those are like the top three that I'm seeing all the way up there. Blackwell is always up there. I mean, he's, you know, just fast on on any given day. So, yeah. >> Monte, what you think of uh kind of the feistiness of uh some of the drills today? >> Uh football. This happens every year. It's training camp. Um after a while when you uh hitting hitting your uh teammate every every other day, day in and day out, you uh you get those type of reactions. So, are you looking forward to this joint practice and what do you think how beneficial do you think it can be? >> Yeah, um I'm look definitely looking forward to the uh the joint practice. Uh get a different look from a different offense and uh actually hit on some other guys who not our guys is uh probably feel a little bit better. So, >> [snorts] >> uh yeah, I'm I'm definitely looking forward to it. >> What's new for you this season? What are some things you have been working on that you think? >> I mean, not not necessarily new. Uh, I think um I'm revisiting some uh some fundamentals and uh pro possibly uh expanding my game to some uh new techniques and new things like that that uh DA wants to um implement within the defense. >> What kept you out there for 10 days? >> Sir, >> what kept you out of practice for a while? >> Injure. >> What you've seen some of your teammates go down, some of them for short times, some of them will stretch into the season. How do you balance kind of the need for physicality in practice with the fact that it can get a little dangerous out there? >> Um, I think it's a time and a place of everything. Uh, obviously some periods are live, some periods aren't. We like to uh just follow follow the lead of the coaches on that.
