I mean, Ben has a good a good idea how he wants us to practice and uh how he wants us to transfer to the game. So, uh, we just follow the lead of the coaches on that aspect. >> What did that mean for you guys last year when you kind of establish that physicality during the early days of returning camp? I mean, it was a part of it was part of the culture, but I mean, this this is a new year, so I mean, we approach approaching the year different. I mean, we still uh bringing that phys that physicality to to football because that's just what football is. >> You have a feel for how the pass rush uh will be this season, if it can indeed improve? >> Um, I mean, uh, I got a feel. I guess we'll have to see. the the the focus in the spring on get off and and [snorts] the fundamentals. Are you seeing in the summer like the fruits of that like you're seeing that because you guys focus so much and then the spring like what are you what are you seeing so far as telling you that was a promising decision? >> Yeah, I mean the the fun the fundamental side of the football that we've been uh honing in on is definitely uh transferring to the film within practice and and in the uh the past preseason game that uh that the guys played. I mean, you see it uh on the on the makeup of the film and uh you see it in practice. So, yes, it's definitely transferring. >> Do you need Marcus St. >> Uh we we rubbed a couple shoulders uh while in the building. We introduced ourselves uh I met him. >> What do you know about him? You know, him have been in the league kind of roughly. >> Yeah, I mean I know he was uh he played with the Saints uh for a while with uh DA and was uh pretty productive. So, um we're glad to have him part of the group. at the uh Stevenson practice, you spent a ton of time with the fans signing autographs. What like what what was your why did you want to do that to the level that you did? >> That was actually Ben idea. Um we was actually uh all the injured players who was on the injury report. I couldn't uh participate in the walkthrough, so Ben made us sign autographs. I I actually enjoyed it, but yeah, that was Ben. >> Well, you you could have like, you know, you could have done it for a little and gone away, but you like I don't know. See like like you were saying like you enjoyed it. Yeah, that was that was just a pleasure on my coach. >> With Austin Booker, he said he's tried to work on like lower body strength and some other things. Um, what's your assessment of uh how he's progressing compared to last year? >> Yeah, Book is uh turning into a complete uh complete player. Um he's a guy that wants to be out there on first and second down and obviously he shows uh his pass rush to us on on third down. I mean, [snorts] I I believe he's uh coming into a complete player that he can be. >> Seeing uh seeing Darnell get that contract extension and getting to see watch his growth. What how proud are you and what was it like just to see him make this get to this point? >> Yeah. Uh the uh the stride that that that Darnell has made within his uh his technique, his work ethic, and just way he goes around the building is tremendous. from when I got here and and where he where he's at now. I don't think I don't think I beat him in a one-on-one rep, honestly. And it's he's it started off with with me making him better. Now I think it's the other way around him making me better. >> Ben has said repeatedly since the end of last year that last season was your, in his opinion, best season in the NFL. How has he expressed that to you and what's the next level for you? Uh, I mean he I guess in the same way the same way that y'all hear is the same kind of the same way it's told to me. Um, but I'm not get not to get too high on that. I mean it was a it was a cool year. I mean, but uh obviously I want more >> what are the goals >> more >> once you get that that that pay that that you've gotten that Darnell just saying like what's your experience on like I and even though I've got this in my bank account that I'm going to keep this my motivation where it's at like he just talked about it's like money so but but on this other side it's it's a life-changing thing I would assume. >> I don't understand the question. I'm sorry. So, how once you're set financially, how does the motivation to be great still? How do you maintain that? >> Yeah, I mean, it's just a a competitive edge that that you keep uh and I mean just really just wanting to get the respect from your peers day in and day out. Like, uh yeah, I ain't I ain't lost it. I still got it. So, uh, I come out I come I come to work every day with willing to prove that really the the bank account is is cool and, uh, your family set and your set, but uh, you still just want to want to have that respect of [snorts] the peers around you. >> You you make it sound like it's a very interesting relationship between you and Darnell from just going against each other for the last few years. Yeah, he was a sec He was maybe in his second year maybe. No, no, no. He was a rookie because I played him I actually played him earlier that year. The same year I I believe the same year I got traded. Uh I mean it's just really been a dog fight. I mean when um when I first got here I I felt that I seen the athletic tools. I mean a big guy that could just mirror you with the with with his passet and also strong enough to to sit down with with a bull rush or a long arm and things like that. and just um has how he's developed um on the field mentally. So yeah, it's been been [snorts] fun. Do >> you remember when it turned when it became that he was on [clears throat] your level or he was like you said >> I think I think this year is maybe the biggest jump that I've seen personally last year was like uh you know what I'm saying? we kind of just hit for hit, hit for hit and uh this year I just I just see like a a huge jump in his uh technique >> with uh them working Dio back into the rotation. Uh what have you seen from him and how does that affect you? How does this new dynamic affect you? >> I mean I don't know if it affects me in any way rather than just having somebody else on the on the other side willing to um you know what I'm saying give 100 give give 100%. [laughter] >> Joe Tuni don't trash talk, man. His his his favorite uh word, his favorite thing to say is, "You let it.

title: Ben Johnson: 'I feel really good about the path we are on' | Press Conference
text: Big week coming up here. Obviously, we'll take off tomorrow and and head to Cincinnati uh for a joint practice there with those guys. We've been talking about it for a couple weeks now, it seems like, and and how big that'll be just to assess where we're at as a team. Um had a really good staff meeting yesterday with the player day off and and just being able to see where we're at and there's competition throughout this roster right now. Um offense, defense, special teams, it's it's heating up and I wish there was a little bit more clarity at this point, but there's not and so um I think that's going to make for for a really good next 2 weeks as guys try to separate themselves and make it clear that they belong on the 53 or on the practice squad. So uh we talked about that a little bit this morning in the team meeting. But uh with that, I'll go ahead and open it up. >> What's the timetable for Minaya? >> He'll be week to week. >> You guys have any bad injuries pretty good here in the first couple of weeks. Where does that fit in your idea that practices need to be as intense and physical as possible? As a coach, do you have to turn the dial a little bit? >> We we turn the dial every single day. We look at what we're doing, how we're doing it, um and we always adjust and and that we're going to continue to do that. we have a method to to what we're doing. Our guys believe in it, we believe in it and um I feel really good about the path that we're on. >> Do you look at any of these injuries as just kind of bad luck? >> They're things that you can't control sometimes. >> And we saw Ozigbo back on the field on Sunday. What's your understanding of kind of the timetable that he's under to get ready for full speed, full contact, full competition? >> Yeah, he's another one we've talked we've talked a lot about just having a plan in place and um the best thing for him, ramping him up and uh you know, obviously, physically, we feel really good about where he's at or else we would we wouldn't have brought him off PUP. Um now it's a race to see how quickly we can rebuild the confidence and so uh it's going to it's going to look different for him than it is anybody else just in terms of how we continue to integrate him into into drills, team drills, um um things like that, but we felt like this is a good opportunity over the next course of training camp with the padded practices that we're going to have that gives him a chance to start building that confidence back up again. >> Can you provide any more update on Kyler Gordon or have we pretty much gotten a non-update? >> Yeah, there's no there's nothing to add right now. Yeah. >> Do you have any interaction with him or see >> Yeah, I see him in building. Yeah. >> Do you feel like he is progressing? >> Yeah, there's a plan and he's working towards that plan. >> What does he do right now? >> He's rehabbing. >> I don't know. When you guys do these joint practices, the coaching staffs try to plan together. What role having Press and Zac obviously being brothers has that played in you guys getting together with the Bengals or any of the planning going into this? >> Yeah, you know, Zac and I had really good conversations in the springtime. They're they're really organized over there and so it was probably in May that he sent over what he wanted the practice to look like. You know, field diagrams and all that and so it's really detailed. I know they put a lot of time into you know, what we want this to look like. I think we're going to get, you know, call it just under 2 and 1/2 hours of really good work. Um and and so I'm excited about that. Uh Press has certainly helped out just in regards to you know, he knows a lot of those guys on that staff. Um there's a lot of coordination going on between the coordinators. You know, HT's been talking with Daron Simmons and um you know, we've got we've got Press talking to Al Golden and and all that and so um a lot going into it, but I I think we're on the same page with what we want this to look like, what we want to get out of it and I I think both sides are going to come away pretty pleased with with the work we get in. >> Have you determined what you're going to do with your starters after this? >> No. No. I think I said last time it depends on what the joint practice looks like for the team and there's a certain number of reps we're trying to hit and we'll see where we're at after the joint practice. >> As far as the competition, is are you still mostly looking for consistency or anything else that you want to have your eyes on? >> For Are you saying >> just determining who's, you know, left tackle, whoever, just [clears throat] with starting spots. >> Just Are you talking one position or you talking about as a team right now? >> Well, let's just [clears throat] say one position was left tackle. >> Left tackle? Uh yeah, we're we're we're going to make a couple changes there. Um you you'll see it today where where Braxton will be back, he'll take the the rest with the ones. We're going to move Theo over to left side, get him some reps with the twos there. Um so as far as I'm concerned, the the competition remains wide open. And uh we'll continue to play that one out. >> And you view him as part of that competition right now or working on his own? >> He's he's got his own timeline right now. >> What about swing tackle? Theo's got most of the reps at at the right side with twos. Does that mean nobody else is in the swing tackle competition? >> No, we we got to see those other two guys at right tackle now. So, get them a chance. >> As you as you've been dealing with that last year and this year, how has it helped like in what specific ways has it helped you with that instability to have Joe Tooney right next to it? >> At left tackle? >> Uh Joe Tooney at left guard, yeah, next to the rotating left tackle. >> Yeah, I I think Joe would like some clarity on on who he can build a rapport with. It it's been a little bit of a revolving door, so um he's a pros pro and he's willing to to do everything, but you want five guys playing as one, so um you know, we'll we'll go as long as we need to to figure out who those five are, but at the same time, the sooner we can make that decision, the sooner they can gel as a unit as well. Um you saw it last year, it took us through the the bye week before we really started clicking a little bit as an offensive line and and the run game coming alive the way we wanted it to, so um yeah, I I think he's doing a great job right now. Uh the communication is a huge piece of it. With Garrett at center, there's I I don't have a whole lot of concern from the communication piece, and yet um you know, the sooner we can we can be on the same page without even saying anything, the better off we're going to be. >> How much is Joe's input in that at all? Like, try to get insight from him on who he is working best with. >> [snorts] >> No. No. No. We we judge it off the tape. The tape tells us everything we need to know. >> You know, you don't think I'm really good at separation, but maybe that's an area where Roman Wilson could improve. What have been your coaching points with Roman? >> No. I Ro- Roman's looking to play fast, and he's looking to be great at the top of his routes. Um, he's a bigger body, and so, um, part of what he is superpower is is the contested catches as well. So, I I'm not concerned. I think he's making plenty of separation as is right now, and, uh, I'm really pleased with what it looks like between Caleb and him, where where the ball's being placed, and him being able to to torque, and and, uh, go up for the football when needed. So, he brings a different element to the offense than than, uh, maybe what I've been around in the past, and and, uh, I look forward to sinking into that. >> You don't put it all on one guy, but can capable of carrying your pass rush this season, and and making it better? >> I think he's he is capable of affecting the quarterback. I think he did that last year. I thought, uh, I It hasn't been a secret that I thought he played his best season last year, um, run game and passing game. So, I I think he can piggyback on that with another really good year. That that's what we're looking for from him. >> Last two, Pat and John. >> And last year you guys had that >> super physical practice that everybody talked about setting the tone for the season. Have you felt that this training camp, or was it not quite as needed given that, you know, half your team is familiar with you and what you >> Yeah. I I think I think we've had some pretty physical practices, and, uh, I feel really good about where we're at. I thought it it translated to that game. Our physicality showed up week one, um, on all three phases. So, I I'm pretty pleased with that right now. >> And when you have a uh moment like that with Kyle on Sunday, Grady seemed pretty upset with himself afterwards. Do you I know he's upset he's been through it, but do you have a conversation with him afterwards or what's sort of a >> No. He he he's a pro. We're we're all good. Yeah. Thank you.

title: Devin Lloyd: 'It was fun to go against them' | Carolina Panthers
text: being back here as as we are. >> Oh, wow. Coming in with some heat. Um it's you know, it was just nostalgic obviously driving in and you know, seeing the stadium and then coming in the locker rooms and being in the visiting locker room for the first time. Um coming on the field is just nostalgic and then seeing you know, all these familiar faces, all my guys, you know, uh it was really cool. So, um but yeah, being a I don't know. It's uh let's just say it was fun going against them. >> How do you How do you think, you know, obviously wearing the green and gold is important to you. How How do you think you did against your former team teammates like sliding up at the defense and communicating in the joint practice? >> Yeah, comms were good. Um I mean, everybody was on the same page. Uh it was a clean day communication-wise. >> I know you're not big on compliments, but who stood out to you on the opposite side? >> Who stood out? Um I mean, shoot. All them guys honestly, you know, looking good. I'd say just you know, everybody's uh you know, getting each other better. Iron sharpens iron. Um I seen BT make that one-handed catch in the back of the end zone. I don't know if he was in or out, but that was good to see from him, you know, just understanding type of player he is and has been and you know, it's going to be a big year for him. So, yeah. >> And you played against these guys. You played against these guys in the opening game last year. Now you've been on this team. What do you How much better is this team now than it was the team you faced in the opening game last year? >> Oh, there's more talent. Um I mean, I don't know what it was like per se um that team, you know, last year I know they talked about just inconsistencies one game they're not playing up to their standard and one game they're playing great. And um now, you know, being with these guys in this locker room you can definitely see the talent and just us upholding that standard every single day, harping on being consistent and coming out and giving great effort every day. So, um I maybe somewhere along the lines of just um consistency. >> They made it to They made the playoffs last year and I think but from what your experience here, what do you like the most about this guy this team? >> The all around defense. Yeah, just all a group of great guys. I mean, it's so much fun being in the locker room. Those guys are just hilarious. Um and it's, you know, I'm blessed to be a part of the locker room and then obviously we got talent on every level uh on the defense. Um and then I know Coach E, you know, he uh calls it up and dials it up based on the personnel he has and uh wants to put his guys in position to go make plays. >> Dylan, what did you learn about the defense out here today? >> Our defense? Um I mean, shoot, we got a lot to clean up. I don't think we uh we were as good as we wanted to be uh but, you know, guys made plays, we played hard. Um you know, and there's it's never as good, never as bad, got to go watch the film. Um but like I said, communication was good, we were in the right spot. I think everybody understood the task at hand as far as coming out with the right energy. And so, um but that's why we had joint practices. Um unscouted looks, you know, we haven't been studying these guys and so, um it was good to see you know, them uh running plays that we haven't seen and it was good work today. >> Was that helpful like a stress test for you guys basically? >> For sure, yeah. I mean, unscouted looks, you know, we haven't been practicing against that. So, you know, all this is kind of new to us and it's really just going based off of reaction and uh just athletic ability, just just playing ball pretty much. >> Dylan, a couple uh a couple of scrimmages out there today but obviously that's what to expect in a joint practice. What would you make of the intensity today? >> Yeah, the intensity was right. Uh I mean, it's competitive, guys uh care about, you know, just just making plays and and playing hard and and playing for each other and uh stuff like that's going to happen, you know, I mean, being great teammates uh whenever you see your brother down, you know, you go uh protect him, you know what I'm saying? So, I know in Jacksonville they talked about protect team and we we harp on the same things as far as protecting your brother. So, um all that's good and uh at the end of the day we still got our work in so, that's the most important thing. >> Your role in Coach E's defense compared to your role in Coach Camp's defense. >> Yeah, playing the weak side backer in Coach Camp's uh defense, playing the Mike and um uh coach E's defense uh not wearing a green dot to wearing a green dot and then obviously everything that you would ask uh those positions to do. Um I mean coach E is definitely fly. Uh you know, uh learning me as a player and uh trying to put me in the best best position and um you know, he knows my ability and so I'd say from a defense coordinator's perspective for both of them, it's just hey, let's uh get this guy going downhill uh when we get favorable matchups and obviously let's um get uh in coverage so he can make uh plays with his eyes on the quarterback. >> Why does this feel more natural for you? >> Um it's freaking fly. Uh what do you mean? >> Just being in this position in the middle. >> Uh I mean it's what I played in college. It's shoot. It's um it's it's what I've been playing up until I got into the league. Uh whenever I got to the league is when they moved me to weak side linebacker. So I've always kind of been like the man in the middle when play I just um started playing linebacker as the Mike. So I I don't know. I mean I think it's just uh it gives me more of an opportunity just to go sideline to sideline. Um you know, I don't know. Uh it's I like it though. >> You said that defensively y'all have some things to clean up. Seemed like y'all got off to a slower start. Y'all ended the practice with that three and out and that's that seemed good. What about the the the process of the practice? Do you feel like y'all got stronger there? >> Yeah, I mean just um there's a conditioning aspect to it. You know, guys um are in pretty pretty good shape especially coming down here with the heat. Um you know, that allows us to continue to build. Um also just kind of getting a a feel for you know, how the offense is trying to attack us with they're doing um you know, play what scheme wise. Um but then also I think it's just uh a mentality as well. You know, it's okay even if you don't start off slow, how are we going to finish? How are we going to respond? Okay, we gave up some plays. How are we how are we going to respond to adversity and just having um everybody's mindset in the right place. >> Your first person that you saw from the Jaguar side when you arrived here today was who? >> Ooh, first person I mean you know it's crazy I was actually I I had to go to the bathroom before I came out here. Walk out the bathroom and then the defense is getting out of their defensive unit room um their defensive meeting. So I chopped it up with a lot of the guys um obviously you know I walked out walk out the hallway and the first person I see is Foye and then he's like oh no way. So uh just one of those stages it was good to see everybody. >> When you broke up that pass and Travon comes in delivers a little pop guys got some kind of way. Is is that just a natural outburst of what happens in these situations? >> For sure yeah I mean you know for outside of me guys don't know each other see somebody who uh takes down one of their teammates okay you know we got somebody who wants to protect their guy and so uh that's natural I think that's just uh love for love for your your brother and and trying to do right by him. If you see him on the ground hey go protect him and everybody has different ways of of going about it but um in that instance you know if it's a little physical maybe respond with physicality. >> Do outsiders make too big of a deal out of out of that type of stuff like the the pushing and and the recent some of the fights that happened during during practice and training camp? >> I mean I think it's natural I mean you see it all around the league like uh you know they talk about not throwing punches otherwise you're going to get kicked out of practice and what not and that's harped on by the coaches but like the pushing and shoving like that's just a part of football and so I think to answer your question yeah probably is is natural and um I mean happens pretty often. >> I know it'll probably be a pretty jam-packed schedule next two days but since tomorrow will be a little bit of a quieter day is there any place in Jacksonville that you might go to? If I could sneak out this is the place I would go to for food. >> Yeah we got some free time. Um I'm actually going to link up with some of the guys but um I would I we're we're going to order some food and have a chef make it and whatnot, but uh yeah. Yeah, yeah. All right. Thank you guys. Good seeing you. Yep. >> Thank you. Thanks for having >> [music] [music]

title: Bryce Young: 'Super proud of how the guys settled in' | Carolina Panthers
text: My bad. >> That's a That's a sensitive subject on this team. >> No po- podiums are sensitive? >> Lectern because it's not on a raised platform. >> It's the same thing. >> Is it like a What is it? Like a >> thing. You stand on a podium. You stand behind a lectern. >> We don't stand on a podium. Cuz we just It just be on the stage. >> Right, but I'm saying a podium and a lectern. >> Argue with the old man about it. >> Anyway, Bryce, it seemed like a pretty successful day for the offense being tested by guys like Hunter and Brown and and everybody that the Jags have on defense. How much of of a positive challenge can that be if you guys have a good day like you did today? >> Yeah, um have a ton of respect for those guys for that group. Uh yeah, really good group of guys. Um I was proud of how we competed. Um you know, it's great. Um but just like anything, you know, can't get too high, can't get too low. I think we did some good things. I think there's plenty of stuff that, you know, left out there that we want to go and and watch the film on. So, um it's always great when, you know, we're all in the same color. We all get to go out as one team. Um and and go up against someone else. So, we love the opportunity. And then now we'll watch the film and try to grow from it. >> Can I ask you about the slow start? I asked T-Mac about it. He said y'all were being too cute at first. That's his term, not mine. Um what do you think led to that? And then how Talk about how you guys ended up finding your footing at the end of practice? >> Yeah, um you know, I think we Yeah, I think we settled in. Um you know, I I think that that's for us, you know, newer newer group, you know, we have some moving pieces. I think that's something that uh you know, we we want to make sure that we're proactive about. Um you know, every drive, every every play is so meaningful um throughout for the course of a season. Uh we don't want to leave any of those out there. So, um yeah, didn't slow start, but I was super proud of how the guys settled in. Um think that for us it's just a being able to refocus. You know, it's not the end of the world, but we have to have that sense of urgency. Um you know, try to relay that to the guys, you know, guys as well kind of doing that amongst themselves. And uh you know, once we settled in, I think we did some good stuff. So, again, just another part of our game that, you know, we can keep growing and improving it. >> After only having played against yourself in practice, you know, very few snaps last week, did you almost need that reminder of of what it can take to come back? >> Yeah. Yeah, I think that Yeah, I think that's it for sure one of these the benefits of these practices, you know, you kind of get in that rhythm. Uh you know, you're practicing at the same time, same place, same people. You kind of know when to ramp it up, when not. Something like this when you're in a new environment, our schedule's a little different. We're on, you know, their schedule, so I I think that's great for us. It's great, you know, in games again. We're going to play at different times. We're going to play at different venues, uh different looks. Uh we have to be able to go whenever it's time to go. Um and, you know, that's something that I think is a a great opportunity for us to grow from today. >> Bryce, it it seemed like the connection with you and Tedarrell really ramped up at the end of practice. after admittedly a slow start, what how important is it that you have someone like him as a security blanket and as someone you know you can go to when things might be difficult? >> Yeah, it's huge. I mean, it makes my job so much easier having a guy like him out there um that you can trust um you know, one-on-one. You know, a guy that you know you can go to. It's It's huge. Obviously, it speaks to the player he is, the person he is, the work ethic he has. Um so, you know, obviously, he's a huge part of what we do. >> Kind of on that note, that touchdown that he had in the front of the end zone right there with two defenders, you said you put that ball where only he could get it. What did you see on that play to trust him? >> Yeah, same. Uh you know, zero look. You know, we have to get the ball out quick and, you know, when when it's that, you trust your guy. Um he did a great job. Had some pop out of some movement. Uh ended up being a contested catch and for me, just wanted to give him a chance. Um and, you know, it the catch looked a lot easier probably than it was. You know, that's not a not an easy catch at all. Um but again, speaks to, you know, having a guy, you just want to give him a shot. Goes up there and competes and comes down with it a moment like that, you know, it's it's what you expect from this sort of guy. >> Bryce, I know those those plays get a lot of attention, but there was a play where Mitchell Evans was just like streaking open down the field. And sometimes it's easy to kind of overthrow or like match up on that. When you can make a precision throw with that much wide open space, like how much of a of a moment is that for you guys, especially when you're in the red zone? >> Yeah, um yeah, it is actually a different It's kind of a different mindset. You know, you know you have a big play. Obviously, you don't want to miss that, but um the more you keep someone on the move, uh you know, that's that's more yards after catch. So, Mis did a great job of, you know, it's kind of a nuanced route and him, you know, doing a great job giving me angle, me knowing where he's going to be. Great job of of running through the catch, playing with the transitioning. Um so, um also great play design, of course. You have a guy running that open. Uh great play design. So, yeah, all of us takes you to a high level. It takes, you know, it it takes all 11 and the coaching staff. >> Can you quantify these during practices as [snorts] far as we won, we lost, or do you not look at it that >> Yeah, uh you know, I think, especially this part of the year, it's a practice. It's just about growing. Um you know, I don't think, you know, a win or a loss, you know, for us, I think you you look at a practice and think you won, now you think you don't have to correct things. You think you lost, now it's all right, what do we have to, you know, what do we have to change? I don't think that's really the mindset of practice. Uh we love to compete. We always kind of we keep score and we do that. Um you know, we practice against ourselves and we have the slide I'm sure we'll put up uh put things up, but from a mindset standpoint, it's just about finding the stuff that, you know, you want to get better at and isolating that, trying to improve, find the stuff you do well and and try to make it uh consistent. >> I know you're on the other side of the ball, but what kind of teammate or kind of leader have you found Devin Lloyd to be? >> Yeah, uh he's been huge. Uh like you said, other side of the ball, but that doesn't um mean it's not felt through the whole team. Um you know, he's a he's a very vocal guy for us, does a great job around the defense, um and and all of us. We all have a ton of respect for him. The way that he carries himself works. Um in this this short turnaround, um he's become a uh he's become a leader for us. So, uh it's been been huge to have him here. >> All right, thanks, guys. >> Yeah, appreciate you guys. >> [music] [music] >> Mhm.

title: Tetairoa McMillan: 'Bryce put it in a spot only I could get' | Carolina Panthers
text: How y'all doing? >> Fire away. >> Pretty quality uh red zone work um between you and Bryce. Uh it seemed like they threw a lot at you in coverage, but you were able to make some big plays. How important are joint practices to you after having them last year, but also having this experience? >> I mean, uh joint practices are good, especially this year. Obviously, you know, the starters, um, we never know how many plays we're going to do, how many drives we're going to, uh, do in come the game. So, join, you know, we we in the whole time. So, that's always fun. And just going against new competition is always fun. >> Canalis mentioned how offensively y'all got off to a slow start, but in that last period, I think you connected with Bryce with two touchdowns. Can you talk about the slow start and then how you guys started to find your foot, you know, toward the end? >> Yeah, I mean, yeah, I I don't know what was going on. I feel like we just, you know, we started slow and, you know, we got to we got to fix those kind of things. But, um, you know, we all came together and was just like, man, let's step it up. We got to stop trying to be cute and, um, you know, move the ball period and and and all that. We did pretty solid. So, um, you know, we'll go over the film today and see what it's talking about. >> Usually when you when you come off the season like you did, win offensive rookie of the year, like defenders are going to start coming after you a little bit harder. Did you notice that today at all just with tougher coverage or them targeting you a little bit? >> Uh I mean yeah a little bit. You know you always can tell kind of which way uh the defense is flowing too. Um but at that point you just got to play ball. Um so >> you had that catch I think there were two defenders. I don't know who they were in the end zone um for the touchdown. Can you take us through that play? You remember it? >> Um on the front line of the end zone. >> Yeah. In the red zone. Yeah. I know you're talking about uh yeah, I I was backside just uh one-on-one and you know, Bryce saw something that he liked. He checked out of it. So, um you know, I guess he got me open on that one. >> I mean, but you were able to make that play over over two defenders. Was is it your high like what what makes you win that type of play? >> Hey, Bryce just put it in a spot where only I can get it. So, he just made it easy for me. last year, uh, it took you a couple games to get in the end zone, but then you got in the end zone a lot. Um, this this offse training camp, you've been in the end zone quite a bit. Has anything changed or was is it just opportunities are coming and you're making the most? >> Yeah, opportunities. You know, obviously I'm moving around. Um, the coaches are doing a good job as far as just moving me around, getting me different matchups and, uh, just making the game easier for everybody. So, you know, I feel like everybody's getting a lot more touches, a lot more opportunities, and you know, we making the most out of it. >> You said y'all y'all were being cute. Did y'all have a meeting before and say we got to tighten up? >> Nah, no, we ain't had no meeting. It's just like >> we're making a huddle. >> We It was just, you know, we all just had a little nod like, "Come on, let's go." >> Um, Darren Waller's a pretty big zone target for a tight end. I know you haven't got to be on the field with him yet, but how do you imagine that might just open things up for the rest of you? >> I mean, yeah, it's going to be lovely. I mean, already our tight end room is uh is pretty deep and um just adding him just makes us that much more better. And just seeing what he did versus us last year um you know, and the amount of reps that he got versus us, he was able to score versus us and has some big plays on us. So, um you know, hopefully he can bring that to our team. Yeah, >> thanks team. Thank you. Appreciate Nat.

And guys settled in, our guys are in great shape. We've had a heck of a camp. Um he plays with his hair on fire sideline to sideline. That's what the games are going to feel like. And I saw our guys maintain their fitness level. Got to give a lot of love to Josh Hinks, to Denny Kellington for having our guys ready. Uh Jeff Brown helping me just kind of orchestrate the last couple of weeks with the demands we've asked of our guys. A loaded week before we played the Bills, come back and practice two days later in full pads, another half day travel day, and then here we are practicing again. And so that whole thing flowing so that the guys can feel confident that they could just go full speed and uh and they can handle that. >> Sto can be pretty black or white win or lost. Um, can you win or lose a joint practice? >> Um, you can certainly look at, you know, who had the most success if we scored it like we do our practices. Um, we can look at it that way. I didn't keep track of that necessarily. Um, I heard some good oo and a's happening on the other field. So, I know the Jags were making some things happen. Um, even some of the defensive guys said, "Hey, they they got us pretty early and then they kind of settled down. We had a successful two-minute drive at the end." But, uh, there's a way to quantify it, you know, um, in terms of the physicality and all that. Can't wait to watch it and kind of take my assessment of what happened. >> Had a couple had a couple of really big catches today. What has it been like just or how fun is it just to kind of watch him grow in that area? >> He's been grow like you said daily growth and whether it's in the run game or the pass game, he's showing himself to be a really reliable target. He's huge. He's fast. It's why he's so dynamic on special teams. For the guys who contribute on teams and don't play as much on offense, it takes time. It takes sometimes years to accumulate the amount of reps it takes to be really technical in your position. And that's what I'm seeing from Felipe. Was so proud of him today. Got knocked on the ground. >> Okay. Kind of a little bit of a late hit, popped up in front of the Jag sideline. Guys were walking toward him and he backed away, came back to the huddle. It was just like I was just it was a proud moment for me. >> [laughter] >> Obviously, the tight end room is a little bit different than it was a couple weeks ago with Darren Waller coming in, but Felipe, as you mentioned, with his special teams experience, does that sort of kind of inoculate him from uh the uncertainty in that room right now? >> It could be. I mean, he's certainly one of the top special teams players in the league in my opinion, just in terms of his physicality, how he gets off of blocks, how he blocks on the return in the return game. So, and in that phase, I think he's an elite player. um as a tight end, he's continuing to grow and develop. This is a really competitive room. When you start to get an overloaded room, but someone is a critical special teams player, then the competition kind of spreads out to other positions. So, it's the determination of can we carry an extra back when we need this extra tight end? Can we carry an extra inside linebacker or safety when we have this guy that we're counting on if there's a receiver that brings special? So, Dan and I have to really look at that picture and that's where it gets really hard, really tricky for us. But um all these guys are trying, all these guys are putting great effort out here. We got another game coming up to evaluate how they can help us. >> Dave, in a general in a general sense, where have you seen the biggest progress defensively during this camp? >> Um really just the consistency of communication is what I've seen. And where we started off last year, we added some new pieces. We added a few more this year, but these are veteran guys that kind of, you know, Jaylen Phillips, Devin Lloyd come right into the mix and immediately have that kind of interaction and communication with their groups, with the front, with the with the backers. Certainly in the secondary, there's a lot of carryover there, but I've seen those groups really start to gel and um galvanize. And that's what I'm I'm hopeful for is that we can just get that elite level of communication. the Gerald came off and said there were still a couple of things that we misaligned to. We can clean those things up, but in general, speaking of the camp, that's what I've seen from this group. It's a group that's coming together uh really quickly. >> Can I ask about injuries real quick? Any injury updates? I know. >> Yeah, a couple. Yeah, a couple. So, we just had um Xavier, he got rolled up on a little bit, had some soreness. They evaluated him. They were able to look at it. He was fine as a precaution. We held him out for the chance to get him back on Friday to play um in that first group. So, we held him back out. Um, anything else, Bruce? >> Uh, David Moore left for a minute, but I think he went back to the drills. >> Yes, he that was a private matter. Um, uh, then J Jaylen Phillips, um, came off at the end. They checked him out, checked his wrist, uh, his elbow. They're going to just check that out a little bit, but he was able, he said he was fine. He said he would finish. We held him out as a precaution. So, we'll evaluate that when we get back. >> Thank you, coach. >> Cam Jackson. Cam Jackson had a concussion in practice on Monday and he's in the protocol right now until we clear him further. >> All right. Thank you. What up y'all? What up? What up? I would say anything you do and and you do over and over and over, you going to have um you going to improve in in some fort some form and fashion. So, uh the clock and everything within myself, I would say improve every day. >> Um sure I obviously not you don't get you're not supposed to get hit out there in practice. Um that play yesterday we kind of got bumped. It look I looked like it was accidental but is that disconcerting as a quarterback when all of a sudden there's one of the defense guys either touching you or so close to you >> Nah. That was just a friendly reminder of I just got to step up. You know, that's how it was. Um which which I've been focused on this whole time but it it's like even when even when certain situations happen that's just me having to to to to have more of a plan. You know, if if if plan A doesn't work, you know, having a better plan on where to dish the ball and get rid of the ball, you know, so that that's really all that was. But that was like my first reminder of it so I'm like, okay. I think pretty much overall I've been focused on, you know, staying um in the pocket and stepping up and when I retreat the only time I retreat is if you know, it's got to be free blitz or whatever and I know I've been making those type of throws my whole career. So, some things is a part of my game. Some things, you know, I'll improve in but yeah, that was just a little friendly reminder. >> Two more. Two more yeah. >> Coach Montgomery said that after this game Saturday is when he might make the the quarterback decision. So, here you are starting this game. How important in in that scheme is that for you as a quarterback? >> Uh I'll say every day of my life is important. Every day is important. I won't say it's a day that's not important. So, that's just another day going out there doing what I got to do, honestly. Um I don't really feel anxiety or any pressure, you know, even going into things like that anymore because it's like that's how I approach everything. you know, it's just another day of of of of going to work, you know. That's how that's all it is for me. >> Coaches have been talking about this kind of philosophy that he's had in camp. Like Kyle has been saying maybe you guys practice a little harder than some other teams. Jared Veldheer said that he's doing more work here than he did with the Rams in the past. That is and maybe you pick up a few more bruises here and down the road it'll help you guys. How do you think that that that philosophy can help you guys down the road? >> Uh I think coach came in here understanding that we have ways to go overall when it comes to like you know, our wins and losses over the past few years and everything. So, it's kind of like building that mentality of toughness. So, it's like some places may not have that may have that luxury to not have to do that. But, you know, it's more about a deserved thing. I don't think, you know, we we deserve to take as many days off like that because we have a lot of young players on offense and young players on the team that we got to be able to um expedite the process on catching up with the game speed and and and really understanding the game. So, um it's a thing that, you know, sometimes you may feel a way about it, but it it is in the grand scheme of things it's moving towards the direction of where we're trying to get as a franchise and as a team. So, as long as everything's aligned with that, then that's how you know you know what what what's good and what's what's not good. And that's very good for us because we have we we need to be able to to go out there and execute regardless of um age and regardless of experience. >> Appreciate it. >> Thanks. Thank you. >> Deshaun, can you talk about your travels a little bit going up against the Bills, the number one pass defense from last season, and what you think you might be able to get out of this tomorrow? >> Um yeah, it'll be a good challenge for the team, the offense especially. Uh really both sides, but just going against one of the, you know, top teams in the AFC. Uh they've been proving it over the last couple of years. They keep reloading, so uh a good one-on-one battle. Um get to show a a lot of different things. Um get to see a lot of different uh looks from their defense, and you know, see and and see where we test it, and um where we can be at this year. >> Deshaun, what was the one thing that um after like going over the tapes of the 50 most improved, you were like, I know I can I can be better. You want to be better going into the second preseason game. >> Um I mean, just everything. Just operational. Uh just continue to just be as sharp as possible. Um, connect on the throws that I need to connect on and just make sure that we all on the same page, uh, going to each and every play. >> I'm [snorts] sure. >> Coach, just for a quarterback, you there's obviously a feel you have to have for the clock, the play clock, the game clock, getting rid of, you know, the clock, you know, kind of in your mind in terms of get rid of the when you need to get rid of the ball. How How do you slow that down so that, you know, it's not going to moving to all moving too fast for you? >> Uh, for me, uh, I'm not sure. I just go with my instincts, honestly. So, I just kind of play ball and whenever that time clock goes off in my head or, you know, in that situation, that's when I kind of, you know, usually react off of it. >> For you for you this week, is is the Thursday practice more, uh, >> [clears throat] >> productive for for your game than playing in the third quarter of the game? >> Uh, no, I mean, every situation, uh, every rep I get, every opportunity I get to just go out there and play football is is just as important as, you know, playing just one quarter or playing, you know, a lot in practice. So, I think the more reps I get, the more opportunities that I get to see is is more beneficial for myself and and just improving my game and just catching up from what I missed the last few years. >> Obviously, it'd been a long time since you played in a game setting. How did the body feel coming out of there? >> Uh, felt good. Um, you know, of course, you know, getting hit a little bit. Uh, the next day was a little bit sore, but that's typical football and nothing I was surprised about. So, I think just being able to just continue to just stay on top of that and just making sure that, you know, um, I'm ready to for each and every, you know, opportunity that I get is is super good. >> Given that time away, did you feel like you're still getting more comfortable each time in the pocket, right? You haven't actually played in so long. Like, do you feel like you think room to grow as far as your comfortability inside the pocket? >> Of course. I mean, there's always room to grow. Even you know, week one to week 17, there's always room to grow of that being comfortable and and trusting everything and trusting what we want to be as an offense and especially as a quarterback. So, um yeah, I mean, every I got to mention before, every opportunity, every rep that we get standing back there in the pocket is definitely opportunity for us to just get more comfortable. >> Do you expect the coach to make a decision Monday perhaps or Sunday on who's starting this season opener? >> I'm not expecting anything, honestly. So, like I said, I'm taking one day at a time and whatever comes, that's how we're going, you know, go go about the situation. >> Do you feel like you have to uh maybe kind of lock down this competition in this joint practice on Thursday? It seems like you passed the first big hurdle uh against the Bears and now this is the next one sort of before he makes his decision. Do you feel like you've got to like really nail it on Thursday? >> Um no, I mean, every opportunity for me, I just want to go out there and prove that I'm capable of being the starter. Um but as far as just nailing it and trying to You know, my main focus is just trying to improve. You know, I'm not really focused on just the competition. You know, I think the front office and coach Monken is going to make that decision based on how they're going to make that decision, you know, so you know, I can't really control that as far as what they want to go with, but I can't control uh my opportunities and my reps that I get and being successful with that. >> You mentioned last time we talked to you here that, you know, 30 now might be a little bit different from the way it was in Houston. How, if at all, do your instincts have to change um along with everything else that's changed about you? >> Yeah, I mean, I think y'all took the the wrong words out of that saying that I I think somebody asked Monken that, you know, that I I'm I'm not capable of playing like 2020. I never said that. I just said that I'm not going to be running guys over like I used to be when I was 24 years old. So, I think I got to preserve the body as much as possible so I can be able to stay on the field and I think that's one of the things talking about with the front office and and coaching staff is don't take the unnecessary hits when I don't need to. So, uh but as far as that, my instincts and the way I play, I don't when I'm on the field, I just play ball and and react. >> Yesterday, you aired out a ball to Boston against the >> Bears on the field, you remember? >> Yeah, I do. Yes, sir. >> Would you like to exercise that part of your game in the game? >> I mean, of course. Yeah, I mean, that's that's something that I've always been >> [music] >> pretty good I pretty good at. Um especially in the past, but you know, those little sudden opportunities are going to come up. So, you know, whatever coach is calling, I try to execute as much as possible, keep the chains moving especially early on. It's hard to really, you know, just start taking shots and you know, and and the defense is sitting back on that. Um especially with Chicago, they were playing a lot of two-high shells. So, you know, a lot of underneath things were were were right there. But, um that's something I definitely, you [music] know, want to keep continuing to work on and when those opportunities come. >> Did the pass along reassure you that your arm is 100%? >> Yeah, I mean, I've been through that. I think it's I think it's you guys in the media that don't, you know, that toss about that. Uh I think everyone in this building know that I'm pretty healthy and strong. >> Deshaun, just to go back to the actual preseason game on Saturday, I mean, playing the third quarter, you're obviously going against backups and and stuff like that. But, for you, is the value and the opportunity about getting those live game reps just because it it had been so long without them? >> Yeah, yeah, I think every opportunity regardless if it's first quarter, first half, third quarter, um is really just being able to just go out there, execute, get those live reps, guys flying, bullets flying, you know, both teams on the sideline, you know, in practice it's a little bit different, it's more controlled, but this is not. So, you know, anytime we out there on the field, you know, in a live game action, it's definitely good for anybody that's out there, so especially myself playing quarterback. Getting that feeling, the timing, and the rhythm back is definitely a a good opportunity. >> And do you feel like it will be really good quality work even though you will be with backup backups, you know, third, fourth teamers, and you're going to be going against fourth teamers and third teamers, you still think it's going to be like super valuable for you? >> Of course. I mean, you have to bring those guys up that don't either are new rookies, um and the younger guys that don't have a lot of experience, try to bring them up to speed and [music] and if you can execute at that level, then um I think you're doing a pretty good job of leading and taking charge. >> What was uh my Todd Monken's message to you guys when you stopped practice early yesterday and, you know, you're watching you've been around a while, did it feel like the defense had crossed the lines with some of the physicality? >> Um I don't think like crossing the line um is the right word to say. I think just being able to I think he wanted to do it just to protect us cuz, you know, we're already kind of uh going through a couple um you know, internal things, but at the same time we got to protect each other. You know, we're going Browns versus Browns, so, you know, they don't they don't count that on the on the wins and losses, so we got to make sure that we're, you know, healthy going into tomorrow um practice against a very good Buffalo team and then into the games, you know, it's a marathon, so, you know, you want to be physical, you want to set the tone, but at the same time you got to be able to protect each other as much as possible. >> If uh if uh Todd next week does name you the starter, how would you put in words what an accomplishment that is for you after what you've been through the last 2 years? >> Uh for words, um just really proud of myself. That's all I can say, really. Just proud of myself, you know. >> What do you make of um Todd's been working you guys a lot. You had six practices in a row at one point. He's He seems to be more willing to play starters in the preseason than maybe some of the newer school coaches. What's your philosophy on maybe his old school philosophy? >> Um it's definitely new for me. Um I think it's new for a lot of the veteran guys, but you know, we we we want to embrace it. We want to embrace what he believes in. Um he's the head coach. He has a uh a rhythm and a method behind it. And um you know, we just got to put in the work. And you know, I think everyone in this locker room obviously, you know, we might be banged up or hurting a little bit, but at the same time, you know, the work is not is not going to be um just given to us. We got to go earn it. And um I think, you know, over the last couple years, you know, we got to make sure that we earn that. We got to earn that respect. We got to earn that grind. We got to earn each win. And uh for us to do that and get prepared for that and put in those miles, you know, we got to do it on the practice field first. So, it's definitely different, but I think everyone in this locker room and in this organization embracing it. >> To expand on that concept uh that Jeff asked you about, what are you most proud of of yourself over how you handled the last how many every year since you >> Um I think the biggest thing that I'm proud of is just my mental. I think just being able to block out the noise. You know, just being able to just keep smiling through everything uh and being able to control my own narrative regardless. So, I think that's the biggest thing is just my mentality, keeping it keeping it at peace, keeping it fresh so I can be able to, you know, be in front of you guys and talk to you today and still be in a quarterback battle. So, uh I think that's a blessing for myself and I think that's what I'm proud >> And what about the reaction and have you thought about any type of reaction that you might get at the stadium on Saturday? Are you prepared for whatever might come? >> I don't I don't care. I don't care. >> Deshaun, you've talked a lot about the the similarities with what Tom Savage with what Bill O'Brien with you in Houston. Can you expand a little bit more on what specifically is it about those two systems that really you think accentuates what you do best as a >> Uh I think it's really quarterback control. I think he get he puts a lot on the quarterback plate. So, I think he gives the opportunity for us to be able to showcase our talent, showcase the knowledge of the game that we have, and just being able to really take lead on the field. Um and I think being able to have you know Bill O'Brien's and Munch's system, they they teach they teach you everything that they want you to know, and then once you get in the game it's like, "Okay, here you're the coach on the field. You know, we're going to give you a couple plays, and now you pick the right play that how you feel, and make it right." And um I think that's the the beauty of not being kind of set in stone of this is what we got to run, and if it's not the perfect look, then you're kind of stuck in that situation, and give us options to be able to get to the right play, and make sure that you know we pick out the weakness in the defense. >> Have you ever had a coach in practice really like that? Like that type of occurrence, or is this the first time you've been a part of something like that? >> Um I I'm pretty sure that I've had that happen before, especially in Houston. Uh with Billy O'Brien and and the type of with Vrabel as a DC, uh I think the coaches had it in it on their own. So, not even the players. I think it was a coach situation in that in that situation with Bill O'Brien and coach Vrabel. So, uh it's not the first. >> Good. >> Thank you. >> Thank you. Appreciate it.

title: 2026 Cleveland Browns Press Conference
text: Who have you seen the the most development out of that first offensive line group? >> Well, probably what you see the most out of it is the rookies. You know, I I I think we've seen a lot of development and taking steps forward from Austin Barber and Spencer. The guys that you would expect that uh to occur. You know, obviously between Elton, Zion, and Titus, uh you expect them to play well, uh which they have. So, it's just been hard cuz we all been and most teams go through this, haven't had them all in there at one time. But, that's part of camp. >> So, why did Barber move inside this week? >> We just want to see him inside along with seeing maybe KT at tackle. Uh yesterday, we want to take a look at that. Um it kind of came out of you know, when Tevin was a lot having a few issues with his back, we thought, "Well, why don't we, before we get too far down the road, look at Austin at guard?" Cuz you you're really trying to piece it together. Austin at guard, K-K-T at tackle, could Elton play guard? Could Whip play center? Parker got dinged up. We were thinking maybe he could be at center. We're just trying to move those pieces around to see what the best the best uh combination is. >> Coach, how has Tevin Green been doing in his limited amount of reps, I know, but do you feel like he will get some time in any of these preseason >> He'll get in the preseason three. He's doing fine. Really smart, uh doing a really good job. But, uh but, uh we just don't have enough reps for him. >> What have you seen in the the competition for the depth in in your secondary in particular? >> Well, we've been banged up there. Uh losing Terrance, you know, D. Ross has been out. Um and I know I'm missing some guys that have been out. Uh Miles has been out, Bryant. So, we've been banged up there. So, it's been fun watching Michael Coach play. I mean, that's guy who just shows up every day and makes plays. Um so, that that's probably the one that stood out with the other guys beat up at corner. >> How concerned are you with the depth behind the starters at corner given all those injuries you mentioned? >> Well, I'm not yet. We're not playing a game yet. As we get closer, certainly you know, trying to find a third corner is on our radar. And so, and within the guys we have here. >> Kind of going back to Austin, you talked about seeing We've talked a lot about Spencer moving from right to left, but Austin played primarily left at Florida moving moved to to right. Just How has he kind of handled that transition? >> I thought he did really well yesterday. I mean, you wouldn't have you wouldn't have thought that he hadn't played guard before or even on the right side. So, I was really impressed yesterday with the way he handled it. And I thought KT looked better at right tackle he did at guard. Sometimes things just happen a little too fast inside at least now for them. I would never say never. But uh uh actually looked a little bit better flipping those guys. >> Coach, you mentioned it yesterday this idea of callousing take a few more bruises now it'll help you later. In in what areas down the road do you think that can that can help you guys? >> Well, it's been proven the more reps that you get whether it's in preseason games or in practice against other teams that uh you get some nagging injuries, but you callous yourself for some of the major injuries down the road. Now, again, knock on wood we won't have it this week either, but um I'm just fired up about the way our guys practiced. They they don't blink. Came out yesterday. I know I meet with you guys beforehand, but that was a pretty damn festive practice. I mean, the guys were fired up. Got a lot of good work yesterday. And uh which is impressive for some of those guys really didn't play a lot on on Saturday and then having Sunday off, usually you don't have that kind of juice, but that that's just how our guys are wired. >> Todd, Alex today was talking about some of the stuff he's learned from working with Jared. I guess looking at him, Alex, from the spring till now, how has he grown and, you know, how do you think he can up his production maybe? >> Well, it's hard to really say. I I haven't been here with Alex in the past and in the spring we don't have pads on. From afar, I've always had a lot of respect for Alex, how physical he plays and I think he's really developed, not only being around Myles, but then Jared. I think he's developed a real niche for pass rush, being a kind of a crafty, powerful pass rusher and I look forward to seeing him. I mean, the more he plays and the more opportunities he gets, I think you're going to you're going to see it. >> Alex and Denzel talked about life without Myles for the first time. You game planned against him. How do you think offenses are going to approach the Browns defense differently than they did when, you know, Myles was out? >> Well, we still have Jared. I mean, that's that was the greatest thing about the trade is you get a Pro Bowl player in return. So, and going against either one of those guys is very, very difficult cuz they can wreck the game. You know, Myles was a guy that could wreck the game, so you have to know where he's at at all times and Jared's one of those guys. We had to do the same thing at the last place I was at. So, you know, that it's it really you'd have to ask the other teams of how they would approach that. Uh they're both special players. >> Full pads today, longest practice, what are you hoping >> Full pads today. Um Yesterday was really just shells. Uh we when we put the pads on, we will get nine on seven. I mean, certainly we've got to irrespective of what we face defensively, we've got to be able to run the ball better. It starts there. You can't control the game. I think from a a protection standpoint, when you got the full pads on, you have a chance to really see where you're at hard and shorts and spiders. So, that's what it is. To me, it's really when you put the pads on, it's about the guys up front. Um we'll see. He's got a few nagging things. I mean, lower body. I I don't know if he'll be out there today, but he's fine. Well, he's still a work in progress. I mean, he's a rookie. We're asking him to do things in the backfield as a fullback, which he didn't do. I think he's willing. I think he's physical. He's learning to get his pad level down and strike. And then have movement, moving targets. And he he's a developmental player in a lot of areas. And I've been really impressed with his work. Um he's certainly been durable. He's been out there every day, which is important. We haven't had that with every tight end in the group. So, um I'm excited to see his progression over the next few weeks. I feel good about the guys we got. I think we're always looking uh for another edge rusher, corner, uh potentially a blocking tight end. You're looking for guys uh that you can fill in spots. And that just happens to be one of them. Well, it helps if you can run the football. Um that that's probably the most important thing if you can stay ahead of the chains. Obviously, I'm not even talking about the operational piece. But if you can run the ball cuz where a lot of that communication comes in is when you have to throw it with all your pass protection rules, communicating with the quarterback and the back. So, your ability to to run the football, stay ahead of the chains, and the ball can come out certainly helps with that. Uh you're definitely up against it if you're throwing it, get back on track, third downs, two-minute, you better be on point. >> Todd, you guys uh signed a wide receiver this this morning. Was that is that sort of because of Said uh being out kind of to give you another >> A little bit that that way. Said being down, you know, Cole had dealt with a little bit of a hamstring, he's fine. So, just to make sure we have enough legs in practice. >> Is it safe to say we're not going to see Joe Burrow at >> Uh I don't know that. That's uh I'm hopeful that we get Joe back soon, but I I can't speak to that. >> Good? >> All right, guys.

title: Head Coach Matt LaFleur Press Conference
text: Good. Nice. Heat. Heat. I don't Hey, hey, hey. >> [music] >> Hey. Hey. Hey. Hey. Hey, hey, hey. hey, hey, hey. Hey hey Um, yeah, no issues at all. kind of what he's doing. >> Yeah, he's I mean he's working through um he he overheated at practice. Um so obviously you take that very seriously and he's kind of working through the protocol to come back. >> Is that a conditioning thing or is there something else at play there? >> I wouldn't say it was conditioning. No, it just overheated. I do think hydration plays could play an effect into that. So, um that's something that we take really seriously with our guys and try to educate them and make sure that they're properly hydrated and fueled. >> Have you seen Kamal had adjust to playing the slot? He wasn't there last year, was he at all during any practices? >> Uh yeah, he's done a nice job. I think he's he's put in a ton of time. He's constantly in meeting with Bobby and and um Bulocks. So, I I think he's doing a good job picking it up. He's a competitive player. And, you know, one thing that we saw from him a year ago is I mean, he'll he'll throw his face in the fire a little bit and fit up in the run game and that that's what you need at that position. Matt, as you go through this process, when is it that you start to get a a firm idea of what your roster looks like week one? And does that come in stages where you kind of have your core guys and then you got guys that are fighting to the end? What's that process like for you? Yeah, I think I mean there's there's a good handful of guys that you know are are locks and then that's something that obviously communicate with Goody with on um when we're making those decisions, but there's still, you know, a handful of spots certainly up for grabs. >> Matt, after the way Kyle played in Pittsburgh, what's the next step for him now going into this next preseason game? >> You got to repeat that performance each and every week. and whether you're a rookie or a a vet, it doesn't matter. So, I'm excited for his opportunity against a really good team. I think Denver and they showed it they showed it last year obviously going um to the AFCC championship game. Um they're a physical unit and they got a lot of good players and a lot of good coaches. >> How do you feel the [clears throat] installation of Jonathan's defense has gone? Is that something that will usually be a work in progress once the season starts? And do will you run two spot in this camp? >> Well, I would you know me, I love to do two spot drills, but we just unfortunately with kind of where we are from a health standpoint in certain positions, we've had a lot of guys out, so we haven't been afforded that that flexibility to do that. But as far as JG's defense, I think, you know, you always go in with um a vision for it and sometimes just it evolves naturally organically. So, I think it's it's gone well. I think our players are are picking up the the core principles. Um certainly, there's a lot of things that we have to get corrected. Um but that's that's every phase of the game. Matt, you know, early in your career, you really loved having Mercedes Lewis on your roster. Um, I know you're expecting Zire to play pretty much every defensive staff, but is there a little bit of that to him with the way he interacts with his teammates and the energy he brings and his veteran experience? >> Yeah, I mean, he's a he's a really smart football player. He he can call out things um out on the field which if from whether you're offense or defense, if you know what's coming, that allows you to anticipate a little bit better and that's how you ultimately make plays. So, and I love the edge he brings. He brings a toughness. Uh he's a great communicator and just plays the game the right way. When you have guys like him and Hargrave or a couple years ago when Josh and X came, does it take them a while to kind of figure out their place because they're all kind of natural leaders, but they're also the new guys? How do you see that kind of evol? >> Yeah, I mean I I think it's they do a good job of being themselves. And I think that's one thing that our locker room and what we encourage. I want people to be themselves and fit within the the framework of what we want as a Packer, but um he's all those guys have done a great job coming in and just being themselves and it kind of happens naturally. >> Jordan and Matthew Golden look really connected out there. How have you seen Matthew take that next step? >> Yeah, I I just think it's time on task and those guys have, you know, have gotten more reps together and I think that's the what you want to see and what you expect to see. The longer they're together, the the better the connection. >> What have you seen from Jonathan for during this, you know, second stint now that he's been back? >> I see a guy that's really matured as not only a football player, but as a person and I mean, he is a load inside and he's done a really nice job um playing the nose position and, you know, defeating blocks and he's he's been pretty imp impactful throughout camp. Is it is it fair to say that Colin Oliver doesn't necessarily look like your typical sized edge rusher and yet he seems to have some effectiveness to him that what what if that's a bad premise? Tell me. But like it it looks like he can really get to where you want him to go. What do what do you think of what he's got there? >> Yeah, I think I mean like everybody, they all come in different shapes and sizes. Uh certainly you're always looking for great length on the edge, but I think what he does so well, he obviously he's got natural leverage, but he also has really good quickness and speed off the edge and he he creates a lot of problems in that regard. >> In general, it seems like your defensive line, both tackles and edges have had a pretty active camp. Is that a byproduct of camp practices? Have you been impressed with those guys or they kind of showing some things for the offensive line to work on? Yeah, I think I mean it's twofold, right? There's always for what's good for one side is not good for the other. So, um but I've been I've been impressed. I think DC and and um VO do a great job with the front. Uh just and those guys have to take what they learn from the classroom to individual and then apply it to team and then ultimately to the game. So, I think those guys have done a really good job. They take a lot of pride in what they do and they've been pretty disruptive. >> Two more please. >> Has that given you any sort of confidence? Obviously, you know that Mic is not going to be back for for some time to to know that you have maybe some depth as guys that can fill in during that time that you have more confidence than maybe coming into camp with that. >> Yeah, absolutely. But I think, you know, every year you just kind of come in uh I don't want to ever pigeon hole somebody into a box. I mean, I think you got to come into it pretty open-minded. Every year is a new year and you give these guys a clean slate and then you know you just let the natural progression take take place in regards to how they go out and perform on a daily basis. >> Matt, um Banks obviously was able to do some team yesterday like Rob mentioned. I'm I'm curious, do you have to start figuring out what the best plan is to get him to be able to play every week? It is not too much going there. So, with these live periods too, remember with these running backs is another deal of sometimes you can see certain things, but really you're just looking for how your offensive line I think holds up your thing. >> Exactly. I mean, it it's not the easiest thing to evaluate running game when you're not supposed to be tackling, but you know, when you see a gaping hole there, you know, like like you saw maybe in some of the other uh periods earlier today, then then you can, you know, then you can say, "All right, that was a nice run or whatever." But they all take it to the end zone. >> Jake Ferguson moving closer to the line here as Prescott waiting for the snap. Trying to draw them off sides. They're going silent count here.
