How you feeling when you come to the field? Like you just want to be average or you want to be great? And you know, I think everybody's been taking it like, man, we want to be great. So, I think that's been our mentality. >> Last two, Brandon and Eric Fisher. >> We heard a few winning coaches mention precision quite a bit this off season. Can you describe to us what that looks like for you guys out there? >> Man, precision is one, everybody getting lined up. Everybody getting lined up, everybody communicating, everybody being in the right position they need to be in, going over their technique, being in the right right place at the right time, making sure that their technique is on point, making sure their eyes, feet, and hands are exactly where they need to be. So, when the ball snaps, we know exactly what we're doing. So, we just talk about precision, man. We talk about communication. We talk about getting lined up with urgency and just being where you need to be at. >> Coach made a comment last week coming out of Thursday that he didn't like the energy or brand of football that was played. Was that your message to the group as well? And how do you feel the guys reacted or came back from that this week and especially today? >> Yeah, I talked to the I talked to the defense after the game and I was like, "Man, that wasn't our standard." You know, you don't you never need somebody else to get you motivated for a game. For a lot of you guys, that was your first time taking an NFL field. But, man, they responded the right way. But, that's the type of guys that we have in the locker room to respond the right way, to know like, "I got to look myself in the mirror. My brother's counting on me." And it starts with the leaders on the team, just as us cuz we should have better energy as well. So, it's not just those guys, but all of us as a collective, man. But, I thought we did a really good job of bringing the energy today and so far throughout camp. >> Thank you, guys. >> Appreciate it, guys. >> How you doing? Yeah, I thought it went great. I thought we made a lot of plays. Um, of course all those things you can clean up. Um, but I thought, you know, we moved the ball very well, ran the ball great, threw the ball great. Um, took care of it for the most part. Of course at the end you got to do better there, but um, I think overall we had a a really good day. Yeah, I think they're both great out the backfield. >> Max Crosby is second to hit you, but you see his presence. Is that good to play against a player like that, to have that chance? >> Yeah, he's great. I think Max is one of the best in the league. Uh, I get to see two of them every day, so. >> DJ, what's what's the value of this day particularly for for you guys as a as a unit whole? Going against somebody else and then they can see what you see that offensive line here go to work today. >> Um, his value anytime we touch the field, but it's always good to go against, you know, another opponent. You know, it gets camp gets a little bit, um, it could it can just be like seeing the same guys every day can be hard, you know, running the same plays. Um, but I thought today we tested it against them pretty well. Um, I thought everybody showed up and did their job. I thought he's been great since he got here. Um, I think he's gotten stronger. Um, and think his vision has gotten good or gotten better, but um, I think he's been doing great. >> I guess finally getting to show who he is out there and make plays. Just knowing where, you know, he came from from, you know, the situation with his brother and and just now Jerry Wayne. Yeah, you know, he's having a good camp. And just knowing where he's been able to come from, you know, he was really hurt of course about the tape. But to now be in a different place, what have you seen, you know, from him? >> He's been doing great. I think Jerry Wayne has been a one of our best guys who I've we've always had since I've been here. I'm super proud of him just the work he's put in. And you know, I think he's been able to show up this camp and I'm super happy and proud of him. >> Is there any adjustment you have to make when it's a different center in there or do you kind of trust all those guys the same? >> We all do the same things, but yeah, I mean everybody's different, but we we the protection and the run game is all the same. >> So the guy you're still where you have play center right now, but has been one of the key highlights of camp. What do you know about him and his progress? >> He's doing great. I think he's Coach is doing a good job coaching him up on what is being asked of him. And he's been able to show that dog that's in him. >> So give me a little background. Like I wonder what do you think about Fernando Mendoza and the college career he's had and what he's trying to do now? >> Yeah, I think he's a good player. Um I think he's he'll have a lot of success in the league if he you know, continues to be himself and put God first and you know, of course what it what they put around him matters. And I think he has a great coach, a great play caller, so I think he'll he'll do good. >> There have been some deep plays where they they brought heat, but you guys were able to answer some of it. How do you feel like the way you guys answer pressure and the team say heat or same pressure or things of that nature? How do you feel you guys have been able to progress throughout camp in those scenarios? >> I think we've done a good job at it. This versus I D'ing it correctly and then my part getting the ball out. I thought, you know, our routes were clean today. I was able to anticipate, but I thought, you know, it's gotten better. >> CJ, with some having been in the system for a year and kind of knowing with now, did you have to Was there a lot of mental reps in the off season of just going through the process of running the offense? Did everybody you talked to say you just feel you seem more confident in the offense? >> Yeah, I think it's year two, you know, that happens. I mean, I think uh no matter what system you're in, if you're going to do it year and year over and over, you're going to get better at it, so I feel like I've gotten better. >> What does that look like? Like in the off season, are you just kind of like mentally going through the process of everything to like above and beyond just throwing with your guys? >> Uh more so it's like working on yourself, uh your body and, you know, uh footwork and that stuff and those things and then you come back to OTAs and when you start, you know, getting into the deep of like the um the scheme and whatnot. >> It seems like you have a more tight connection with Jaylen Higgins ever since last year. How tough is it to see him go down and just your thoughts on Jaylen overall this camp? >> He's doing great. I think he's been able to um put some great um some great days, you know, consecutively and um I think, you know, I think he'll be fine, but I wish the best and hope he's all good, but, you know, he's been he's been doing great. >> And you guys look like you worked on the quick game early and then attacked down field more as the sessions went on. Was that something conscious and is that something you guys want to do with this offense? Maybe attack down field instead of the deep throws today and that kind >> That was kind of just like the practice we had. It was early on it was two-play sequence, so we were allowed to like get back on track. Like second and long, so you're not really going to be taking shots like second and long, so just playing the drill the right way and trying to just take care of the ball and get us in a better third down. But yeah, we want to, you know, be aggressive and take take opportunities if if they're there. >> Two more y'all. You're going to have penalties, you're going to, you know, make mistakes, you're going to have turnovers. It's all about, you know, um getting back up there and trying again. Um cuz if you if you play scared in this league and scared to make a mistakes, like you'll just you'll just be dead in the water. So, you have to take risk. Um and even when you do make mistakes, you got to just go to the next play and keep playing. >> Finally, uh that guy with if anyone makes plays down field, he can. Um what have you seen from him and and and how is your relationship with you all kind of going? >> He's getting better. Um I think, you know, he's um somebody who is very raw, you know, um somebody who is very talented, um but needs a lot of just work with just his mental. And I think he's taking that step. I'm proud of him. He's been he's been working his tail off at it. Um but when he knows what he's doing, he's he's really good at it. >> It looked like the biggest last play y'all moved before the snap like how did you feel like the offense handled the communication there? And how did you >> I think we did great. Um you know, we worked on it um and our coaches did a good job preparing us, but um a lot of times it's getting on the same page and um getting our IDs right. Um I think we did did really good at it. >> Thanks, y'all. >> All right. >> Thank you.

title: What's next for Texans? What's the right move? Intel from league sources

There are some guys that aren't available because they're on reserve did not report list like Brandon Iayuk. He'd have to be reinstated. The 49ers have to be willing to trade him. [snorts] And then, you know, looking at some other teams, the New England Patriots with Kahan Booty definitely on the trade market and he's been the good soldier in New England, but he continues to lose ground on their depth chart. Last year, Stefon Diggs. this year. AJ Brown, I think it's interesting to watch and just kind of think what would happen there. Haven't heard anything developing yet. A, you know, what about the Bills and Josh Palmer? That's another one to think about. We just think about trade markets and the potential to acquire a player. A player that I think is interesting and that I think would fit the Texans offense is Ravens wide receiver Rashad Baitman. And I could see them being interested in Baitman. Uh we'll see if anything comes of that. But yeah, Baitman makes some sense to me. Uh a player that is 61, 193 pounds and can run. title: WR Chris Bell meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: How did it feel to finally be back out there? >> Uh it felt great, you know, haven't played football in a little minute. So, you know, my first practice I was a little nervous, but you know, I'm just out there getting my feet wet, you know, and getting back to the you know, swing of things. >> What's the toughest part just feeling confident in the knee again? >> Uh no, I feel very confident. I would say you know, the toughest part is just you know, getting adapted to the you know, NFL you know, these hot practices and you know, just playing you know, an NFL player. >> Talk about wasting no time and hitting the ground running back at practice. Do you feel like you're getting >> Yes, sir. Yes, sir. I do. >> How does it feel physically in terms of running, cutting, all all those things? How does it feel? >> Um I feel pretty good. Like I said, I haven't played football in a little minute. So, you know, just getting back out there, you know, to be able to run and cut and things like that it feel pretty good. Thing that I'm just mostly focused on now is just getting back into football shape. So, >> It just seemed like the toughest part was standing around during all the early stuff. >> Yeah, yeah, yeah, it was, but I'm just happy to be out there, man. You know, I've been standing on the sideline, couldn't get inside the line. So, you know, it just feel good to be back out there with my brothers and getting ready to play football. >> Jonah Jonah said that one of the most impressive things was that even if you weren't practicing, you were ready to go like >> Yeah. >> Tell me about that mindset. >> Um I feel like even when you're not practicing you always got to take mental reps. So, my thing was to even though I'm not on the field, you know, I study my position, study my spot, you know, and just you know, try to practice the play in my head because they used to give me a little mic. So, I used to hear the play call in the huddle and you know, just try to do those things to you know, stay focused and you know, get the mental reps. >> Did you watch what Kahlil Douglas did this weekend thinking hey, there's there's a role here for some of the younger wide receivers to stand in? >> Say it again? >> Did you see what Kahlil obviously watching what Kahlil Douglas did this past weekend getting in there with the ones the one handed catch? Did you see that and think hey, there's a potential role here for you know young guys. It's not just lip service that they can do. >> Yeah, I I definitely feel like you know uh the rookies have been doing a great job. I ain't going to lie, every time I see uh Caleb make a play, I just like, "Man, I'm so happy for you, bro." Just to see him, you know, out there, you know, putting on in NFL, you know, how he did in college, bro. I just be I just be smiling at him, you know, he you could ask me every time he came on the sideline um during the uh Washington game. I was like, "Man, I'm happy for you, man." Uh I'm just excited to see what we do this year. >> Chris, can you talk about the potential of not only you two, but also Kelvin Harmon as a rookie wide receiver trio? >> Uh I feel like we got a good receiver room, a great receiver room. But uh the young guys are coming along right with the vets. So I would say uh we got a good chance to be something special. So uh y'all just wait and see. >> Chris, what did What did Sony and how tell you about their planned timeline for your return into the uh What did they tell you about just being patient uh in this recovery process? >> Yeah, there's really no timeline. Um every time, you know, they come up to me, they just say, uh be honest with how you feel, you know, let me know you know if if there's a little you feel a little off today or you feel good as day, you know, we don't really want to put a a timeline on it. We just want to keep, you know, getting better each and every day and see how it is, you know, from there. >> Is that tough to I mean as a competitor and football player, of course you want to be back on the field, but is it tough to admit those days where it's like, hey, this is I got to take it easy here? >> Uh yeah, but at the same time, no, because um I would say you're going to have days like that, you know, coming off of an injury. It's all about how, you know, it's a mental game at this point like when you coming back from an injury, you're I got to think that my knee is is good now, you know, I just got to learn how to, you know, just push through the little soreness and things like that. So I wouldn't say it's tough. >> Chris, I saw a little highlight where you were playing a game at Kentucky and you helped a teammate break a long run with a key block. I don't know if you remember that. >> Yeah, I know what you're talking about. >> What What What did you What was your approach on that play? >> Uh I would say my mindset was just you know make this play for my teammate you know I'm always a team first player you know I'm I feel like I'm a all around receiver you know I do good in the pass game and in the run game you know I take pride in blocking just like I take pride in catching so that's something that on that play I took pride in. >> Last night that you kind of stepped on the field and you >> Yeah >> Uh-huh >> kind of dominated right? >> So what will it mean for you the next time you set set foot on >> Uh first I want to say man it's just crazy how you know I had a good game in that in that stadium and then spring break was here and I was out here and I was just like man what if I get drafted to the Dolphins and I was it happened so like it's going to be very special I'm not going to lie I love playing on that field you know the environment and just that feeling when you inside that stadium so I can't wait to you know play on that field. >> Would you prefer to play in a preseason game? Say it again. game before starting the regular season? >> Um whatever the coaches plan got planned for me that's what I'm going to do that's all I would say. >> Over the last year and nine months or so of rehab is there something you learned about yourself whether it's professional or personal in that process? Was there something I learned about myself? Uh I would say I learned that I'm very impatient kind of I would say that because like you know as a as a player like me you know just wanting to get back on the field and just wanting to you know show the people you know who I am and what I got after coming back from an injury like this you got to be patient you know what I'm saying like you can't rush it so I learned how to be patient you know at first you know I was like man like I need to be doing this I need to be doing that but now you know it's all you know just a it's a time time thing so you know I'm just taking taking my time. >> How much are you thinking about the Raider game or is that too soon do you think for you to come back? >> Say it again. >> The how much are you thinking about the the game against the Raiders? Is that >> Uh am I How I think how much am I thinking about it? >> Yeah, is that a chance of being able to play or is that out of the question, do you think? >> Uh I would say like I said, you know, I'm just waiting, you know, taking it day by day, not putting a time frame on it and just, you know, trusting my little my God, Lord and savior Jesus Christ, and trusting the coaches and the trainers stuff with the plan they got for me. >> Because I thought I would have noticed but the league takes your reps. You always take reps with Malik on the on the individual stuff. >> Mhm. >> How's your connection with him on the Have you noticed that that he always wants to play with you with your reps? >> I feel like our connection, you know, it's it's coming along. You know, I just got back out there so I can't say like, you know, we got a a connection yet on the field but, you know, it takes time, you know, we just got to get on, you know, the right page and things like that. Off the field, you know, he's always checking on me like when I sit beside him in the meeting room in the team meeting room, you good? Like how you need feeling and things like that. So, I could say he's a pretty good leader and a pretty good quarterback. >> Two more guys. Man, he's a athlete, man. Just the way he throw the ball in different angles and how he throw the ball across his body like that. One pass he just threw to Malik Washington out there, man. He just be doing crazy stuff every day and I'm like, man. But like he he he can run with it too and and throw with it. So, like he's a very special quarterback, you know, I can't wait to play with him this year. >> Is the next step to be cleared for tackling or are you actually already cleared to be tackled? >> Um that's Yeah, that's the next step to be cleared to be cleared. >> Last question. >> Um I just know a lot of DBs are a little smaller than me, you know, they got long arms but I know my size and you know, me being a a big body receiver, a lot of people can't handle that. So, I use my size to my advantage.

title: S Dante Trader Jr. meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: So, Dante, tell me about getting back out there in the action a little bit today. How did it feel? >> Felt good, but you know, me, I'm trying to get all the reps. Hey, pitch count me and like, "Nah, you got to chill. There's a process everything. Trust in everybody." And this this whole time just trying to help all the guys I can. Running with different groups and trying to get me, you know, help them communicate and everything like that. So, it's been good. Definitely seeing them boys working. Everything just trying to stay locked in the whole time. >> How do you balance the frustration of wanting to be out there and and not being out there? >> Yeah, that's what I got coaches for, you know what I'm saying? I'm a I'm a wild guy. They got to calm me down. They got to take my helmet cuz I'm trying to do extra. If they're doing something, I'm going to do something just as hard or trying to meet extra, but it's it's been tough, you know, even though it's been short short coming, but I'm just glad to be back out there to be honest. >> Feel like when you sit on the sideline, you kind of get to see the game a different way. Just what did you pick up during that period? >> It's definitely like there's more nuances that you don't see from like a coach's perspective of why you got to be where you are on certain landmarks and things like that. And just the communication of the situational ball you get to see. When you get to see it from a coach's lens, you kind of understand the coach speak and you're, you know, talking. You know, cuz you're on you're playing, you trying to, you know, negotiate hitting and your assignment and alignment. So, just in seeing the coach's perspective on the game and everything like that is kind of cool. >> Dante, tell me about the patience in the safety room cuz I know that some of you guys are inexperienced, but there's a need to make plays. Is it tempting to get out of the scheme and and try to force plays or how how can you be patient? Tell me about that. >> that's the first thing to get beat, you know what I'm saying? Is trying to do something outside yourself and outside your skill set. You got to know your your defense and know yourself, too. So, you can always press when things aren't coming your way, but again, that's how you give up explosives, give up big bombs. And especially as you see with Malik, if you're not where you're supposed to be and he starts moving, he's extending plays and scoring touchdowns. So, just emphasizing doing your job and just going out there and doing your 1 of 11. >> As far as on-field stuff, is there something Dante that Zane has told you not to do if you don't want to upset coach Hafley? >> Not really. Um he kind of knows everybody's their own individual. He just is like, "Ah, like in our system we don't do this." Like if I ask something that we, you know, there's some things you got to do on the field. He's like, "Hey, that's not in the playbook that you might try." You just got to tow the line and be careful and make sure it actually works. Cuz if you're going to do it, you better make a play or it better be right. So, otherwise you're going to be hearing, you know, coach Hafley behind you screaming at you. So. >> You talked about Will as playing off script. What's your guys' communication like on the back end when you're preparing for a play that Michael calls off script? Like how do you guys communicate what you see from him out there? >> Yeah, you got to know the situations. Um you got certain down and distances that can key, you know, QB runs and QB design plays. And also like especially when you go more man coverage, he has a better chance of getting out of the pocket and scrambling cuz there's less eyes on him. So, you got to be aware of that. So, if you any type of certain schemes where you got eyes on him, everybody got to keep their lane integrity. So, we we talking to our edges, don't just run up field because we got to keep him in the pocket. Um it's it's all everybody's job just to do their job and everybody else, you know, contain the quarterback in every coverage. So.

title: ILB Trey Moore meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: So, tell me about playing multiple positions. And it is it is it difficult to learn two positions or does it kind of make things easier because you can kind of break up the monotony? >> Yeah, I think for me what I used to say is I started off at outside linebacker. Then at Texas I played some some defensive end in 4-5 and some inside linebacker as well. And obviously outside linebacker in 4-3. So, you know, I played in multiple schemes. I played multiple positions through college and I think that's helped me transition into, you know, the NFL and be able to do the same thing. And so yeah, I think I can handle it. >> What are you doing are you doing either position better at at this point? >> I think just naturally I've had more reps more like outside linebacker edge type position. So, like sand backer that I'm playing. So, I'm probably more natural there. But just getting a lot of reps at inside linebacker this past game and this past week has been good for me as well. >> What what have you learned about the NFL game just from practices, joint practices, and the first exhibition game? >> Yeah, I mean it's definitely a a new level of course just like when you go from high school to college or you know, when I transferred from the American conference to the SEC. It's just another transition another jump that you know, you go to and you adapt to and but at the end of the day it's just football and that's what I do. So. >> What's the skill you think and you have a lot of them. But what's the skill you think is going to most translate to the NFL that you have just from being in an NFL training camp playing in that game? >> Yeah, I think it's my mental toughness and resilience. That's what I always go to. I mean I think you know, God has blessed me with many things. But I think that's the most important thing and I think he gives us endurance and challenges that build endurance. So, just being able to do that and be mentally tough in this game is the most important thing for me. >> Coach this morning was really emphasizing the one-on-one, the fundamentals, how the preseason's not really about tricking or out-scheming another team. How much of that is reflected in what you guys do here practice? >> Yeah, I think that's that's what we're doing. It's just iron sharpening iron. We're just trying to get better at obviously the basics and just learning the the defense and you know, you know, get it to a T to where we can just be out there and play natural and you know, obviously when we come to you know, games in the real season stuff we'll be game planning and stuff. But right now we just want to work out the kinks. >> You you had got the most reps on defense in that first exhibition game. What did you learn from those those snaps and opportunities? >> Yeah, I think like I said just getting a lot of reps inside linebackers that was good for me just because you know I haven't done too much of that in my career so I think that was the biggest thing. >> And the biggest thing for success there was what? Principles or >> Yeah, just you know learning how to get my feet in the ground and you know working on some jobs obviously the run reads and fitting the run from inside backer position is a lot different from outside backer and edge position so you know those types of things. >> And when you're playing outside backer and edge, do you think your pass rush is ahead of your sending the edge as a run defender at this point or the other way around? >> Uh I mean I don't really look at it like that. I try to do it all you know whatever the team asks of me I'm going to try to do it to the best of my ability. >> Trey always asks guys this uh making plays and and compiling stats versus staying disciplined and in the scheme is it tempting to know that you know I need to put some tackles on film I need to put some sacks on film that is it tempting to stay within the scheme and maybe the play doesn't come to you as opposed to forcing action and making a stat making a play? >> Yeah, I mean obviously you know as a kid when you grow up all you want to do is score touchdowns and make catches and you know you that kind of leads up to you know get to high school tackles sacks whatever college sacks and stuff but you try not to get focused on numbers once you get to high level it's all about playing clean defense and when the play comes to you. >> What did you think about the physicality that you guys showed against Washington both in the joint practice and in the >> Yeah, I think that was good and that's you know one of the things we really harp on is being physical and that's something that I pride myself on as well so that's what football is it's about being physically and mentally tough so. >> And what are you hoping to show against the Giants both individually and as a unit? >> Yeah, I think the same thing that that I just mentioned I think that's the most important thing as long as I'm physically and mentally tough and I'm getting better and it's the same thing with the team that's that's important you know.

Uh real quick, uh we want to start with Allen here. Malik Willis, what what did you like about what you saw last night? >> Boy, what's there not to like? The ball came out on time, it was very accurate. And I will say this also something else. The great catch by Caleb Douglas. Watch the replay. That dude is really not that open. There is only one spot >> The placement. >> Malik could place it and that's exactly where it was. It was basically going to be Caleb makes a great catch or it's incomplete. Cuz if he under throws that, it could be a pick or a PBU. So that was an underrated great throw because of the acrobatic catch by Caleb Douglas. >> You know what's funny about you uh funny about you saying that, Allen? If he had thrown that like a normal pass in stride for the original angle, interception or pass break down, it's one of those throws you look at, why would you even throw that? It wasn't open. But, putting that ball high and on the outside where only his guy can get it, I keep telling people that's one thing about Malik Willis's pass is even if they're incomplete, he's going to put it in a place where if the guy can make a heck of a play, he's going to give him that opportunity to and that what that that's what that throw was for me. But, go ahead. >> It brought me back to like this was what Ryan did so well in 2020 is he wasn't afraid let's put it up let my receiver make the play. And that's something that didn't really happen the last three years. So, that was and there was right off the bat Omar you got It's not a shot at anybody I'm sorry. >> Almost a decade. >> And then even like right off the bat he was quick and on time the quick out stick to Malik Washington. It was again there was there was nothing that we saw last night that wasn't like okay this is what I want to see this is what I want to see this is what I want to see. It was >> What about you Omar? >> If I had a crown I'd wear it also. >> Thank you. I I'm going to get you one Allen. >> I don't want to crown him. But, I will say this and people will know where it's coming from. Um there are passes that he can make that other people could not.

title: Robert Mays on Vikings Strong Defense, Veteran Players & Kyler Murray | 2026 Training Camp
text: We have joint practices now out at Vikings training camp and I'm joined by the athletics Robert Maize. You do the athletic NFL show. >> Yes. Athletic football show. >> Okay. So, it's it's a fun time. You're joined by a bunch of your crew. Recently, you guys diagnosed or you didn't diagnose, you drafted a bunch of the best defenses in in the league that you guys would want on your side. I think the Vikings were nine. >> They went n uh knife. That's right. >> Okay. That's what I remember. you guys felt like it was a steal at that position that they maybe better than what you see. What what what went into the assessment of it all? >> Well, I think they've been a top five defense for the last couple seasons and so if they are as good as they were over the last two years, you're getting a steal there. But obviously, there are questions. You know, it's just a different collection of players among that group than we've seen over the last few years, not having Harrison Smith on the back end, a lot of youth along the defensive line. And so it's this combination of a proven track record with the defensive play caller, but some new faces and where do we land between those two things. And so I think that was the discussion that we were trying to have. >> When you look at some of the depth on this team, is there a name maybe going into their second, third season that you look forward to see taking a leap? >> Honestly, I think it's more about players that are veterans that have been surprising like what Eric Wilson did for this team last year and just having another layer to your linebacker group. I think those are probably the players that have stuck out the most. And even Jaylen Redmond's another great example where you have these guys who've been in the league for a couple years and then last season I think really opened some people's eyes for one reason or another. And I think that is not an accident. Like I think this defensive system and its ability to highlight what players do really well. They're going to be guys that feel like they're kind of coming out of the woodwork seemingly every single year that maybe you think you knew what they were and then after a season as a more rotational piece within this defense, you're going to look at them a little bit differently. How how do you think that will play out, I guess, in the NFC North conversation with the Vikings kind of being this offense no one's really seen. They say they're going to add some more wide zone to their run game. They have a new quarterback. How do you think that will play out? >> It's a great question. I that this this division >> Yes. I think when we preview the division in the next couple weeks, I might just flip a coin every time I think about who's going to win each game and who's going to win the division because you could make a really confident argument about every single team being the best team in the NFC North for the reason we just said the Vikings coming into it, I think, have clearly have the best defense. The offense, we've seen the heights they've reached over the last couple years when they have a certain level of quarterback play. You'd hope you're going to get that. And so, I could sit here and lay out every single reason the Vikings are a 12- win team. I think I could do the exact same thing for the Lions. I think I could do the exact same thing for the Packers. I think I could do the exact same thing for the Bears. I don't know if there's any division in the league I could do that about. There are other really strong ones, but not a top four like this where I think it'd be really easy to make those arguments for all of them. >> When you look out today, you chose joint practices to come take your traveling uh visits. I know you've been going camp to camp and this is uh the joint practice against the Ravens. What do you like to draw from uh the information you like to gather when you're out here? >> I like seeing who's playing where. That that that to me is the most important thing. I don't ever like to draw conclusions about who's playing well in camp based on one training camp practice. I would never presume to think I know, but where are players being deployed? Like how are they thinking about this guy's role? Because this is the time to try that stuff out. And so that's always what I'm most interested in at any training camp practice is more about the ideas that are being trotted out rather than who looked good that day because there's 30 of these and so you can look great one day and not good the next day. >> For sure. Now we're deploying a new quarterback this year and Kyler Murray. How do you think his style will mesh with what kind of Kevin Oonnell does? >> I I like it a lot because I think that Kyler played more under center in Arizona, especially two years ago than he ever had in his career. I think he looked comfortable doing it and his ability to push the ball down the field is probably one of the best things he does. And when this offense has been at its best, you know, two years ago when Sam Darnold was here, they were explosive. That's what they wanted to be in the passing game. And I honestly think that Kyler is able to tap into that in a way that could be really beneficial. >> Awesome. Well, Robert, thank you so much. You can listen to the Athletics NFL show daily. >> Yes. Soon. >> Soon. Okay. When does the daily start? >> It's hard for me to say. I I I think the schedule's in my mind. I I honestly think starting next week we'll have something every day. >> There you go. Well, anyway, check them out, please. This is Robert May with The Athletic, and we appreciate you visiting us at camp. Thank you so much.

title: Minnesota Vikings Team Press Conferences Post-Joint Practice with Ravens | August 19
text: It always gets more intense with these joint practices. How much did it level up out there today? >> Uh it felt really good. Um finally get to compete against somebody else in a practice setting. Um and we were able to just uh come out and just work on the things that we were working on this whole camp against a good defense and um in a practice setting like I said. So like um it's just great to kind of get it done in practice and then um to go watch tape, see our corrections, and have a chance to come do it again tomorrow. >> Can you do things in this setting that maybe you almost can't do in a preseason game where everything's a little more it's live but it's >> Yeah. >> it's a little more vanilla and not as much scheming whereas here you you you might be trying to do some things that you won't be you're showing people in a preseason game. >> Yeah, 1000%. Um it's it's way different than the games or it's practice. Uh we're kind of cutting it loose. Just trying to get those those reps against a good defense like I said and um uh it's just a great opportunity just for the team to see where we're at and um like I said to have the two days against a a good front like that, Baltimore man, it's really it's really good work. >> What did today tell you about how well the offense is gelling? >> Uh well we still got some things to clean up. Um but that's what like I said practice is for and um I feel like we're at the the right point and like I said we'll be able to watch this film tonight and uh come out here tomorrow and really execute. And uh we we see what they're going to do to us uh that we didn't know coming out onto the field. Um we're going to make our adjustments. I'm pretty sure they're going to make some too but yeah we'll be ready to go. >> Appreciate you guys talking a lot about the run game this camp. How do you feel it transferred over today against Baltimore? >> Um they they did some different things uh to kind of stop that. Um and that's some things that we need to clean up. Uh but like I said we're right where we want to be and uh we'll continue to to stack days and and continue to get better. >> As I was going to ask you about the run game when you especially you have an Aaron Jones and you have a AJ Dillon who can just They both have come back to camp looking amazing. You guys like made super sized holes for them against the Giants. What was different today do you think in their scheme? >> Uh yeah they brought a lot of pressure. Um and and it's just kind of just like we got to communicate and uh just be ready for put pressure and just and and just attack it. >> What did you think of Kyler's throw in the two-minute drill? >> Well, him and him and JJ, man, they they they had two great throws at the end. Um it's a great way to end practice. >> What does it mean for you guys when you're going to face them again tomorrow and again on Saturday? You know, you you really get that chance to get that familiarity. >> Exactly. Um against a premier defense in this league, we have one, too. Um but B Flow, he's kind of a little different. And um just to be able to go against Baltimore, man, it is like I said, it's a true test. Um just to see where we're at and uh but we know we got some things we can fix, but we're right where we want to be. >> Do you welcome the edge, the chippiness maybe, with the familiarity? >> Uh no, man. We we just come out here to practice and get better. >> So like to to go against another team in joint practices, the energy, how do you describe it? >> Uh we kind of just treated it like another practice. Trying to go out there, be smart, stay off the quarterback, and kind of just just be a pro. So we just kind of use it to take our physicality and apply the pressure that we usually would, you know, going against our ones and twos. So we kind of didn't go in it with a different mindset. >> With Lamar Jackson out there, how would you describe how the secondary unit did? >> Uh we just had to be ourselves. We didn't try to make it bigger than what it had to been, but uh I think going against a great guy like him, you know, it was able to teach our, you know, our eyes great eyes and great techniques and, you know, filling gaps and things like that. So we kind of just went in there with a great mindset. >> How much pressure did you guys bring in in the 11 on 11? >> It was a lot at the end, especially. The great energy from the fans, so you know, that's that's what that's what we do it for, you know, so we got to find a way to keep making plays and give the fans a reason to cheer. >> What have you seen from J Ward this camp? >> Uh he responded a lot, you know, came back from, you know, a concussion and first day out he's making plays, great play, you know, last week as we know against Jackson. Should have went for the ball, but he knows that. Uh just just showing up when his name is called, so. >> When it comes to those blitzes, just like how much communication is involved in every one of those pressures before the snap? Like how much do you have to know is going on before that happens? >> A lot of communication. Above my pay grade for that one right there. Uh shout out to the safeties. You know, they're they're great. They're always in their books and and they know what we need to get in in certain situations and things like that. You know, I just get the call and just do my job. >> Mhm. How does it change your job when you know that those guys are probably going to get home? >> I just got to just be prepared for the ball come my way, make the play, and the ball goes out to the side, just chase the ball, and then make a tackle, help my team, but you know, just whatever call they call, I'm pretty sure we're going to be all right. >> Is there just want to ask about Jacob Thomas, just coming in as as a UDFA and obviously, you know, he said he still has a lot to learn, but just what have you seen from him and his willingness to kind of get out there and >> Uh he's he's waking up now. He's talking more. I don't know if the interception or whatever, but he's talking a lot more now. Got him from the team and had to sing a song, so he's kind of getting comfortable. So, just seeing him walk around and actually talk to a lot more people and starting to be more vocal. I think he's kind of finding his way through, but he's he's growing a lot. >> Well, his ability to get around the ball, is that athleticism or is that quickness or people? >> I think it's both. I think he's a a great player. You look at his JMU tape, he was one of those guys, and he helped JMU turn that program around as well. So, just bringing his energy here and and showing it and putting it on tape on the actual preseason game, so I'm proud of him he was able to do that. And then coming out here and just being where he needs to be, filling, like I said, filling in the gaps and great communication, so he's filling it well. >> So, that talented group over there looked pretty good. >> Uh it was good today. Uh obviously, we brought that energy. Um I feel like obviously, I I gave up two catches in one-on-ones, so you know, that's already still in my mind. I got to get back on on that, but I feel like as a defense, we uh we did a hell of a job today. And obviously, we got another day tomorrow to go get better. >> How's Jay Ward look today and overall in >> Man, good. He's obviously been flying around. Um playing multiple positions, so he just it's good to see him out there actually, you know, just going fast, playing ball, and just going, like I said, picking his speed up every single every time we're out there. >> Is it interesting to see it get a little heated, not too much? >> Uh you know, we are competitors. It's going to happen here and there, but you know, you just got to go the next play and keep working. Obviously, we've got to come back tomorrow and do the same thing, so we can't carry it over. >> Felt good to see the defense kind of shut them down a a lot over there in the corner. >> Definitely felt good. Obviously, have the whole sideline turned up like that felt good. Like I said, yeah, we did a good job today, but obviously, I think there's a plays we could do better on and then obviously, go watch the film and get better from that. >> As a veteran, do you enjoy this situation with more of a practice situation that you're facing another team? >> I definitely love it. Yeah, you obviously get to go compete against another team that's not in the same color as you. And obviously, like you said, they got a good group over there receivers, so we're getting that work in every day. That's just going to get us >> Keep your eye on him and ask about the young guy, Jacob Thomas. What have you seen from him in your room since he joined back in February? >> I would say Jacob's a very a smart player. I would say uh, most of the times he's always in the right spot just knowing what he's doing. So, to just to come in and get the defense down like that, especially because, you know, it's kind of he's kind of everywhere, too. He's one of those guys that's playing multiple positions. Just to see him come in every single day just know what to do. He's always in the right spot, but smart player for sure. >> You don't see too many rookies do that. >> Definitely, dog. You know, there's going to be some mistakes. Even sometimes I got mistakes, but he's just always in the right spot doing the right thing. So, that's one thing about Jacob, you just you rely on him for sure. >> What do you tell young guys to embrace when it comes to joint practice? >> I would just say just go out there, obviously, just get better. That's what it is. You're just going out there, you're going to work. It's practice. Obviously, you want to treat it like a game, like you're getting ready for a game, but it's definitely practice. You just go work on your craft, your technique. And obviously, what the coaches are telling us to do. Just, you know, all those little things, little details that we've got to get better on. You've got to work that out there at practice. >> I mean, it's fun, man. Some stuff is a little extra, but it is what it is, man. >> Kevin talked to you earlier that sometimes preseason the games are meant to be vanilla, but today maybe some actual chances to see some live looks, some real things. Do you see that fair? >> Yeah, man. I think it's uh, a little more uh, realistic, to say the least, cuz you know, you don't know what they're going to run, they don't know what you're going to run, so you kind of got to just play by your rules and play football. That's I mean, I just like it that way, you know. Just move the ball and you know, things aren't really set up to to scheme one another. You you of just out there playing, so it's it's it's nice, man. >> You chalk today up as a win in your mind. You guys kept their off their one offense from doing much. >> Yeah, yeah. Well, I mean, for sure the that last bit um you know, we did a good job. Um the other stuff, I mean, we'll just have to check the tape and see, but I think guys were playing hard. Guys are playing physical, and that's what it's all about, man. Coming out here and playing physical ball. >> Do you enjoy this more so than a preseason game? This kind of style of workout with another team? >> Uh I mean, for for, you know, guys getting a lot of reps, it's definitely kind of like that, you know, cuz it's uh it's definitely physical. It's definitely that aspect of uh you know, just playing ball. So, it's kind of like uh playing a a game without, you know, taking people down to the ground. So, it's it's good work. >> How special is it this year already with you? I know Blake Cashman, he Blake played lights out last game obviously against the Giants, but just the familiarity that you guys have. You kind of in this flow with the defense. >> Yeah. Yeah, yeah, it's good. It's good. It's definitely uh a lot of defense is just chemistry, you know, communication, chemistry, being on the same page. So, it's fun playing with these guys. It's It's so much fun, and uh especially when out there rolling. Um yeah, I think uh we're on the same page today, and just a matter of stacking days just over and over again. >> And some of the young kids say that they're on the E-will kind of training regimen. They want to kind of beef up a little bit. They're kind of make a joke about that. I mean, what do you say to the young guys that are like like I got to keep I got to keep up. >> Yeah, yeah. The our young guys are doing a good job, man. They're They're um you know, in the playbook. They're doing the right things. They're playing hard. Uh they're trying to do it right and do the the right way, show up. So, hats off to those guys. >> Were there any moments today? I mean, now that you have a day of joint practice under your belt, do you just want to expand on tomorrow? Maybe move forward from it? >> Yeah, it's definitely um you know, whatever success you had today, whatever mess up you had today, you got to just let it go and keep stacking days. Um come with your best foot forward, you know, over and over again. So, tomorrow um regardless of how today went, we got to bring it again. So. >> How'd you feel like it went the first day? >> Good. Joint practice is always unique, you know, because both teams are kind of seeing what they got and it's fun to hit someone else and uh you know, feel a different technique, especially from an offensive line perspective and uh excited to get back to day two and improve on, you know, what we need to improve on. >> How much did you feel like they were showing you guys? >> Say Say it again. Sorry. >> did you feel like they were showing you guys? >> Um No, I mean they they brought a lot of different looks and uh that's one nice thing about Bevell's defenses. It's It's a lot of different looks. So, um no, it's it's just good to see another defense. >> To be able to finish like you guys did, I mean how I don't know. What is that? >> Yeah, it's huge. Um you know, I think I think we wanted to be better in the run game today, but um that's a that's a big thing for us is just finishing strong and we did that, which is awesome. >> Yeah, man. It looked like a hell of a throw by Kyler to hit JJ there. >> Yeah, baller. You know, I think he's off his back foot. I looked at the replay and then, you know, JJ is always open somewhere. So, uh that was awesome. Good way to close out practice. >> You talked to Icko about what he likes about these kind of practices rather than just a preseason game. What do you like to take from it rather than like bright lights out in this stadium? >> Yeah, I think um you know, one thing about training camp is you're going against your own guys that you've been going against for three, four weeks. Um and so, to to experience something kind of new and you know, use your technique against a different style of defense. Um there's many different ways to play D-line and so, the way we want to run off the ball, it's it's good to hit hit these combinations and man reaches uh a little bit differently. >> How about the familiarity? You get them again tomorrow and then again on Saturday. It can get a little chippy, but you can also learn a little bit, right? >> Yeah, absolutely and that's part of the learning process is, you know, we're going to go in tonight and watch the tape and uh figure out what we need to change and improve on and then go from there. >> How do you evaluate your snapping today? >> Uh I thought it was good. I I Kyler and I have a open line of communication for sure and um you know, I asked him throughout practice and he said they were all good. >> When do you know that then if you're in the flow with him. >> Uh the flow? >> I I I think we're always in a flow state, you know, that's kind of a thing as an offense. You need to be seeing things the the same way and all that and so uh I think we kind of stay in a flow. >> Uh different go to playing against another team with a different scheme. Tired of being up our own guy. But two minute you talking about my play? Which one? >> Both of them I said. The sack and the near the near pick. >> That was a pick but Flo J had them on the first play so we came back with a sack. >> What what's it like when you guys are blitzing a whole bunch against them in in these drills and these practices? >> When my blitzing uh defend ourselves for the season. I mean put all 11 on the field and you go go out and compete. >> Hey Jay, just how much more confident are you feeling this time around compared to the other training camps? >> I'm definitely confident. I know what I'm doing, know my assignment, communicating more. Feeling more comfortable who I'm playing with. >> Is that the big part? You you seem like you're in the slot a lot. That kind of big nickel stuff. When when you don't have to think as much is that a big part of just kind of feeling like you can play fast and all that? >> No, I know. Yeah, I mean wherever they need me I can just go and play. >> You also seem really in sync too with Cashman and and help. He does his role you do your role even in the uh preseason game that it resulted in an interception. Like what what's it like to kind of have familiarity and kind of get into a flow with the other teammates like that? >> Uh just knowing who you playing with kind of building up a communication and knowing how they going to play and how you going to play. It's really the chemistry that build up and you can play off of it. >> Yeah, it's like now you're playing on instinct, right? Not even on thinking about the playbook which is hard to say with a guy like B Flo and everyone, >> Yeah, just know what I'm doing and know how the person will fit it so it just move a little lot of smooth with me. >> When did you feel like you started to really click with this defense just cuz you've had some years to develop? Like when was that that you thought I really got it? >> Uh last year. When don't know if found my swag about myself. >> Has this camp gone like according to plan to date? Is kind of how you wanted it to go? >> I mean, it's all right. I got I always got room to get better. But, it's going along. >> Do you do enjoy these joint practices? Kind of treat it like a preseason game cuz it is a practice situation against another team? >> I mean, I I really enjoy both. Just going out here to compete. I mean, we ain't going to be able to go on Sundays and compete with our own team, but so I really enjoy the joint practices. >> Specifically, but watching Blake and Eric do their thing. >> Yeah, yeah, yeah. You know Blake and Eric and our captains and our linebackers and our defense, they going to lead the way. They going to make sure they do their job every time. >> What's the fine line like? I mean, there were some mini skirmishes, but there wasn't anything like the Cowboys and Saints. >> Yeah, yeah, yeah. It was cool. It wasn't nothing crazy, you know what I'm saying? It's going to get physical out here. It's joint practice, you know? It's only my second joint practice of my career, but I I know for a fact it's going to get physical. >> How much do you think things ramp up? I mean, you remember from last year with the Patriots joint practices like this time of training camp as we're getting closer to September 13th? How much do you think things ramp up? >> Oh, it's ramped up a lot, you know what I'm saying? You know what I'm saying? We got the We got the season about to start, you know? We got this preseason game and one more and then we here. So, you know, things are ramping up, you know? It's getting physical, getting chippy. It's football. >> How do you evaluate your play so far? >> Oh, I'm doing I feel like I'm doing great, you know what I'm saying? I still got a lot of things I need to work on, you know? Keep doing it. Come out here doing it day by day. >> How great is your versatility in being lined up in some different spots? >> Yeah, it's definitely it's definitely helping me, you know what I'm saying? Being able to have be on the defense a little bit more, style on the field a little bit more. Um, just got to keep learning and keep, you know what I'm saying? buying in and learning new things every day.

title: Minnesota Vikings Legends Share Mankato Training Camp Memories | Slice of Mankato
text: Hi, I'm Bobby Bryant. John Turner, JT. Hey, I'm Wayne Smith. My name is John Henderson. >> I'm Andrew Jordan. This is my slice of Mankato. >> And then this is my slice of Mankato. [music] >> And this is my slice of Mankato. >> Back in Jake's in Mankato with a slice of pizza. >> This is my first time being back since 1973. >> It's good to be back. >> Where are we going today? >> We're going for some pizza down in >> What's up, babe? How you doing? >> I'm here in Glass Bank. >> We're here for 52 training camps until 2017 was our last training camp in >> How you feeling? >> No, man. I'm about to cry up in here, man. All that money I left on the table. >> [laughter] >> Yes, sir. >> It's good. Bring back memories. >> I know when I first got drafted to the Vikings, um, first thing we did was ride the bus to Mankato. You know what I mean? All the rookies had to ride the bus to Mankato. So, different route, but same trip. You know, things have changed, you know, but uh, the memories, you know, bring back that feeling of, um, you know, what you used to do, what it was like 20, 30 years ago and to now, you know, so, um, it's a great feeling. It's a great to be back. >> We rolled up. And of course, you remember things being in different places. I'm looking for Jake's where it used to be. It was a different place and then they said, "Oh, well, no, it moved. It's up a little bit." So, we came on down the road. And then we pulled in and the sign is just as I remembered it. I had so many fun memories at that moment cuz I didn't get them until that moment when I saw the sign. And I thought about at many days after practice we sat in there, all the guys sitting, we're talking, we're laughing, we're recuperating from the practice, and that was some of the fondest memories I have, sitting with Ahmad, laughing and talking with him, sitting with Sammy, laughing and talking with him. And the offensive guys are talking more trash to the defensive guys. You know, cuz we just had practice, or we may have just gotten through with 7-on-7. And it was just a special moment, cuz not only was it fun, but it's bonding. >> I think just being around the guys, you know, going out with them and talking at night, having a beer or something. That's the most important thing that I enjoyed about training camp. With the camaraderie and the people that you meet and the friendships all after work. >> We came to Jake's in our off time, and uh and it was always good to be able to come in and and and have a cold one, and uh uh the people there were always nice. And it was close. It was only a couple blocks from from our uh dorm, so so it was not hard to get there, and we didn't have to worry about getting a speeding ticket going back to the dorm. >> That was. >> One of the most traumatic experiences that I had was my first week that I was here, Jim Marshall came up to me. He said, "Come and go with me. Jump in my car." I did, like a fool. And there's a big, steep hill off the campus, and he had it floored. The car was airborne, and I thought I was going to die. >> Uh I don't remember nothing but for me seeing blue sky. >> And I hadn't even been in practice yet. >> For me, a little skinny defensive back from the University of South Carolina, 160 lb to play 14 years on a team like the Minnesota Vikings uh was a dream come true. >> I've got some fond memories of Bobby Bryant. One of the memories that I have of him was that he ran my patterns better than I did. >> So so I'm responsible for him being as good as he is. >> I was lucky to be able to look at film of of John and of course we we practiced against him twice a day. That's not an efficient use of the space. Somebody's got to take the cutback lane. Somebody's got to cut off the just like cut him off if he goes screaming down the field, and somebody's got to do something in the middle, and you know, you get 10 versions of that, somebody's going to make the tackle. So, somebody, one of those three people, and I would even put it on the guy in the back, who was Adams, um needs to take that cutback lane away, and then that thing doesn't break free at all, and you have a probably a field goal attempt. Relating that to Adrian Peterson. Peterson, what what you described there requires very rare athleticism. To be able to press so that a defender has to full send, they got to be blazing. And if that defender is blazing, they're probably trying to track at that point to to the to the runner's near hip. Or actually, back in that day, a lot of times they would go to the op hip. So, if you think about, you know, somebody's running and they're like running past you, right? You've got the hip that's close to you, and you have the one that you have to kind of get across to, right? So, back in those days, tackling was a lot more get to the opposite hip, so you put your whole body in front of their waist and and their chest, and then it's going to be a lot more difficult for them to run out. But you would get a lot of spin moves that way. A lot of LaDainian Tomlinson would would kill you that way. And so, nowadays they say it's a little more common to see near hip, and then to like kind of roll away and do like they they'll call it the gator roll tackle or like the hawk tackle, which came out, you know, in the Pete Carroll era. Uh or that was what the Pete Carroll Seahawks called it, and that's a very famous example. I guess it's not like he invented it, but I digress. With Adrian Peterson, being able to press and essentially force that player to attack his opposite hip, and then being able to slam on the brakes as quickly as he did meant that you could essentially abuse the tackling logic of the day where you would get to the opposite hip and and try to like spin somebody down, but it would force that defender to essentially dive across you. And if you could snap slam on the brakes right before, you could you could snap off a big cutback. And what Peterson did so well was also the jump cut. So, you need to have the speed to force it, the deceleration to punish it, and the jump cut to get all the way across and ruin everybody's angle. And when he would jump cut, he could jump cut across the universe. And then all of those tackling angles would be ruined, and people all had to go adjust and find a new way. And sometimes they could do that and catch him if they were fast enough, but that's going to make you go way further down the field, right? It's going to turn this from a nice gain into an explosive. That's I guess the best answer I have to that Adrian Peterson question. The last one I'm going to answer comes from KOC, the B Flo merchant, who asks, "Now that it's clearly established that any QB under the play under the age of 30 playing in KOC system has been a total embarrassment, JJ Dobs, Hall Brosmer. And the offensive head coach not being able to put an offense together means not that we need a new head coach necessarily, but that we need a new guy in charge of the offense. And who should be the head coach is a question separate from that. Some people have even said, you know, KOC should be the C should do the CEO role, become a John Harbaugh, and then hire an offensive coordinator to do his offense, you know, Pete Carroll style. I don't really buy into that very much. That's just not a thing that he will do. You're you're not going to get that. Like that's I'm sure that could work well if you're really chase the rabbit there, but I don't think you're going to get that. So, rather I would like to see if we get to a let's fire Kevin O'Connell, which is not going to have anything to do with Brian Flores if and when that conversation comes about. That's going to be about O'Connell being a head coach. if we get to that promoting Brian Flores is absolutely a candidate and they should interview other candidates as well, but keep that idea very much in mind, especially if Flores ends up getting like an interim head coach deal depending on when this kind of thing happens. But the ball is very in O'Connell's court about that. It doesn't have anything to do with Flores outproducing him or anything like that. Flores outproducing him means that if you do can the head coach this is an option. Look how good he's his unit is playing. And guys have rallied around him, right? But head coach is not just the guy with the best unit. That's the other thing about this. Kevin O'Connell being head coach as a leader, as a guy who tries to, you know, get this organization under his feet to to try to get peace and collaboration in all of this, right? That's why you brought him in instead of Mike Zimmer. Getting all of that is paramount. And with that stuff maybe starting to crumble, that's another reason to say, "Hey, it's not just about your play calling as a head coach. It's also about what you do as the CEO of the team basically. And if that starts to crumble, that's a thing. But then you look at Brian Flores and how he went with the Dolphins, that's kind of the biggest argument against Brian Flores. Is what happened with the Dolphins in terms of him actually having to be a leader and establishing a relationship with a with a quarterback that mentally was not in the place to take coaching the way Brian Flores gives it. Um maybe Kyler Murray's a different mentality or whatever, but that's also a thing you probably have to reckon with if you're going to start calling for that. And so for me, while it's an idea in the back of my head that's like, "Oh, this is maybe a possibility in 2 years. Maybe we're looking back and saying, 'Oh, that was going to happen.'" That's not something that I'm going to call for before I'm just generically saying, "Oh, we got to go and fire Kevin O'Connell." Which is not where I'm at. Maybe his seat is hot, but it's going to take a one and four start for that to actually materialize into anything. And I'm not going to call for it before the one and four start. I'm just saying if there is one, we got to wait for that. And that will have that impact down the road. I will talk to you all tomorrow. And as always, skull.
