title: Aaron Glenn Training Camp Press Conference (8/19) | New York Jets
text: morning. Uh came out of practice uh fairly well today when it comes to injuries. The guys that we had on the management plan today was T Sweat, uh Osai, and Kiko. Kiko probably had the most reps out of anybody in camp. So, we want to make sure we monitor him um and take care of him today. Um guys that had vet days was TP Tim Patrick and Anyada. Uh other than that, when it comes to practice, obviously man was quick, fast, to the point. Um the base down reps the first two uh series, then went right into the red zone where we had about 15 reps of red zone. I think our guys did a really good job of that. Um man, practice started out really high for the defense. I thought those guys were getting after it fairly well. And then the offense picked it up when it came to the red zone. something that you want to see as a head coach, but man, you want to make sure that we always on go no matter what. So, that's something we'll talk to the guys about. Um, other than that, our practice was good. So, any questions? >> Have you came up with your plan for Friday night with Gino and the starters? Are they still playing on plan? >> Um, listen, the players going to play. Um, and then things can change, you know, as we get closer to game time. >> When you say the match with those guys, will you play them this week or you going to give them a little more? for guys that didn't practice that. >> That's something we'll continue to talk about and think about as we go through um like next couple of days. >> Is Gino's ankle limiting him in any way in practice? >> You know what? I wouldn't say that. I just think there's soreness. And listen, I think any player at this point knows that, man, something's going to hurt at some point. So, um but listen, he's a competitor. He wants to make sure he gets those reps in. But the thing is, we want to be smart, too, about how we go about doing things when it comes to him and any of our players. So, um, it's not to a point to where he can't go out. Obviously, he's out there practicing, but again, we want to make sure that we're doing the right thing when it comes to him playing. >> That tough decision for Friday night because you got your starting quarterback on. You don't want to put him in harm's way in any way, but you probably know he he needs revs, new offense and everything. So, how does that kind of, >> you know, it it is it is, but I think the thing that we do um quite a bit is make sure we have game intensity in practice. And I think our guys do a really good job of that. And it's it's not just with Gino, it's any player, you know, um Bree, Garrett, you know, Double D, any of those guys is as we get towards the end of it, man, we want to make sure we make the right decision on playing the guys or not. And then sometimes, man, the guys want to get out there and play, you know. So, um I've never been a coach that that was afraid of injuries because it's it's it's part of the game, you know, but I also want to be a coach that's smart and make sure I get our guys ready for week one. there. Can you speak a little bit to the the time that it takes a receiver to acclimate from from college to pro? So, I feel like 10 years ago it was an understanding that it takes receivers a little more time and then you had the Odell class kind of blew that out of the water and you've seen some success immediately, but still like that it does it's sometimes a challenge specifically with Cooper like did you get up to speed? >> Yeah, absolutely. and and and to for my opinion, um I think when when you're in college, the coverage system is not as vast as you get to the NFL. Obviously, uh in the NFL, the guys do a really good job of understanding like when they want to rotate. Um they can be a man coverage and still be 10 yards deep. So, it's kind of hard to really like understand exactly what the coverage is until post snap. So, um in the NFL, like defense does a really good job of that. And I think that's the transition that most receivers have to make to really understand what is the coverage so I can understand what route I have to run. So um but I think these guys are getting more intelligent, you know, and understanding uh the defense a lot better and I think coach is doing a good job of teaching guys that so they can go out there and be effective as young players. So but I think it's a process and how you coach those guys. Everything every phase of camp is obviously critical, but for young >> players trying to make this team Yeah. >> or trying to make a roster in the National Football League, >> can you speak about how significant it is coming up the second preseason game next week, these final practices? >> Yeah, and for me, I look at it um I look at it a number of different ways. And I think the most important thing for me is, man, taking a good look at this player for us and how he fits in what we're doing. Um, and then how is he playing? Is he playing to a point to where, man, we can't ignore, you know, that how good this player is and how do we get him to fit into to our roster when it comes to that. Um, but also giving those guys a chance to be on another team cuz listen, it's we all know you can't have everybody that's in camp. So, um, some guys are going to make it, some guys are not, but at least you give those guys an opportunity to put put film out there so they do get a chance for other teams to see them and and we talk about that quite a bit that man, there's 31 other teams that's looking at this tape. So, you want to put your best foot forward every time you go out on the grass. Um, and I think a lot of uh young players understand that. So, and we try to help them with that quite a bit. But again, man, we're looking at every player on how do they fit within what we're doing and giving those guys every opportunity to make this team. With that being said, do you like the increased depth on the roster? >> Say it again. >> With that being said, do you like the increased depth on the roster that you see? >> Absolutely. Absolutely. And and it's something that just happening to us, happened to every team is injuries are going to happen. And listen, there there's always going to be a a talent drop off, you know, when you go from your top guy to the next guy. But the mentality doesn't have to change. The mentality could be the exact same. And I think that's the one way that you keep your team afloat when you do have injuries to where, okay, is the talent down? Yes. But this league is about mentality, you know, and how guys can come in and actually play the same way that the guy in front of him was playing. So, um, and we we talk about that quite a bit and I've experienced that quite a bit in this league. So, um, yes, building the depth and also building mentality of the players that you have. >> After what happened last week, how nice is it to see Stickers out there doing stuff with you guys again? >> Man, it's really good to see Stickers out there. Um, and man, that's anybody in this league cuz I've been a part of some scary situations, you know, my time as a player and as a coach. Um, and to see him out there running around on the cusp of actually getting back to being out on the field, man, it's always good to see. So, um, listen, we pray for him and we know God works. So, um, he's a dang good player and he means a lot to us, you know. So, it's always happy to see him out there. Aaron, have you thought at all about what you really want this defensive identity to be under you? And and does it change from what your defenses look like in Detroit to where they are now? Does it evolve? I mean, what what do you want it to be? >> Yeah. Yeah. Um I I I would say this is from my time in Cleveland to New Orleans to to Detroit, there's a mixture of what I've learned in those um in those places to build exactly what I want. Um, and when you say identity, I I I start to look at that a different way. And to me, your identity is exactly what does the other team say about you. And when that head coach watches tape, you know, there are certain things I want him to say, you know, as far as I want him to know that, man, we're we're going to disrupt the pocket. And when I say disrupt the pocket, meaning we're disrupting the quarterback, I want them to say we're disrupting the receivers. I want to say that we're attacking the ball and I also want to say we're not giving up explosive plays. If we if we can have that head coach saying that about us, I think we're doing a pretty good job. >> Along those lines when you talk about the defense, you know, we we know why uh Deario was brought in obviously, but when you talk about his leadership, like how have you seen that? What impact has he had? >> Wow. Um it's been a number of things and there's a there there's a number of guys that we brought in that's also helped that. And but when you just talk about Deario in itself, it's the energy every time those guys go out and play. And listen, camp is dog days and there's going to be times where you're riding high and man, the guys get tired. It's all part of it. But do you have a player on that team, man, that can keep that energy going and keep guys going at a high level? And I think he does a hell of a job of that. I think he does a hell of a job in the meeting rooms when we're meeting together of man, this is this is what coach wants. This is what he's looking for cuz he's been with me. He understands what I'm looking for. Um, him doing that, his ability to pull guys to the side and have one-on-one conversations. his ability to pull the whole defense to a side and have conversations. His ability to pull the whole team together and have conversations. All those things you see, but again, it's it's not just double D. We have a number of guys that um that has that trait. And I think they're doing a hell of a job for us. >> As he continues to grow, what would you like to see the club make on Friday night? >> That's exactly him growing and the mistakes that that he made in the game that those same mistakes don't show up. And that's what you want to see with everybody. Um, and I know we're speaking on on Cade right now. And listen, I think every time he practices, he's getting better and better and better. Um, but I also like the fact that those mistakes that he make in practice, we're able to coach him and he understands those mistakes. I think that's the number one thing when it comes to um, any player is, man, when those mistakes happen, let's attack those mistakes right now. Let's make sure we clean it up. Let's make sure he understands the why behind the mistake. Uh I think that's the most important part part for any player is understanding the why behind it. I think that's when you improve the most. >> You just quiet over that man. >> What's that? >> You being quiet over that. [laughter] >> I got sneak attack. Um big picture question. You're locked in dayto day right now. But you talked last year about you know takes a while to turn big ships. >> Y >> where do you feel like you are in that process of turning this around now? You've seen this team all spring, three weeks of camp. Where do you feel guarding the big process? >> That's that's a really good question. And listen, that process happened, I mean, obviously right after that process continue to happen after the end of the season. We have our exit meetings and then getting the players that we want to get in the building. Um, now is man, you got two different schemes offensively and defensively that you want to make sure that you tighten up and make sure those things are going right. Um, and I think I think our guys doing a good job. I think our coaches are doing a good job of that. Um, and we'll know exactly where we're at once the season starts and I'm excited about where we are. I would tell you that. So, um, I guess to answer your question, we're still turning that ship. We're still turning it, but I like exactly where we are. >> How did you like the game operation last week? I think you had Duker and uh, Reich upstairs. And also, can you just speak about >> You've been calling plays out here. You called plays before, but >> Yep. Did you like just having that >> under your player? >> I really enjoyed it. I I really did. Um again, it felt like old defensively it felt like old times um in Detroit because Duke was upstairs and he was my eyes upstairs and when you're upstairs, you're able to do that. So, I I totally understand why some coordinators like being upstairs. Um, I just always like being on the field as a coordinator. I always like being on the field to be able to touch, talk, you know, have have a um, firsthand with the players when something happens. Um, but defensively, man, it felt really, really good. And our communication was on point, you know, just like it always been. Um, and then with Frank upstairs, um, his ability to to relay information to me, to be able to talk to the offense or have the quarterback coaches or any of the other coaches relay their messages into the to their to their positions was good. And the thing is, I'm able to to relay a message from Frank if we have to pull the offense up if need be. Um, Sean Jefferson's able to pull the guys together if need be. So, that dynamic worked really, really well. And again, it's something that we're going to continue to see how we can get better and better at. Um, but I thought it went well. >> Do you know whose cars came in the parking lot there? >> You know, it's funny that you say that because um, some of the players are saying that that I get those cars, the electric cars, you know, that's lined up on that deal, man, that they're going to have some dents in the in the hood. So, um, but I'm assuming, you know, that's something we got to look at. You know, we're gonna continue to keep kicking that way. But as long as it's going through uh through through the uprises, man, I'm all good. Guys going to have to buy new cars. [laughter] All right, fellas.

title: Aaron Glenn Training Camp Press Conference (8/18) | New York Jets
text: Good morning. Um injuries. Uh Breece and Mike Kale, uh both of those guys will be out with Breece with the groin and Mike Kale with the calf. Both of those guys will be out two to three weeks. Uh that's why we had a two-minute at the end of it. Knowing how tired the guys were going through it. It was physical also, you know, so uh being able to run a two-minute at the very end, um try to get the guys going and understanding, man, we got to continue to compete uh at a high level even once you get into that fourth quarter, even once you get into that end of half situations. And uh I think our guys did a really good job of that. Listen, we still have a ways to go, um but we are improving on a daily basis and that's uh that's all I can ask for these guys as a coach. Improvement and discipline is what we look for. So, any questions? >> How much of a relief was that to get that news on Breece? >> Not [clears throat] just Breece, Breece, but any of our guys that has injuries that we know it's not going to be a long-term injury. So, but obviously for that player knowing how important he is for what we're doing, um it was really exciting to hear it. >> What are you expecting or hoping to see from Grayland against the Steelers? >> Um exactly what he's been doing for the most part and then listen, it's it's it's no like we're not looking at that at at him as you know, a second team it's 1A 1B with those guys, you know, and even with our other guys. I mean cuz those guys are going to be in. I mean we know how important they are to what we're doing. Understand what your landmarks are, hit it up in there and be Grayland. >> It seems like Siddiq's starting to move around a little more. Is he Is he getting closer? >> Um I would say so. I'll say him and Pons, they're getting closer. And and the goal has always been getting those guys ready for week week one. So, um again, we have a management plan on all those guys and we're going to make sure we stick to that to make sure that they're ready for week one. >> Has Pons taken longer than you thought, KG? Cuz it seemed like at the beginning of camp you were pretty optimistic he'd be back quickly. >> No, that thing from the very beginning, that timeline has been exactly what we've been talking about. Um I mean obviously got guys have different times of of of when they're going to get better at because just knowing the body of of each player, but um we targeted that week week one for him, you know, from the very beginning. Um and hopefully he'll be in practice before that to make sure that we get as many reps with that players we can. But again, he's in every meeting. He's done a really good job of understanding exactly what their what the responsibilities are from a nickel and outside corner perspective. Um and we're looking forward to getting him back. >> How much can you expect from Siddiq considering the time that he's missed in the spring and then >> Yeah, well, that's to be seen, you know. Um the thing is is he's in he's in walk-through. He's in the meeting, so even though he's getting the mental reps, well, I understand he has to get those live reps. Um he's a very intelligent man and listen, we don't think that he's going to miss a beat when it's time for him to get on the field with us. >> I know you want to be cautious at times. Like how do you handle Geno's situation? Is it beneficial for him to play in the preseason based on, you know, whatever >> Well, we'll see. We'll see and um every day it's a management plan for that player and um and I think you guys have heard me say this about all of our players. We want to make sure that we get our guys ready for week one. So, whatever we have to do to be able to do that, I mean, that's what we're going to do. So, if it's playing in this game because he feels up to it and he's ready to go and he want wants to be with the other guys, let's go. If it's not playing because we want to continue to be cautious in that situation, we'll do that, but it's all about how he feels and then exactly how do we see this going going moving forward. >> If he's healthy enough, um what is your philosophy on playing? There's been a big trend in the league where a lot of guys aren't playing any starters. >> Yeah. Yeah. Well, it's no different than what we did last week. We played everybody last week, you know, and then we have guys that has um some little nicks and bruises. We'll see exactly how that is and make a decision that they should play or not. So, um listen, we're playing our guys. That's what we've done and each case-by-case basis, we'll see exactly where they at when it comes to injuries and things like that and um we'll look at it at that point. >> With Geno, if he's healthy enough and wants to play, what what what do you deem as the importance for him to get some game action against another team? >> This is his first time. It's something about being able to do that just live that it's just totally different from practice. So, um I think it's beneficial to be able to do that. Um I understand, you know, other coaches and and and their philosophy on it. Um but, there's a certain belief that I have and and the players are all in um on what we're trying to do. So, if guys are up for it, you know, we're playing. >> Obviously, you still have two preseason games remaining, but how much uh how much attention are you looking towards towards week one? >> Say that one time. >> How much how much attention are, you know, planning are you doing for week one? >> Yeah. Right [clears throat] now, man, we're in training camp mode, you know, so there's other things that we're trying to make sure we get accomplished when it comes to that. We have a training camp plan that we all understand and that's where everybody's head is at right now. Um listen, we have plenty of time to get ready for Tennessee, you know, but so man, it is like it is about what we're trying to accomplish right now during training camp, going through these preseason games, and then we'll get to Tennessee when it's time. >> All right, so and sweat on pitch count still and when you went back and watched the film yesterday, what did you see? >> Yeah, they are. Um again, we have a management plan for those guys. Man, they just got back, you know, so um it wouldn't be wise for us just throwing them out there and just let them go, you know. Today was a day that we wanted to hit 40 reps. All right, with our ones and we actually hit that. We might hit 42 those guys. And I've already explained that man, this is this is what I'm trying to get our guys callous to play 65 or 75 plays a game. And going into week four, we're going to hit those 40 reps. Next week, it'll be 50 reps, and then we'll have a scrimmage at the very end that's going to get guys about 65 reps. So, our guys will be ready to play, you know, week one when it comes to that. >> Did you when you talk about getting callous, did you see your your former teammates out there today? >> They're all callous, aren't they? >> They're all calloused. >> I see Keisha Keisha lifting around like, "Dude, what are you What are you lifting around for?" So, he's he's calloused. >> You guys just got to do it a day. Like, it wasn't that hard to get calloused, right? Do you think you Do you think you've lost something with it without without that practice? Or I mean, it's obviously has to be a long time before you retire. >> No doubt. And And listen, um And we were all talking about this. And And actually, it wasn't It was three days, to be honest with you. Some The coach used to get about 20 plays in that third practice, that middle practice, sometime. But, um but that's all we knew. You know? And listen, they tell us to go, we go. That's just what it was. >> [snorts] >> Um but, I think from a medical standpoint, from a from a scientific standpoint, um we've done a lot of things to make sure that we help the uh the health of the player, um and still be able to maximize the reps that you can with walk-throughs and things like that to be able to um to be able to get your concepts exactly how you want to get them. So, um I like what we're doing. I love our schedule. Um I've worked a long time on this. Uh it's From New Orleans to Detroit, there were some things I put together to to make the schedule. I think the players like it, too. You know, cuz we want to make sure we build in not only hard work, but time to recover, also. And that's important to uh to me and the staff and the medical staff to make sure we do that. >> Couple more? No more? All good? >> Nothing else? >> Thank you. >> All right. Thank you, guys. >> Mhm.

Thank you. Good, man. Just you know, it's a great real great team. You know, little competing, but it's getting better like getting better every day and I love I love the battles and we going to keep going. Well, really just focus on and everybody, you know, focus on me just staying healthy, keep being healthy, keep working hard, and just keep doing what my own with my organization want me to do, my coaches, you know, Vrabel and T- Woods and my man my guy Clint and Dylan Cole. So, it's just like every time I hurt, just give the best effort I can and just keep getting the best I could be so I can be the best I could be for this team. >> that's private, man. next time. That's that's just we keep our things private, you know. That's my coach and I respect him so much, so you know, I like to keep things private with me and him. >> What's your relationship been like been with him from last year to this year? How have you seen that grow? >> When I first got when I first met him, I feel like I was with him for 10 years, I feel like because he just he want when I first seen him, I seen a bond. He got me better as a as a player, as a as a better person, as a man. You know, he check up on me even without football. He check up on my family and I respect a hell out of him for that and you know, I really appreciate him as a coach. That's why I really play hard for that man and I do the best I can do to be the best player I can be for him. >> Look like you had a big sack there in the two-minute drill. >> Take us through that and how nice was that for >> Oh, you know, it was we got a good blitz and you know, I'm really just our goal was to get off the field two-minute, you know, don't let them get down field goal range. So, that was our goal keep on dominating. Of course, we're going to keep getting better every day, but you know, like we just all about getting better every day. Everybody had a good great detail. Everybody had good communication. So, you know, we're just going to keep doing what we got to do. >> Do you get the sense of how good your group can be this season? >> Oh, yeah, man. We all stayed out there and we all stayed on consistent to stay everybody being a great on great mindset and great on discipline. I think we're going to be really great and we're going to be really fine and it's all about just keep going every day. >> And that two-minute you got a lot of experience. On that sack, you you talked about quite a few times talking about wanting to finish. Being better when it comes to finishing the pass rush. That's got to be gratifying for you to be able to come out here and put that on tape. >> Oh, um, say one time? I didn't hear you a little bit. >> you you talked a lot about wanting to finish when it Oh, yeah. >> To be able to do something like that has got to be gratifying. >> Yeah, my goal was like, you know, it's it's a lot of athletic quarterbacks in the league, you know what I'm saying? So, they all fast, they got quick feet, you know, they all got good mobility. So, my goal is like every time I get there, I got to bend down, just have good good patience and don't run past them cuz a lot of you know what I'm saying? That's the goal, you know, I missed a lot of plays I wish I had back last year, but I'm focused on the future. My goal is not to do that again, not miss the plays I make and I'm really every time I get back there, I just got to have set up down and make them make them sacks or make any I got to do. >> You talked to Corey yesterday and he said the other day he said he wants to get five sacks. That's his goal. Do you have a similar type of goal that you want to shoot for this year? >> Really just whatever comes my way I'll get them. You know what I'm saying? I don't judge them on the number but what if I get them I get them. You know I had a lot of pressures, a lot of QB hits but you know I got to finish some plays I should have made and that's the goal I got to focus on. So every day I'm out here that's my goal every time to finish them finish them every time I get back there. >> Christian you've been here a couple of years now. Do you feel like the joint practices over time prepare you for week one of the regular season or do you still feel like you want those game reps? >> Of course it's you know we going to get some our team our O-line our O-line is very good. You know I think one of the best O-lines in the league so I mean they make us better they make we make them better. So every time I go against them you know it just make I love going against cuz you know they know our move we know they move. So it's like we love competing against our O-line too but we love I love going against other guys too you know and you know you know they're great players in O-line on the Eagles. They got some good Hall of Famers you know what I'm saying? Good good players and I love going against competition so it's like you know and it's I love to get I love the great work to keep going. >> Christian what does it mean to you talking with Graves, Frank and the training staff to work with you on days where you might need more rest or less practice? >> Really man just that's um that's that's just from my own that's like my organization I'm listening to my coach that's his decision so I'll listen to him whatever he want me to do I do it. >> A lot of familiar faces? >> Yeah for No for the most part got a lot of friends over there from the defense and the offensive side so it was good to see everybody even from Nick and Howie. So No we had we had some good work today. >> Impressive two-minute drill up there at the end like you got in there Christian and all that sort of take us through that and I guess how how good of a moment was that for you and >> Yeah like I said I mean when you going up against a different team in a joint practice you want to have success and obviously I think we we had some great success today. We had a lot of takeaways obviously finished one to finish the day winning the two-minute drill we was able to do that. So no it's I think we're leaving the field feeling good about things but obviously we still had to watch the film and we still some plays being left out there. You know, I kind of felt left out of the the takeaway, you know, count cuz I didn't get one. I got close to one, but um no, man. But it it was fun just watching the guys fly around and make plays. >> Kevin, what were some of the newer looks you felt like you saw today that might help given obviously it's a different offense, it's a different system? >> Yeah, I mean, even from when I was in Philly, obviously they've been having a new coordinator. So, um definitely a lot more different looks that I'm used to with Philly. Um a lot of condensed sets, a lot of motions, um a lot of I will call it eye candy misdirection and things like that. So, but like you said, I think we handled it pretty well. I think our communication on the back end was pretty good. But you still got to watch the film and see the stuff that we can clean up. Probably especially more in the run game as well. >> You've preached takeaways for pretty much your entire career. What's the challenge like for marrying the back end and being able to get takeaways and and you know, track interceptions like that with with getting pressure on the front? How long does that take to kind of come together for a defense? >> Well, I mean, it can it can happen in a flash, honestly. It's something that we definitely preach. Um because they definitely all work together, you know what I mean? Like uh from the front getting pressure, that's first and foremost, the front can get pressure. Obviously, you don't have to cover as long. Maybe you can be more aggressive as far as in your coverage, being able to like you said, being able to jump certain routes and things like that cuz you know, the ball's coming out fast. Uh but then sometimes we got to go out there and cover. At the end of the day, you got to win your one-on-ones. Um but I just think as far as today as far as the calls that was being made, too, cuz I think you got to put it on defensive coordinator. Like obviously, we got to make the plays, but the coach makes the calls and we bring the picture to life. So, uh no, like I said, it was fun. We're going to preach it every single day. We got five. We're looking to get even more tomorrow. It's not something that's like we want to be a flash in the pan. Like we want to be able to get turnovers every single day. If we want to be able to get more takeaways than we did last year, we got to continue to preach it and try to get them every single day. No, I mean, he's been having a phenomenal camp, in my opinion. Uh two takeaways today. So, I mean, can't get no better than that. Um but he's a very mature guy. You know, I think he's a want to say he's like 25 or something like that. So, he's not a a young 21-year-old second-year player, 22. Um he's very mature. Um he obviously played in this defense all last year, started every single game. So, it's not like this is his first time learning anything. So, we've been helping out each other, honestly. I think me just bringing my experience and things I've seen around the league, but also as far as this defense has been good for me to have him because this isn't the same defense that I was in at Tennessee. So, we've been helping each other a lot, and it's been fun just getting our chemistry together. >> Kevin, what's distinct about the sports performance staff and how they manage you guys during camp from your previous experiences, maybe even in Tennessee, though I know Frank was there. >> Right. >> Um and obviously Philly and Chicago. What's different here? >> Um it's very similar to when I was in Tennessee cuz obviously I had Frank in Tennessee. me personally, cuz like I said, I can't speak for everybody, but I have a I'm very routine-based. Um I mean, I literally once I leave the building, I do all my recovery stuff. I literally go home, jump in a hyperbaric, and I jump in the bed and go to sleep. So, I I'm all about recovery for myself. I honestly try to stay out of the trainer room as much as I can cuz I'm always doing different things. Uh but no, I think they do a great job of guys that are injured, and if something happens on the field, they get them off the field and kind of bring them back. So, um but yeah, it's very similar as far as the strength staff, but I think these guys are first-class here. >> What's it been like getting a chance to play with Christian Barmore? >> Oh, I mean, it's funny. Christian Barmore is one of the funnier guys on the team. Uh we we actually have a Philly connection. He's from Philly, I'm from Philly. Uh no, he's fun. You know, I've always said that I feel like personally interior guys and interior defenders, interior pass rush is more valuable than any other position on the field, in my opinion. I think there's a lot of talk about edge rushers and how much they get paid or whatever may be, but at the end of the day, you can do a lot of things to those guys. You can chip, you can slide protect, you can do a lot of stuff, but when the guys that are closest to the ball, if they can get off the ball and affect the game, affect the pass, affect the run, those guys are the most valuable. So, from Barmore to Milton Williams, those are the two guys that set the tone for our defense. So, I'm excited to play with those guys. Oh, he's hilarious. Honestly, just uh we we have a lot of camaraderie in the locker room. He's one of the funnier guys on the team. Well, you know, you have certain guys on your team that are like you always look at it like I will always remember having a teammate just by his personality and just kind of who he is. He's one of those guys for sure. Yes. Yes. No, he's a baller. He's a guy that obviously is a young player was undrafted. And I think he was here a little bit last year, but seeing him in this training camp, he's learning. He's still learning, but at the end of the day he has the unique ability to take the ball away. And I think those are certain things that you truly can't coach. And I think he's really just taking advantage of every time opportunity that he gets. And I'm looking forward to him getting more opportunities and taking the ball away. It's like once you put it on film once or twice, that's who you are. You're a guy that takes the ball away. So, I'm excited to continue to watch him grow and make plays. I mean, I'd rather have a guy that you got to reel in than tell him to go. You know what I mean? Like I think you would want that from your own child. You know what I mean? So, it's like it's one of those deals where as a young player when you're out here trying to make a name for yourself, where you're undrafted and you're on practice squad and you have limited opportunities, like you want to be able to put something on tape where they'll be like, "Hey, who is this guy?" I'd rather, like I said, being in that position, I'd rather them have to tell me to chill because I want to get noticed somehow or some way. But I think he's been getting noticed by his play-making ability. And so, like I said, John's one of the guys that, you know, I kind of just look to him like, "Hey, bro, when you get out there, set the tone for the DBs. Set the tone for whether you're with the twos, the threes, or even if he's going to be with the ones. I don't know. You know what I mean? I think he's just a player that I'm excited to continue to watch grow. No, for sure. Absolutely. I I appreciate the compliment, but that's the that's the business we're in. As receivers, I just try to work on it Yeah, that's what it You got to be able to catch the ball. That's kind of like the the main thing for our position and uh obviously there's there's times where you you don't always make the catch, but you want to build that consistency where you feel comfortable in any situation to make that play. >> How was it going against the Eagles today and just kind of having someone else to compete rather than your own team? I don't know. I don't play defense. I think defense and like O-line D-line really be Yeah, they like really feel that. Uh as an offensive player like we have to run routes. Um it's obviously good to go against somebody else because they haven't seen the routes a million times like our defense has. so yeah, I guess it it's it's always good to go against somebody else and kind of feel that energy on the sideline where everybody's on the same side. Our defense is cheering us on. We're cheering the defense on. >> Offensively, considering how well you did kind of overall as as a group, could this be used kind of as a bit of a confidence boost for the group given how well you did given you know the Eagles were terrible a couple years ago? >> Um I wish that mattered. But none of it matters. It's the next day. It's a very what have you done for me recently league. Um I wish there was rollover minutes and rollover good plays that you could just pass on to the next year. Uh but all I can give us is like, "Hey, we we had a good day today." But that doesn't mean anything for tomorrow. You know, it doesn't mean we're going to come out and automatically have a good day, unfortunately. So you got to go back to work. You watch the tape. You find the good, the bad, the things that get you beat, and you just transfer it into the next day and start off with at zero. >> I'd rather have a good day than a bad >> I take good days over bad days for sure. unfortunately, they just don't roll over. I wish they did. >> What about Can you break down your outfit? Can you break down your outfit today, please? >> Yeah, same as always. the work shirt, everything can get sacrificed for the cause. Uh but yes, it's still same purpose. This is actually better cuz the material is better. It'll stay drier longer. Uh especially when it starts getting sweaty and hot. >> And how do you feel about all the wireless technology around you right now? >> Oh, the wireless technology? Oh, like you talking about like EMF and stuff? >> Does that affect you? >> I think it affects everything. How much it affects me, I don't know. I think there Isn't that what they're doing in the 49ers stadium? They're trying to figure something out. I don't know. I don't think it's that big of a deal, that's another conversation for another day, I guess. >> So, everybody talks about this the seven defense and that seven How is the consistency continue to to grow from the group? It seem like different guys are stepping up >> Yeah, I think uh I swear I'm being stepping in there. I'm sorry. Yeah, they uh it's good to see that that competition though. Uh it's good to see the competition between the whole group cuz it makes everybody better. which I you know, my whole time in the league I've wanted that. That's the only way you can all get better. When when the group is so separate like you got one guy that's just makes all the plays and everybody else just kind of sits around. That not only makes the group below, but it makes the the one guy not not work as hard. Um so, it's great to see everybody making plays and continue to compete >> What is the meaning behind the brick name? >> Oh, that's just a nickname the guys give me. Um I don't know if it's building brick by brick or what. We just go to work No, that's just what they call me. >> Is it due to mechanics maybe? >> The shirt kind of is more mechanics-y, but I got my own mechanics like full fit. >> know? Yeah. >> I don't know. That's what the boys call me, so I'll take it. Yeah. >> What was the message maybe from Vrabel at the end? Just sort of How How did he sum up the day when he addressed the >> Um just go just, you know, whether it was a good day, bad day, whatever we're going to go and watch the tape, see how it is, and then tomorrow's a whole new new day. It's not like I was saying earlier, you can't roll over the the practice like, "Oh, you you ended a two-minute with a made field goal and you I guess you won the two-minute. Well, that doesn't mean you're going to come out first period tomorrow and get bonus points or go start in first and eight. You start first and 10 and line it up the same way. >> Mack, you spent a lot of time with Tommy. >> Yep. >> How have you just seen him grow from last year to this year and how have you sort of been able to build your chemistry with him? >> Yeah, it's been cool to to work with Tommy, great dude. and he's continued to to grow not only as a player but just off the field as well, just like just like one of the guys. Um understanding all his teammates, especially as a quarterback you have to spend the time with guys to really get to know them and he's he's done that and it's been cool to cool to watch. >> For you as a receiver, do you have to sort of tailor your routes to Tommy compared to Drake or are there different things that maybe Drake likes that Tommy doesn't vice versa or are they just sort of the same thing in the end? >> Uh not really. At this caliber, the quarterbacks you know are know where the ball is supposed to put. Like when I was young, I was told I'd write my book, quarterbacks publish it. So, I better put my stuff where it needs to be and the quarterbacks will take care of the rest. >> Mack, is there any extra meaning to you in this week's joint practices against a former team first one last week against just the Colts? >> Nah, it's just the Eagles the same as just the Colts same as once I'm off a team then I don't I don't know I guess I don't have a grudge against the team, they didn't do nothing to me. >> Let's take two more. >> Mack, it seems like in those one-minute drills we see you kind of on that deep end a lot. Uh is there something about that route that works for you that you like or >> Um I don't know if it's cuz of my big body. Um I'll go in there and be be okay with catching the ball in I'm not sure. I I just run the routes and I think I yeah, it it so happens that I get those. Um but shoot, I'll I'll run whatever. >> Do you have a favorite route? >> The one that hey yeah, the one the ball come to me. That's my favorite one. >> One thing on those deep routes we see you give a little bit of shake at the top. I don't always see that. Is that something you picked up from somewhere or have you always done >> Um it just goes along with the shirt, really. Nah, I'm messing with you. No, I think it's just something that you have to craft in certain certain times. sometimes you need it, sometimes you don't. Uh, so I try to just build as a receiver you try to put a little flavor vanilla's not always going to work. You know? Appreciate it, y'all. >> Thanks, bud. Thanks, bud.

title: Mike Vrabel: "This Will Be a Really Good Measuring Stick Just to See Where We are At."
text: Hi, how are you Karen? >> Good. >> Um, how much of a a measuring stick, you know, given where you're at training camp will these two practices be >> Well, I mean, I think they'll be Yeah, I mean, I think that this is uh intentional. This is a very good football team, has been for, you know, quite some time. Uh, really good at the line of scrimmage, you know, big physical lines of scrimmage. Um certainly an excellent quarterback. They're well coached. Um good defensive scheme. So I think this will be a really good measuring stick just to see how we, you know, where we're at at this point in camp and how we can respond. There's going to be some good plays and we're going to have to, you know, make some adjustments really quickly. Uh and then try to keep our competitive stamina throughout the day. [clears throat and cough] >> How do you regulate? It'll be emotional out there. Things >> staying under control, right? the same way we always try to, you know, that, you know, we have to play a certain style and so do they and we have to get back to the huddle and we have to figure out what our job is for the next play and not spend a whole bunch of time um you know in side bars and side actions and you know try to play to the whistle and then get back to the huddle and that's what we want to do. That's how we want to play the football game. That's how we have to practice the game. Do you expect these two days to be uh emotional or uh whatever for AJ Brown specifically? >> I mean Mil played there, AJ played there. I mean, I think these guys are professionals and you know, they've shown that they want to practice for us and um you know, I'm sure there's some added uh feelings for them, but I'm not going to try to explain what those are. Those are their their feelings and again they're part of our team. We're really excited to have both of those guys and you know they've they've practiced hard whether it was against us or against the Colts or sure we'll see great great efforts from both of them today against the Eagles. >> You guys had great >> well three you know I mean started every game for three years. He's played interior offensive line is something we, you know, we're, you know, after the game coming out of here where we needed to to strengthen that and proven player. Um, you know, and somebody that I think has got experience in what we do and a terminology, you know, from Josh a few years ago and then and then Dabes the last couple years. So, you know, somebody that we felt like that could help us. >> You spoke the other day about evaluating the run game. Uh how important are these joint practices in kind of live action compared to even some of the preseason games? Is this as a chance to >> I mean I think we'll see a little bit more. There'll be different you know run defenses or run pressures or you know what we'll have to see today may be different than the game. Um but I think we also have to be smart. We have to be able to run our offense and if it's you know a bunch of guys up there then we won't. But, you know, traditionally, you know, Philly and Vick's defense, these guys are really good at the line of scrimmage. They're they're they're great with their technique and the way that they play blocks and the way that they shed and uh the way that the secondary comes in and supports. So, it it will be a a good test. This is not normally a defense that that gives up a whole lot of yards in a run game. Mil this off. >> Um I think that Milt just is continuing to be comfortable and um you know he's um you know I think yes I think he has. It's just, you know, in his own way and how he uh reaches people, but also by being out there every day and the way that he practices and his tempo and his energy, I think, you know, can be uh somewhat contagious and his ability to to chase plays. We talked about that so many times last year when when you'd look and, you know, unfortunately it's a 20-yard game, but it's it's Milt, you know, making a big hit uh chasing the ball. uh whether that be in New Orleans or Tennessee and you know those things I think can be infectious uh to the defense. >> Mike, you mentioned um you know Philly being good for a good number of years now. Is there something you've come to maybe from afar like a f admire about what they built or just kind of what's your impression of what what they've done these past years? >> Well, sustained success in the National Football League is tough. It's difficult. We know that the system's not set up uh for that. And uh I think they've drafted well. They've retained their players and they found a quarterback that they want to you know, a franchise quarterback. And you know, I think that that's that's a good place to start. And uh you know, when you can draft well and you can develop players and and get them resigned um and then find a quarterback that that leads your football team, um that's a good place to start. >> What have you seen from No. So, we're not deferred to him. [snorts] >> Don't be nice though. >> Entire team. Um, can you explain the reason behind that? Why you decided to kind of have it be right there in the middle of the watching? >> Well, I think just trying to put some of these guys into positions to uh to compete in front of their teammates. I think that's um always critical as a young player is is being able to go out there and and compete and and and do that in front of, you know, the veteran players, you know, that have been there. And I go back to, you know, 1997 and covering a kickoff and having guys like Dmani Dawson and Leavon Kirkland and Greg Lloyd um you know, say, "Hey, that that that's a hell of a job." And and how that made me feel at the time. And so I try to explain to our veteran players the impact that they can have whether that's in games that they're not playing in or at practice or when a player's uh in a competitive situation and whether you support him or find ways to to encourage him. I think that's important. >> Seen what AJ can do on the field. What have you seen from in the building in terms of leadership since he's been here? I just it's funny just not being around him or you know dayto day u for you know whatever years it was from Tennessee to Philly and now here um just a maturity and overall maturity uh the way that he uh communicates with coaches way he communicates with players uh it you know just I would say an overall maturity so he's uh he's accountable he you know gets mistakes corrected I mean you can coach them hard Todd can coach him hard. Josh can coach him hard. Um, you know, he wants to do well for for the entire offense and he and he wants to be a contributor. >> Where where are Landry and Skoo [snorts] and week one? Time table was on, but we haven't seen them at all here in the summer. >> Where are They're here. Uh, they're rehabbing. Uh, they're they're working through the return to play and you know where they are for week one. They won't be out there today. So that that's the only update I can give you. They won't play in the game this week and I think they're just continuing to work to try to get there and when they get there, you know, obviously they'll be there. >> Any other guys we shouldn't expect to see uh in these physical practices? >> Practice is physical. I don't know why, you know, I mean, again, we I hope we practice physical whether the Eagles here or the Patriots are here. Um, but it would be the same group of people. I think Gonzo won't be available today. Kyle Dixon, Riley Wilson. Um, Bar will do some third down stuff, some pass rush stuff as he's working his way back, try to limit some of his reps. Ellis may be limited in some of his reps. Ben Brown obviously, so there'll be a few guys. Mike uh two joint practice plus two preseason game in the next 90 days span. Um how do you manage uh the starters um competitive um uh chance and also managing their workload? Do you plan it like as a whole or just to evaluate day by day? I >> I think the biggest thing is to be able to to be flexible and adjust day by day to see where that is. But I know today will be a lot of good work and then we'll see, you know, where we are when we get into the red zone tomorrow. uh and then you know have to make a decision what that looks like for the game and and all those things. So you know we we have a a plan for today and then we'll see what that looks like and see how much work guys get and then we'll go from there. >> Mike, going back to training camp fights, um what is your messaging to your team now that you're going into a joint practice about training camp fights and what is your message specifically about? >> I mean I've been through this. It's hasn't changed, you know what I mean? We're we're we have to practice a certain way. We have to be able to control our emotions. We we try to ask them to go to the line and and play a certain style and try to create an identity and, you know, have to be able to come back and and and be involved. I get it. It's emotional. We can say it's football. You know, fighting isn't football. Fighting gets you thrown out of a game. Um we we've seen that before. Uh that happens. they're not afraid to to call in um you know from New York. They've changed the rule this year. So even if an official misses a a flag or misses a punch um and New York happens to see it, you know, that player can be removed from the football game. So we know how critical each and every player is for the for the team on on on game day. You know, we don't have that many spots. There's guys that play, you know, they start here, but they're backups at other positions. So if you lose those players, uh ultimately that hurts the team. So we we would try not to do anything like that. >> The change of the rule though, there seems to be a fighting still. As a former player, why do you think it keeps happening? >> Well, I mean, we have emotional competitive grown adult football players and you know that's sometimes happen and uh try to get it fixed as quickly as possible and and get on. We got to we got to practice here. Do you like the way that Andy Barales has responded this week after his performance last Thursday? >> Yeah, I think so. And again, we we I I don't want to make excuses. Um but, you know, we were trying to take a look at at another snapper. You know, Andy was was dealing with something, so we felt like it'd be a good opportunity to take a look at another snapper. And you just understand how critical that operation is, the the the snap, the laces, the all the other things. And yes, we have to make them. But I felt like, you know, to Andy's credit, he had a great day in front of the team and uh and was able to make the one there at the end um at the, you know, after the two-minute. >> Mike, uh last question. I've been asking coaches around the league for their favorite drill. So, uh does one come to mind for you? And if so, what makes it kind of your preference? Uh >> favorite drill. I mean, I like, you know, we try to do an open field tackling drill. We try to just focus on, you know, guys being able to beat people in space. We talk, we focus on guys being able to to create good angles with the ball carrier, coming to balance, not going off the diving board. You know, we were terrible in Miami last year. You guys all know, you guys all reported on it, and we worked hard to improve it. and just how critical and there's so many great athletes in this league with the football and and miss tackles just end up leading to X plays. title: Drake Maye dominates and winners and losers from Eagles joint practice Day
text: Okay, from the steamy practice fields outside of Gillette Stadium, I have cooled off a little bit, simmered to use a word, our next guest with love because he tells this to our pal Mike Reese basically every day to get that pep out of his step to stop skipping around, smiling so much and dropping Richard Mark's references. title: Patriots Knock Out Eagles on Day 1 of Joint Practices | 2 minutes at Training Camp
text: Okay, if you wanted the joint practice between the Patriots and Eagles to be a boxing match, let me tell you, we wouldn't have had a second day.  This was a knockout, a KO by the Patriots.  If they're keeping track, how do they know? How about this?  The Patriots won all four two- minute drills.  Drake May advances, sets up a field goal attempt, and makes it. Jalen Hurts reaches midfield, stalls, and the clock runs out.  Tommy DeVito and the Patriots' offensive backups advance, kick a field goal, and in that final two-minute drill, Kendall Vildor gets not the first, not the second, not the third, not the fourth, but the fifth interception of the day for the Patriots.  Now, it wasn't perfect, but let's get back to Drake May.  It was almost perfect.  15 of 18 with one sack in 11-on-11 sessions. Four receptions for A.J.  Brown, including the play of the day: a leaping catch after a desperate pass from May under pressure, the catch over Rick Woolen, touches with both feet inbounds, the referees present today call reception and the crowd goes wild.  Incidentally, perhaps the loudest crowd I've ever heard at a Patriots joint practice , and they had plenty of reasons to be loud, including the running game.  Rhamondre Hall Stevenson is clearly the RB1 here during practice, initiating periods in the two-minute drill, and is making long runs between Will Campbell and Alijah Vera-Tucker on the left side.  The best day the running game has had in camp, which is shocking considering the Eagles have Jalen Carter, the highest-paid defensive tackle in football, and Jordan Davis.  Another note on the offense, which had good days from Garrett Wilson and Michael Carter, who finished 2-0 in 1-on-1 passing duels.  The rhythm became present.  Drake May's first complete pass is to Demario Douglas on a cross-path.  They hurry. Gain 20 yards and quickly return to the line, without regrouping. So, the things you've been talking about, the things we've told you here on the podcast, are reflected in the second-to-last practice of the summer in terms of training camp, and the most important one of the summer so far.  Now, defensively, we mention the five turnovers.  Something very important .  Three of them were in seven-on-seven drills, but the fact that they shut out the Eagles in both two-minute drills is a great sign for them.  And they started with some blitzes.  The same defense that we saw pressuring hard in the AFC Championship and the Super Bowl did it again today, looking to solidify itself in the second year of this defense, even without Christian Gonzalez, who is still absent.  It's been a week and a half since Gonzalez last practiced, but in his place, Marcus Jones managed an interception. Vildor, whom we mentioned, and John Saunders Jr., the backup safety, are moving up the ranks, and if he were to reach the top, who would he find there?  Craig Woodson, who got two interceptions today. Now, reasons for concern: the edge wasn't so good in defense against the run.  The Eagles controlled the line of scrimmage early on in the 11-on-11. We already saw that containing the rim was a problem against the Colts.  I'm sure it's something Mike Vrabel will insist on tomorrow.  And then, depth.  As much as we talk about the starters putting up blow after blow against the Eagles, the backups, whether in individual drills or in 11- on-11, lost most of those plays against the Eagles.  So we don't have one of the most talented squads in the league.  But as far as the headlines go, the Patriots showed exactly why they are considered contenders again at the start of the season.  Now they head into the second day, which will have a much greater focus on the red zone.  You can bet there will be many more fights.  Today we had one, Jalen Carter threw a punch, but he was still able to stay in.  And, of course , we'll have much more to report from Foxboro.
