title: Bauer Sharp, Jake Browning & more on Preseason Approach | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Anyone want to start? >> Coming into a new season, how does your routine does it change at all or do you keep it relatively the same in this season? >> I try to keep everything the same. I've always been very routine guy over the past eight seasons kind of building it up and so yeah everything basically ever since I got to Tampa it's just been the same routine and um there's little tweaks I need to do here and there then I'll work on that but yeah to answer your question yeah try to keep everything the same. >> With the with a new coordinator with Danny here now does it change things up for you or is it essentially the same job for you and just lots of changing around you? >> Yeah it's my my third coordinator here at the Bucs so it's just like anything it's just a new relationship we have to build trust build that foundation and go on from there. >> What is that relationship like with him? >> It's been good it's been kind of he's played he's coached for 30 some some odd years so he brings a lot of experience and professionalism to the table so it's been a great back and forth figuring out what each other what each other wants expects needs to to have success on the field and ultimately that's what it's all about is is winning and making kicks and and moving on to the next one. >> How unique of a guy is he he just seems like he's just a coach like you never really see in the NFL he's just very unique guy. >> Yeah very energetic guy he keeps everyone's attention in the meetings and yeah like I said it's it's just been great to build that trust with him and build that relationship. >> Got any new material this year in the dad joke department? >> ha ha ha um why can't you trust stairs? Cuz they're always up to something. Thanks not everyone at once don't laugh at once. >> Keep me going. >> yep >> Do you have anything in this off season that you were specifically working on training with anybody? >> Nope like like what I said I just kind of try to keep everything the same um it's been going pretty well been feeling confident and kicking it well out there so just try to keep it all the same. >> Chase you're going into the last year of your contract is any chance or any talk of of getting an extension before the season or is that a wait? >> Yeah, I mean, it's I think that's something anyone on the field would like to have done is get a good extension early. So, um obviously we saw the Steelers, the Cowboys, and the Texans all get something done, which was really cool. I'm very happy for all three of those guys. They They deserve it. And I think it's really cool to see the league moving that direction in that like everyone knows points are at a premium in this league and and I think across the league we're seeing that kickers are being seen more as an asset than an afterthought. Um I think those three examples this offseason were great to see. So, um very happy for them and and uh yeah. >> For I mean, for you, I think you have to like some other guys in this roster have to like the stability of being in the same city for a couple years now and and settling into the team and the city. >> Yeah, no, it's been great to be be here in Tampa for going on my gosh, fourth year now. So, uh that's been wonderful. So, yeah, excited to see what the future holds, wherever that may be. >> Are you more surprised given your performance than Adam Vinatieri? >> Yeah, I mean, at the end of the day it's a business. So, um they can offer me if they want. If not, then we move on and play the season and do as well as we can. So, um my opinion or my feelings about it don't really matter. Um at the end of the day it's I'm signed for a contract for this season. I'm going to do that and uh hopefully perform well and see what happens after that. >> Your accuracy's been great throughout this year and last week with the 50-yard plus field goals, do you think the biggest change has been the biggest that that change or more willing to go for those 50-plus you can stick the yard field goals now? >> Yeah, I think we've seen a a change across the league now starting to trust guys, let them have it. Uh let them have opportunities for it. So, it actually started um back when I was with the Colts the first time at the end of 2019. I I I was able to lucky luckily lucky to come in after Adam Vinatieri. And he was actually the one who gave the advice. He said, "Hey, look, start kicking longer kicks in practice because if they see it in practice, they're going to trust it in the game, so ever since then I tried to apply it to to my practices and and and Todd's been great to give me the chances to hit those long ones. >> Thank you. >> Thanks guys. >> We saw you you know in New York, New Jersey you put your back into it at the end. What what happened there and how do you feel now? >> Yeah, I just had back tighten up on me on a on a roll out pass like kind of went to pump and felt the tighten. You know, I don't think it's like a long-term thing at all. Felt good today. Felt like I probably could have probably could have played in the game and was kind of told like hey, you weren't going to play very much, you know, to begin with, so we're just going to rest you and you know, kind of easy back in and so yeah, feel good. I'm excited to play this week. And uh you know, glad it wasn't a a long-term thing. >> Jake, there's an assumption of your experience that you're the guy the backup guy that coach Bowls said that the competition is open. Obviously Jalen played real well week one. Do you feel pressure that this is a true competition for the backup job? >> I mean, I think anytime you're in the you're in the NFL and and uh you know, if you think you're above any competition, you're you're in the wrong business and so welcome any competition and uh feel pretty confident that I've been playing playing uh really well this camp. You know, had the back thing pop up and uh you know, really before that felt like I was playing really well and then um you know, since coming back feel like I kind of picked up right where I left off. Uh but yeah, JD JD played well and um you know, Bayless is a really good player, too. And so we got a good room. You know, I'm not I'm not shying away from any competition and you know, bring it. >> You're uh set to play in this preseason game on Saturday, I think the first one this What do you kind of look to do when you get in a preseason game? Like what are some of your goals for You just want to get the mental reps under or is there anything else you're doing? >> I mean, I think it's playing you know, you're playing playing a game and um you know, I think I think you just try to operate the offense well, just like you would in, you know, a week three game of the regular season. And so uh yeah, I think anytime you get to play, you're excited for it and uh yeah, I don't think you treat it any different. You know, I think maybe if you're a 10-year vet that's started, you know, over 100 games, maybe you're looking at it a little different, but for me, I'm just want to go in, play with good feet, good eyes, operate the offense well, move the ball down the field, make the right reads and um you know, that's kind of where my mind's at. >> How do you feel about Daniels? Obviously super talented, but a lot of really really great energy as well. What does he brought to this quarterback room? Has he taught you anything? >> Uh yeah, a lot of energy. Um which I think is good. Like I think he's anytime a guy brings a a ton of energy to the meeting room is is nice. Um you know, I still think it's it's Baker's room to run and all that and I think JD's had a good kind of awareness of of when to when to go and all that. Um yeah, I think he's done a good job. Um and as far as like, you know, I think learning about NIL was kind of interesting. Uh it's like, damn, all right. Uh but yeah, uh he's brought good energy. I enjoyed having him around and um you know, like I said, he's been playing well, but uh you know, I'm kind of focused on how I'm playing and and myself. >> You've played with a lot of good young receivers throughout this league, but um what do you make of Ted Washington? >> Yeah, I think Ted's done a good job. Um you know, for such a tall like longer receiver, like he's pretty twitchy at the top of routes, which is uh pretty deadly deadly combo and um yeah, I think the main thing I've seen with like a lot of younger, really good receivers is that first training camp is like survival. Like you're just not it's a different you can go through as many you know, fall camps in college as you want. It's just going to be different. And so uh you know, there's a little bit of someday you know, there's going to be ups and downs and um you know, I I remember like Justin Jefferson was kind of like that in in Minnesota too and then all of a sudden you know, we threw him out there to start week two and just played insanely well and you're like, "Whoa, where did that where did that come from?" And so uh you know, I think Ted's got a chance to be a really good receiver and I think the main thing for him is obviously got the talent and all that is just you know, stacking days and continuing to get better, but you definitely see flashes where you're like, "Okay, that's that's legit and and uh and a rare talent." >> Jake, I wanted to ask you is there any similarities between Baker and Joe Burrow on the field but also off the field? >> I'd say they're pretty different. yeah, I would say they're pretty different, but you know, both go about their their business the right way. You guys are loving that weed whacker in the background. >> [laughter] yeah, there I mean there's some similarities just in like the preparation side and all that, but uh personality-wise I'd say they're pretty different. >> You're also learning the background of the offense. How are you feeling about it now maybe in comparison to other offenses you've been on? What are the biggest things that you notice? >> Yeah, I think I mean Zay does a great job. I feel like the offense is um a decent amount of plays where you just with how we're able to run the ball and uh and kind of build a pass game on first and second down around that um I mean there's a decent amount of times where you just do a play fake and you know, number one's wide open and you're like, "It's pretty nice." and so I think that it's a new offense and then just like new personnel too. And so um you know, it's kind of learning that and and seeing what people like. I think there's always going to be some similarities just once you start getting into drop back. Like there's only so many different things you can do. But you know, I think Z Rob's done a great job. You know, T.J. and Chandler have done a good job, too. And so uh Yeah, I mean I like the offense a lot so far. >> Jake, you were clicking really quickly with Tezz Johnson right off the bat. Can you tell us a little about Tezz and his play and just how that was clicking really for you guys? >> Yeah, I think like it was ironically OTAs like he just he's so explosive. Like he gets out of his routes. Like he just puts his foot in the ground and goes. And so OTAs was just like, you know, I've I've played with like some athletic receivers and stuff, but I don't know if it's like he's so light he just gets out of it so fast or what, but um I was kind of behind him and so you know, that was kind of a point of emphasis for me of OTAs like just from phase two to phase three like, okay, like you do have to like get ahead sorry, to get ahead of the uh of him like especially on outbreakers was kind of where it was mostly shown up. And um so it was good to see that kind of show up early on in training camp and going to war with this fly. and uh Yeah, and then unfortunately he's had to miss a few practices and stuff like that, but um I'm excited to get him back out there. I think he's pretty electric and you know, he just moves at a different speed. >> How important is the preseason knowing that how important is the preseason knowing that you're the backup and if everything goes well with Baker he plays all 17 games and this is really your only potential game action? >> Yeah, I think uh I think anytime you're you're playing whether it's in season or uh my guy uh in season uh regular season or preseason or anything like that, you're building a resume. and so you know, you got to prepare and all that uh for for your opportunities to play. Um I try not to overthink like uh might play, I might not. Like I've I've been backup for a while. Like it's just kind of the you get used to it a little bit where it's like, you know, that that is the job. Nobody knows if you're prepared or anything like that until you get thrown in there. And so, um you know, trying not to really overthink that too much. It's just Yeah, I kind of have my routine that I I prepare and and uh you know, and then once you get on the field you just feel that confidence in that preparation and just let it rip. >> Do you feel a sense of urgency for for this week in particular to get out there and play well? >> I mean, I'm excited to. Yeah. I think uh you know, like I said, if you're if you're building your resume, you know, for us what we put on tape is our resume and um you know, I think that's an opportunity to go play whether it's week one, week two, week 15, whenever it is, you know, I think it's always exciting to go play some live football. >> Jake, obviously the wide out room is led by former Husky K.J. But what can you say about about our Sharp and the progress he's made? >> Yeah, I think Bowers has done a good job. Um he had a he had a good play today. Um like a crossing route and um you know, you can tell he studies it, knows what's going on, and then, you know, in the times that his number hasn't been called he's been able to uh you know, make the plays when they're there and uh you know, I think one of the things is when you're not getting like as many reps as maybe you're used to in college, you know, you get you get your reps and all of a sudden you want to make the crazy play and kind of the the harder thing to do is just make the the consistent play. I think Bowers has done a good job of that. Um you know, as far as run game and stuff like that, you'd have to ask somebody else, but he's looked great in the pass game. >> Thank you. Thanks, Jake. >> Thanks, guys. >> Good. Good. Good. >> Questions for Bowers Sharp? >> Bowers, what was it like to finally just what it was like to be able to take all the stuff you've learned this summer and then kind of put it out on the field and with how that went for you. >> Yeah, obviously that was my first NFL um experience my the game. Um it was super fun. I'm super blessed. You know, all the work that I've put in since last year has kind of been an ongoing train. Um I love it. I love the guys that I you know, you get to go do it with and in these leaders here. So, it was a super fun experience. >> What was some feedback maybe from your coaches about your performance tonight, first game? >> Yeah, just uh, you know, focus on little things. That's what football's all about, right? You know, and so as a rookie, I got to focus on little things just just uh, take my game to the next level for in the future, but I'm just kind of focus on day by day. Take the coaching, the notes that they gave me for the game, you know, and so we'll just move on to the next game with this upcoming one on Saturday. >> About what Jake was just up here kind of talking about, you know, consistently making plays with the opportunities that you've had. What can you say about, you know, just each snap you get, each target, how you're going to make the most of it? >> That's just kind of my mindset ever since I stepped on the field, you know, just make the most of your opportunity, right? And so, that's what it's about. I try to do the best I can for this team, for my teammates, for the guys, and obviously um, for for Baker, you know, or with Jake, you know, whichever whichever one. If I'm with the twos, but you know, I love it, you know, I just I do what I can for those guys when the ball comes my way, for sure. >> How was the the blocking end of it going? You had to go against David somebody like that. >> Yeah, for sure. It's an awesome match up. They made me work. I feel like they get me better, I get them better. You know, we go at it practice every day and and you know, we compete. It was a super fun time. >> It's hard to watch you on Friday. I mean, obviously the tight ends have a ton of motion for each snap in this direction or that. How much more complex is the blocking than what you learned in college? >> Yeah, I would say last year my OC Joe Sloan prepared me very well, you know, for this next level, you know. We were the most motioning position in our offense last year. I've gotten used to that, so coming here, obviously it's an NFL playbook. It's pretty complex. We motion a lot, but you know, you kind of get used to it. You just execute the way, you know, you had to execute. >> We talked to Jack Flaherty the other day. You guys both came over from LSU. What is y'all's relationship like and how's it been having a friendly face to make this transition? >> I mean, it's awesome, you know, we spent every day together last year at LSU. We're boys. It was a little make makes it a little more comfortable coming in here. Seeing each other, you know, go chase the dream that we've always wanted. And it's awesome, you know, his performance last game. It was it was super cool to see that. I was right on the field just celebrating with him. So, it was it's pretty good. >> Going to three different schools before the NFL and having to learn those different systems, does that help you kind of pick up this offense quicker? Obviously, it's more complex, but just the ability to pick things up. >> Yeah, I would just say you know, learning learning the playbook as a quarterback my freshman year kind of set me up for the future I would say. I tell that to everyone. You know, and the guy that taught me that offense as a QB just kind of set me up I would say that is I give credit to that, but obviously, you know, I've I've spent a lot of time around a lot of playbooks and a lot of coaches. And so, that I take part in that as well. >> Jack told us the other day that he got off social media and it's done wonders for him. Are you following him in that regard? >> Yeah, I take breaks social media when I feel like the time is needed. You know, obviously, we're in camp. We're just focused on day by day and ball. So, I try to, you know, keep my distance a little bit. But he's doing him. I like it. >> What's Baker What's Baker been like? I'm sure you know you've seen him on TV this that, but he's your quarterback. What can you tell us about him? >> He's as advertised. You know, he I mean, he he's freaking full of energy. There's not a day he doesn't bring it. I mean, he's just a contagious leader. You know, he everyone wants to rally around him and fight for him and do the best we can, you know, to help lead this offense behind him for sure. >> Last few plays like, you know, he likes to mess with receivers or anybody. >> You said what? >> Does Does Baker kind of challenge you at all as with you all? >> Yeah, I mean, I can't I can't specifics, but like I'm a rookie, you know, he's going to give me some some crap here and there. It's all fun and games though for sure. >> What have you learned about yourself in camp? >> Um nothing that I didn't know. I'd say that. You know, I'm just put my head down and I work every day no matter the circumstance. That's just kind of my my motto, my mindset with whatever's thrown my way. >> Last one for Logan Thomas. Now we're going into this second game, what are you looking to improve on from the first game specifically? >> Yeah. I would just say nothing really specific, but just when it comes to little details, maybe your alignment, uh maybe maybe your route depth, maybe, you know, something you're working with the receiver and something maybe working with the tackle, but just those little things that can, you know, up the game by, you know, that much level. That's what it football is, so. >> All right, that's all for Barr. Thank you, guys. >> Appreciate it. Yeah, thank you. >> Thank you, guys.

title: Rashad Wisdom & DeMonte Capehart on Team Execution | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Hello everyone. >> Hi. >> How are you guys doing? >> Good, how are you? >> I'm doing well, thank you. >> Questions? >> How has camp been for you just overall and everything? >> Camp has been really good. Um, you know I mean the guys have been flying around. Uh, we're taking a good approach to all the new installs and stuff that are coming in. Guys are learning quickly, so um I feel like camp has been going pretty well so far. You know I mean looking forward to this next preseason game coming up, so that'll be fun. >> In terms of how much you You have a sense of how much you want to play? Every Everybody has different expectations going into these games. Just Just for you, is it just as much as possible for you? >> Yeah, pretty much. I mean, you know I mean I think the whole approach for me is always stay ready so you don't have to get ready. Um, I feel like a guy like me, I'm plug-and-play. You know I mean I can fit in wherever wherever's needed. Um, you know whether that's anywhere in the secondary, special teams-wise, you know I mean I can do all four phases, so um that's pretty much the biggest thing, you know I mean to stay in healthy, stay in shape, and uh being ready when my number's called. >> What have you been working on personally throughout training camp? >> Um, I think the biggest thing with me is my eyes. Um, eye discipline I feel like as a DB, uh that's probably one of the most important things to have. Um, your eyes will take you to exactly to right to where you're supposed to be uh play-wise. And and really just like my post work, really reading the quarterbacks, their mannerisms, uh you know I mean all the way from the start of the snap, you know I mean you get a you get a jump on those guys of how their snap cadences goes, when you can get out of your disguise, when you shouldn't, when you should hold a little bit longer, and then just being in the post, you know I mean reading their their shoulders, where they're looking, and trying to figure out and get a feel for uh my my angle whenever I need ever need when it when it when it's time to make a break. So, I feel like that's the two biggest things I've really been working on, man. And after that, it's just just being free, trying to be me and go out there and just play ball, go have fun with it, too. >> Have there been some guys you like going against throughout camp >> Huh. Uh I love going against my guy Tuck, uh Sean Tucker. Um you know what I mean, seeing him in the hole. Um I would say two at receiver. I think Ted Ted has been phenomenal, you know what I mean, and he he brings it not only in the pass game, but in the run game, too, you know what I mean, he'll come and try to block you for real, so um it's been it's been nice to see him out there. Um and then I think just on the field wise, too, um I know I I kind of went up against him today, but Miles Killebrew, like really looking forward to seeing him go out there. Um he's he's a beast on special teams, man. I seen it firsthand today, just kind of how he approaches that side of the game, so um just there's a lot of good things going on all around the around all around the team with the guys, but you know what I mean, I think I think everything's looking looking really good right now. >> Are you close with Sean or Sean Tucker? You >> Yeah. I'm pretty I'm pretty cool with everyone on the team. Uh there's there's not too many people's names I don't know. Um so I mean I'm pretty good with everyone on the team, but yeah, I like I like to mess with Tuck a lot, for sure. You know what I mean, I like to poke at him a little bit, but it's all it's all fun and games, you know what I mean, like we just like to have fun with it, so. >> Okay, so apparently he he told me this last year, he cuts hair. He was like >> Does he? >> teammates' hair in college. Did he tell you this? >> No, but he >> would you let him >> No, definitely not. He's definitely not. He's not coming anywhere close to my hair. >> So you controlled him on this one. >> I will. I definitely will. I wonder if he cuts his own hair now. I'm going to start paying attention to that, too. >> What did Jerry Smith have to say about your special teams uh on the first time out? >> Pretty much that we did a good job. Um I think, you know, a couple times we we ourselves in the foot, but um you know, it's all correctable stuff. It's nothing major. Um Just minor tweaks here and there, but overall did a really good job and you know, I mean just got to keep building on that, but you know, I mean I think sky's the limit for us in that phase of the game and I think with the guys that we have on the field and just the coach that coach Smith is, I think, you know, I mean we could be one of the better special teams in the in the league. >> Do you admire coach Smith? >> Yeah, he's he he brings the energy every day like he he's the same guy on and off the field. I know y'all seen him with the 10 pieces of gum on the sideline. Like that's that's who he is, man, like through and through. But he brings a great energy. You can tell like he lives and breathes special teams and that's the type of guy I feel like you want to have around for that type of phase, you know, I mean you can pick his brain about everything and the thing I feel like I've been noticing in his means is just that whenever he breaks something down like he always has an answer for something that somebody might do, you know, I mean and I really I really admire that, you know, I mean like it's it's like a chess game, you know, I mean like you got to think three steps ahead and you can tell just with his experience and how long he's been around that he everything is very intentional. So, you can really learn a lot from a guy like that. >> Is it hard to understand him sometimes when >> Nah, not at all. You know, I mean I think you get kind of get a sense for the way he speaks, you know, I mean he has he has a he has a little bit of an accent, but nah, not at all, man. It's coach coach Smith is one of the easier guys to understand for sure. >> Can you give us an impression? >> No, I can't. I can't. >> [laughter] >> All right, thank you guys. >> Appreciate it. Y'all have a good one. >> How you doing? >> All right, guys, questions for Demontae? >> Demontae, how did that uh first preseason game go for you? How do you feel like you played? >> Uh it was fun. Uh just, you know, dream come true. Uh first preseason game, it was the jitters, getting the jitters out. Uh I think also just uh just taking what I've learned from practice to the game. Actually being able to go do what I'm good at, you know? >> What was your uh feedback from your coaches for your performance? >> Uh just be more productive. Um just got to make plays, got to go be a guy. You know what I'm saying? So. >> Did everything feel good after the recovery on the wrist and >> Yeah, it actually felt pretty good. So, that's what I was nervous about, but once I struck I was, you know, all settled in and was good to go. >> Obviously you learn the defense, you get comfortable in the defense, but physically where do you think you've made the most progress since start of rookie camp OTA? >> Uh it's a lot of I mean it's it's challenging, but it's also that's what you it's what you're here for, so I just, you know, I take it, you know, once I mess up I take it with a grain of salt. You got to move to the next play. And you I think you learn better that way when you take things with a grain of salt and attack the next play. >> Coach Marcus Washington and that coach here, you know, you got to work with him extensively. What are some of the things the biggest things that you've learned from him and how's working with him? >> Uh he teach you he he teach you fundamentals. He's going to get the fundamental details down packed, so you know what you're doing when it's when that moment comes. That's his big that's his biggest thing and that's what he harps on. >> Captain. Who's been hands-on with you in that room? And you got Nacho in there. You know, Pita Bella is not participating, but we've seen him be hands-on with you, but how's that been like having that veteran leadership? >> Uh it's I think it's just a whole room. We all helping each other. We all want each other each other to succeed. Um nobody's bigger than nobody. The the the the weakest link we we we try to help everybody, you know, so because we all in it together. Nobody's alone in it, so we just that's how we attack every day. >> What do you think the biggest adjustment has been for you in training camp playing in a game? biggest adjustment. Basically trying to also trying to be the quarterback of the defense like trying to learn it that way so you you know it like just like a linebacker. >> Do you want to tell us if there's somebody in that D-line room that you think you're closest to in terms of size, strength, skill set that matches your game or you know? or you like lucky to be here? >> Uh I say Elijah Simmons. We got a similar game. Uh you know, his he's he's been here in the system, so he's know he knows and I've been also taking his tips and learning from him greatly. Uh Vita, you know, also learn from him, but Pitts, I see him when he stopped the run and it looks just like me, you know, so I see myself in him and it's it's amazing. >> You got some veterans on that D-line, too, like you said you have Vita, but you also got A'Shawn, Nacho. Just how how helpful have guys like A'Shawn and Nacho been to energize that room? >> Those guys, they've been playing for a long time and they know a lot of ball, so any question that I have, I literally just ask out loud and it just it get answered, so I love that about this place and uh just, you know, being able to get coached the right way and not by like, you know, don't don't have pride that no no pride is in it, you know, they they're coaching for the right reasons and they want everybody to be successful. >> Is this a dream for you right now standing here talking to us? >> Uh me, yes, because, you know, never everybody don't get this opportunity to, you know, go to the next level and do it do what I get to do every day and I'm I'm so grateful for it and I thank God for it. >> Who do you kind of credit uh your journey to and all you know, the people who helped you get to where you are right now? >> Uh for me, it just took a village. It took a village with me, uh my family back home, uh principals, coaches, like the whole nine. It just took everybody. It took a village to get me where I am today and I and I appreciate everybody for it. Um and and and what like I told somebody in a text the other day, I appreciate what they're going to do continue doing for me even though I'm not even there, you know, so I just appreciate everything they've done to me thus far. >> What's your family been saying, texting you about being here? >> Uh well, my family knows I'm in camp. When I'm in camp mode, I don't really talk a lot. I'll be like just walled off a little bit, but when camp like once after that first preseason game, I gave my mom a call. I was like, okay, we good. Like the jitters is out, so I'm just every week I talk to them a little more a little more, so but once I hit camp it's like I'm dialed in. >> How proud do you think she is of her son right now? >> Uh, she's she's very proud. I hear it every time I go home. I hear it from my community. Um I appreciate my community. I'm going to be a role model for my community. Um and I'm going to continue being a role model for my community. >> Clemson came in with a couple other defenders in this rookie class. One of them's out here putting in some work and you know Josiah, he's he's talking. What's it been like building the relationships with these two guys? >> It's it's incredible. Those guys, Reuben, he's incredible worker. Um something like I've never seen. especially when he's coming off that edge. I was telling guys like I'm like, "Yo, Reuben the real deal." Like but uh yeah, he's him and some of the other guys I've came in with they're they're they're all of what they're advertised. >> Playing at Clemson, you probably did you speak with him any during college time? >> Yeah, I spoke with him a couple times. Yeah. >> So, I'm reading here that your hobby is that you're a gamer. >> Yeah. >> Best question. >> What what do you what what do you I'm not a video game Yeah, what do you >> Is that a good break where we ask them? >> I it's Call Call of Duty. I also just got the Madden 27. I play 2K a little bit. Now, I'm not really good at all of those, but you know, I got I got like I said, it take a team. I got a village that help me help me win a lot, so >> Console or PC? >> Uh console. Yeah. >> All right, thanks guys. >> Thank you.

title: Todd Bowles on Baker Mayfield's Confidence in Offense | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Morning. >> We saw Jay Ajayi out there. What was he able to do? How does he look in practice >> Uh he's just warming up getting accustomed back to playing. He won't be in play. >> We saw Worrilow come out today. How did he feel a day after kind of getting into some work yesterday? >> He felt pretty good, you know, we just got to keep getting him some work and see how he feels next week. >> What you going to play a number of your starters including Is that a feel thing for you like going to operation right you want them to hear plays call plays chance things but is it does it depend on how it goes in other words it's three and out maybe you get another series if we go down there and >> Yeah you you typically want to get between eight and 15 plays if you can get it and if it's a long drive then you got to think about getting them out of it. If it's a short one if they go two three and out then that's six plays so you kind of get them out there but you want to give them a feel for game play and game flow. It's just for the coaches as well as the players. >> With the rotation you got going at defensive tackle and just the front seven how comfortable would you feel playing without Tim Jernigan came to that? >> I'm never comfortable playing without him but you know, we've had injuries before and I played without him before and we got guys up there that's played a lot a bunch of games in this league. They might not have the same impact but they have their own impact in the way. So I'll be comfortable playing with them. >> Does it change the way you call the game? >> It changes what we do probably not the way I call the game. It may change some fronts here and there so we can take advantage of what those guys do do well and that will probably be the only difference. >> You said you wouldn't worry about Ajayi's absence until after two or three preseason games but that's potentially next week. Is there a point where you would expect him to start participating or or face consequences? >> We'll probably talk next week. We'll probably talk next week. Right now, everything's ongoing. >> We saw a little bit of power sharp in his first couple of ones there on offense today. After his preseason game on Friday and what he's been doing now, what have you seen from him this whole game? >> We know he's athletic and he can catch the ball. We got to work on his blocking. He's a willing blocker. We've just got to get his feet and his hands right. You know, with Cade down, we kind of got to rotate everybody in there. >> It seems like you guys used him a lot in pre-snap movement and in lots of different ways. Is it impressive that the newest kid in the room can can handle that much in a first game like that? >> It's impressive that he's got the system down pretty fast. You know, that's very impressive on his part. You know, the quicker you get it down, the faster you play and he's playing fast. >> Coach, how important is it for Buck to be able to get out there and kind of take some of those hits after his time this off season with the surgery? >> It's not so much the hits. It's just game flow for him. He's taking hits in practice. So, that part of it I'm not worried about. It's just getting the game flow and understanding and getting back the feel of the game time. >> Anything else? Uh coach, how do you how do you feel Baker's adjusting and really getting the new offense down? I know it's not totally different, but I know there's some nuances to it. >> There's a lot of nuances to it. I think he's done a great job. You know, he's in here early every morning studying that people don't see and he got it down pretty good. He has a good feel for it. >> Okay. Thank you. >> Yeah.

title: Baker Mayfield on Zac Robinson's System | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: How you doing? >> How's the new offense coming in? I know you're working a lot of contact, coming in earlier to get some of the nuances down on it. >> Yeah, um as an as any offense goes when you're installing in camp, you you kind of have a a base foundation for the plays and your day one stuff and then um as camp the installs go on, you continue to put things in and then it gets to a point where you're really trying to iron out the final details, the checks to make sure that I'm doing my job to put our guys in the best position possible. So I I I think that that process has been good. Uh I think we're in a good place and you know, with guys being nicked up and um you know, having having to plug some people in, it's also it's given us a an opportunity to kind of explore some some different packages, put guys in different spots and uh test some things. So um yeah, obviously want want everybody out there, but it's been good for us to you know, deal with some challenges early on that you know, it's going to happen in season. >> You've got a lot of work in joint practices and things like that, but you haven't played a game. >> [snorts] >> You beat Carolina last year. So for you, what what is it that was important, what do you like about being back on the grass? >> Um it's just different. You know, you go in practice in training camp and you're really testing a lot of stuff out, you know, seeing what guys are capable of doing in the live practice reps and um seeing you know, if you can make certain tight window throws and and in games you you really it's all about the ball, making sure that I have everybody on the same page at the line of scrimmage and then making sure I take care of the ball and and stay efficient with it throughout the process and keep drives moving. >> What are the backs talking about in preseason? You know, it's good to sometimes get hit before the regular season to play that physical style. Is that kind of a a physical thing for you or is it more of a mental thing, just getting those the mental reps in? >> Yeah, more of the mental reps. Um don't get me wrong, I love contact, but uh yeah, I'll save that for the regular season. >> Baker, how has the addition of Kene Nwangwu been going through this offense with Zach Robinson? How much of a gadget guy has he been so far for you? [snorts] >> I mean he's much more than the gadget guy. Uh I I've just been completely overwhelmed with the amount of talent that he has. You know, I I didn't know um until a little later in the spring, more towards mini camp, that he was a receiver going into college. He was a slot receiver at Memphis, and that explains why he's so smooth running routes. Uh and just his run game, he he stays true to his tracks, he reads his blocks really, really well. Um I thought he's been, you know, he a huge addition for us, but just another spark to give Bucky a spark. And then obviously you still have Tuck in there, and and Josh Williams has had a great camp as well, but but KG is another guy just a a veteran presence, a leader, a guy that leads by example, and uh continues to help set the tone for us on offense. >> Hey, you you've had an impact with your receivers the last couple of years. From that perspective, what can you say about the Tampa Bay >> Ted is I mean, he's growing quickly. Um you know, he's picking things up uh really fast, and so that that's good for us. You know, it's allowing him to play play fast, not think, and and just use his size and speed. Um and just I mean, you guys have seen it. He's high-pointing the ball, uh really taking advantage of his one-on-one matchups, just contested catches, things like that, that it's when you're a bigger receiver at 6'4, you want to be a safety blanket for those 50/50 balls, and so um I feel really confident where Ted's at. >> His presence in the red zone, how important is that been? I think about the going back to the Jets throwing that pass interference. >> Yeah, it just just critical moments, you know, I mean, we talk about what what would How would we look at it with Mike down in the red zone? If you're not going to double cover him, we're going to throw it to him, and Ted is is growing into his own right now, and so we're going to try and take advantage of those matchups as well. >> Looking at this offseason, the team put a lot of resources, free agency and draft, into the defense. >> Now that you've got a couple weeks going against this defense, what do you notice about this Chicago Bears defense defense the most? >> They're aggressive. Um there's a lot of things that look different, some schematic things that that Todd's doing different, some good change-ups that uh definitely mess with the QB's eyes, and just your your fundamentals from the get-go. And uh but it it's obviously you added in talent on the defensive side. The front just looks completely different. I mean, Vita hadn't even been out there yet, but it's it's unreal. We've got We've got two deep for sure. And it's it's a talented group up front and then linebackers it allows them to play free. I think Bostic's taken some big steps and Alex Anzalone incredible player. I think physically he's able to cover a lot of ground, get those guys on the same page and then a guy like Trotter he's um he's an animal. He's not He's not a rookie. He's physical, he's aggressive. He talked and you know what, we needed guys like that on the defense and to have a rookie that's that confident in it is really good for the Bucks. >> Another rookie that you've had come in that can catch some passes is Bowers Shorb. What have you seen in terms of Bowers in terms of the tight end room and you waiting for people like that? >> Bowers switched up, man. I think he's um he's not just a receiving tight end. I think he's but he's so quick at the top of his routes, has a really good feel in zone coverage of how to get open, how to stay open. And he's he's taking pride in the blocking and that's something that we've asked our tight ends to do in the last few years to do a lot of dirty work and I think he's taking pride in that. So, Bowers come a long way and I think he's got a really really good shot to make the team. >> Baker, you you said the run game in 2024 was kind of the catalyst for that balanced offense. >> Yep. >> Um what impact do you think Rachaad White can make schematically on the run game? >> I think just not always relying on the gap scheme stuff. I think when you look at you know, we [snorts] started out as much more mid zone and zone schemes in 2024 and then the change up was our gap puller game and that's where we were able to crease people and they didn't know what was coming. And so last year that was we kind of leaned on that too much to where teams can can really tee off on it, bring some pressures to stop that and and and mess with it. It's tough to run when when defenses get a beat on that. So, I think just Zach's understanding the run game, how to keep teams um unbalanced on the defensive side of the ball, how to set things up and just the play action off the run game. You I've said it to you guys, but you can't win in this league dropping 50 times a game, drop back 50 times a game. You have to be able to run the ball, have to be able to play action screen. Uh you need to be able to throw it when you when you have to, but it starts with the run game and then play action right after that. >> D'Eriq, what have you seen from Jaylen Daniels in practice, but then also in the game on Friday? >> Yeah, I mean, Jaylen, there's not a throw on the football field he can't make. Uh he's got a really, really talented arm. Um I think personality-wise, it's just he's he's living his dream. I think he said that to you guys. You can tell though that he embraces every single moment. He enjoys being out here, the grind that it is. Um you know, as a young QB, you got a long way to go learning the process, where just to get guys lined up, but he's he's taking control of it and I think just from the start of spring when he got here to now, um night and day different for him. >> D'Eriq, you were talking to us during the mandatory minicamp that Chandler Whitmer was working with you on feet as or are you still working on [snorts] that and maybe there's some other things so far in camp? >> Yeah, no, definitely still honing in on those little details, you know, making some of the simple throws even easier than they should be and just it starts with your feet. If you're out of rhythm in this system where it's with timing of the routes and the concepts, uh bad things are going to happen. So, it starts with my feet and going through that and trusting the timing of that and going through the progression, checking the ball down. So, Chandler's uh he's annoying with it, for sure. You know, every once in a while you want to put his in a headlock and beat him up, but uh no, I need that. I I like to be coached hard and he's definitely a a stickler about it and I appreciate it. >> What specifically do you want to get done Saturday night with the with the ones? How how long do you want to be out there? >> Just efficient plays. You know, get in there, efficient drives, no negatives. I mean, what you looking for in the preseason? Everybody getting getting lined up, communicating properly, uh and no pre-snap penalties. You know, things in game you're going to have penalties, it's going to happen. You want to avoid them, obviously, but uh really no pre-snap penalties, being on the same page, no MEs from from those ones and uh just getting a good good few drives, whatever that may look like. I have no idea, but uh am getting points on the board. >> John Green is obviously a big fan of yours [snorts] and he'll be in the booth on Saturday. What do you anticipate is going to go up up in there with him and Ronde? >> There honestly there's no telling what's going to happen up there in the booth. It'll all be a good football talk up there though, man. Uh no, he's uh just having him around and and having him still involved around the building is great. Just the energy, um obviously the experience and history that he's had with the program and um it's it's fun to have somebody like that and just the pure joy that he has for football I think is awesome to see as well. >> Do you go back and watch it afterwards? >> The TV copy? I I think I'll have to. Not for Ronde. Ronde's boring. >> [laughter] >> You said when you sat down with Jarvis Landry and Leonard Fournette you talked about your love of playing on the road and your preference for >> Mhm. >> When the schedule came out, were you excited that you're going to be on the road? This is great. >> Yeah, I I think so. I I think um same thing last year. You you get your guys and it's just just the Bucs against everybody else in that city you're going to. Uh and so I think it's a good opportunity for us against the Bengals and um yeah, it's I think we're going to shock a lot of people this year and so I I'm excited to just get on the road and and do that. >> Anything else? >> Did you say surprise people when you said you were going to shock people? >> Yeah, I mean you Listen, we embellish it. I There's no There's no embellishing. I think you you can't avoid it. There's the TVs everywhere. I think everybody's Yeah. Oh yeah, I am. Uh everybody's picking us probably to have a a losing record, so we'll see. >> Thank you, guys.

title: Jalen Hurts on Joint Training Camp with Patriots
text: John, what's your evaluation of the offense? >> I thought it was a good day. I thought we came out and ran the ball well. We had some actions off of that that went well. Thought 7-on-7 was a little tough for me. Um but all learning experience, so excited to get back with the guys and watch the tape. >> Why's the run game been so effective for you? >> Um I think there's the sync- synchronization uh with that group. Um it seems like we've been able to build and um have some you know slow but surely uh improvements. And so we just want to continue to build in that area as well as every other area. That's a really good unit and they've played a lot of ball together. >> Lane Johnson was talking about how you guys stretch the defense out a lot more. >> Yeah. >> How much do you think that helps open up a lot of things with the offense? >> Well, I think it just um yeah, I just think everybody being on the same page really is the most important thing um and I know they're kind of I know they're getting new coaching, new philosophy, and a bit new fundamentals with that, but I guess this comes down to everybody being on the same page in the run game and that carries over through all phases of the offense. Say again? Uh well, I I think we're still putting in a lot of different things. Our offense isn't in fullness. Um came out here and you know, didn't necessarily game plan for the team more so treated it like a a regular practice and so I think it was cool to see some of the raw and unscouted looks, if you will. So um you know, I think he's going to show up and make plays um at every facet of the offense. Ultimately, we're just trying to figure out our identity and what exactly we want that to look like, but obviously it starts with the outside zone and uh in the run game. Yeah. >> Was Was inviting pressure part of that or is that kind of a happy accident? >> Not [snorts] a happy accident. It's definitely a a part of the play. Um you know, when you coach it up, you don't coach it up in the unideal looks. And I think we got a lot of unideal looks today. So, just us being able to respond to when we're hot and hit that as the end is peeling off, it's a a really big play. One that we'd be excited about in the room, but um obviously still something to learn from right there because we want to avoid having a free guy coming in pressure. So, get it off, but it's you know, there's a process there's a process to it. You know, buy into the process of it. >> The deep ball you hit to Elijah, can you take us through through that play? >> Yeah, um I think it was a great route, great great catch. Way to bring it down with the guy coming in from the inside out on his back. Um and great great progress execution. So, you know, it's a a big explosive play in practice. >> You've seen you spend a lot of time after practice with Philly, with Tyler Huntley and other guys. Yeah. How much has that helped and then taken into the joint practice? >> Man, it's it definitely helps. I think every moment. I keep going back to the summer time and all this time that we spend together, how valuable that is and just being able to to to stack stack those moments with day one of training camp to day whatever it is right now. Continue to stack and so I think I think we've got some strides to take in terms of our detail and really being aligned and on the same page from how we're going to run this, you know, new scheme, how we take this new coaching. And and I think when we come out here in practice, every day is an opportunity to learn from that. The good, uh the bad, everything is an opportunity to learn from. So, that's that's what I really get excited about cuz you can come out here and and as you said, you can have success on something, but just because you got the result you wanted doesn't mean it was the way that it was supposed to be done. So, just being committed to the process not the outcome there. >> You mentioned something a little while earlier with pressure today. >> [clears throat] >> What have you noticed in terms of this system and how it has answers with the pressure? >> Um I think ball is ball in the end. I think there's a a mindset that what I've experienced over time is is how you're trained to look at each play. What you alert, what you don't alert. The timing that you're demanded to play with, the timing where it may not have been as uh uh as much of a vocal point. >> Um Now ultimately I think it's it's just a synchronization, you know, to play on time and then play on play in rhythm at the quarterback spot. We've got to make sure we've got the right detail. We've got to make sure we're taking, you know, attacking the right leverage when we get it. It's it's it's it's a a full on time and deal. So we we've still got opportunities to grow to to improve in that area, but I like where we are. >> What's it like being back on the practice field with Mayden? >> I think it was a great day out here. Um man, I know he's going out there and competing. Got a lot of love for him, always have. it seems like it was competitive practice. >> So I saw him catching up with you. you know, I I I think Drake has had a lot of success already, so I don't know what my advice, you know, would do. I just think he needs to continue the progression that he's on. I mean, he's he's already accomplished so many great things in a short time, and I expect more great things to come for him. >> So AJ catching up with you and his teammates on the sideline. Did you guys have a chance to catch up with him? >> No, I didn't get to you yet. Yeah. >> How tough has it been with Makai missing a lot of time and Demonte as well, but trying to get a line with Makai missing a lot of practice, and just getting to know him as a person and on the field? It's it's it's a challenge. It's a challenge because he's not out there getting the actual reps, but just being intentional with the walkthroughs, being intentional with the moments we have, you know, off the field, um after practice as you see, all those things come into the into play when you're talking about trying to build that chemistry. >> Jalen, is having a new coordinator new voice to learn, is that becoming usual for you? Have you kind of learned how to It seems like every year you have Yeah, well, I don't know it any other way. So, I I just um definitely got a way of going about it. Um and I know that there are just things that are part of the process, you know, I think ultimately you you want the alignment, you want everybody to be on the same page and then the goal never changes in terms of going out there and finding a way to win, but we've obviously got to continue to build that chemistry there. >> From your perspective, two more. >> When you and Denzel especially well and I know it's not the best question to ask on a day of joint practices, but um how does he challenge you in practice? >> Well, I think um it's been He's a smart corner, he's fast, he trusts his instincts. I think he plays team football at his position, right? He knows what his front seven is capable of. He um I think he has confidence in his teammates from how he plays the position on an on an island often.
