I think like that's what brings you or that's the habits and the process you have to have to become a great player. Um, and it makes all of us better. Um, it makes Cam better because he's got to understand, like Kevin's Kevin feels like he's not going to get there, but he's going to get there. And so he has to layer the ball, right? He has to, you know, control him with his eyes more. Um, and so him playing like that every day, uh, I couldn't I don't want to ask anything less of him. Like I want him to do that every day. We've seen you go up and make several catches going up over the defensive back winning the 50/50 jump balls. How much do you have to >> I guess earn your quarterback's trust on those 50/50 balls so that he knows that you'll go up there and win the battle? >> Yeah. I mean, if you don't catch it, he don't want to throw it to you. And so, you know, especially in the beginning when they're giving you a chance on those balls, like it's your it's your duty to make sure that you catch that ball. Um because once they gain that trust with you, you know, then you get more leeway because again, it is a 50-50 ball. It really isn't, but you're not going to catch every single one of them. That's just the name of the game. You know, they they get paid, too. Um but the more consistently you do it in the beginning and and when they come back to you, you have a a winning rate, you know, they're going to want to keep coming back to you. Um yeah, it's pretty simple. If if you look back to this time last year, that transition to the league, what were some of the biggest areas where it gave you a tough time? >> Uh, I think it's just there's just a lot going on. Like everything that you experience is the first time you're experiencing something. Um, in terms of being in the NFL and so with as with anything, the first time you do something is not going to be the when you're the best at it. And so I think that's just the biggest thing. everything is new to you. Were there any like particulars as far as that? Um, I think just for me in specific, just understanding like how much like what it means to be an NFL receiver, I didn't fully know all of the characteristics and traits that you needed to have or yeah, like like I said, I didn't know them um or know that that was the possibility or what it looked like. And so now to me that I have a better grasp of that, I think that's what has allowed me to get better at the position. >> Now that you have this better grasp, knowing you have just been through it, what is your take on on Cardell Tate and how he's made the adjustment so far? >> Yeah, he's doing a great job. Um, especially for a rookie. Like I said, everything that you're doing is new to you. Um, and so I think he's done a wonderful job picking everything up uh right away. Um, and you can see that Dan like as he goes on and, you know, gets through the first game, second game, gets past the 10th game, and then finishes the season and then gets into his second year, like this kid is going to be a really great player. Um, and so for me, that's exciting. It's like, you know, the in my opinion, I don't know how everybody else thinks, but in my opinion, the more good receivers that you can have in the room, the better it's going to be. um you know cuz it helps you out individually cuz if you have another weapon out there, it's going to be less focused on you and vice versa. Um and then the quarterback just has more options and it just it makes the team better as a whole. The the receiver room competition increases and so everybody has to get better from that standpoint. Um and so I'm super excited about it. You talked about your lean when uh over the summer or over the spring, I guess. Now that you've incorporated that stuff for several weeks and high intensity work, has it become more second nature? What are what are you feeling about? >> Sorry, what was the first part of the question? >> The lean >> Oh, yeah. Yeah. Uh yeah, I think it's made me just a better player. Like I think if you just watch the tape, I've been a much better receiver. I look more like an NFL receiver. Um and so I'm happy to see that. I'm happy to, you know, keep finding things to help me progress my game. >> Are you thinking about it much or has it become kind of >> I think it's something that you have to keep reinforcing. Um, like especially with a new skill like it's not going to, you know, become second nature even within a year. Um, but I I have some like things that I do before practice to ensure that, you know, I'm in the right mindset to be able to have those things, you know, clicking. >> What are those things that you do? uh like for like I write things down before practice like key focus points for technique on that specific day. Um and then just like my warm-up on the field is a whole bunch of drills that promote uh those uh the good body language, the good posture, the good shride length, the uh the aggressive mentality, the forward body lean, like all that stuff is built into the warm-up to make sure that hey like I hit all these things before practice and now it feels like it's more second nature. Not to uh not to dwell on Kevin stuff, but in most plays where we would call a defenseless receiver, how defenseless really are you? Are there things that you do to kind of protect yourself in case that happens or is it you just have to play? >> It kind of depends on the specific play. Um a lot of the times if you're running down the field, it's hard for you to see the safety, especially if the ball is on your outside shoulder. You're looking at the ball. you might be able to see him in your peripheral, but you kind of just have to trust the quarterback to protect you. And so really what's in your mind is, hey, catch the ball, like secure the catch, and then the the rest is, you know, trust the quarterback and if you get hit, you get hit. Um, that's just the name of the game. >> From your perspective, how have you seen Cam grow throughout training camp and under Dall's offense? Yeah, I think he's just like a more mature quarterback in terms of, you know, he's always going to have the ability to be a playmaker, like a magician with the ball in his hands and make these insane throws, you know, scramble and throw across his body, all that type of stuff. Um, but he's really, you know, taking strides and like being a field general, like being able to operate the offense and, you know, drive it down the field um as a true NFL quarterback. And you know, it's been awesome to see him make those uh that progress. >> Do you have do you have what you consider to be good days and bad days yourself? And how much better equipped are you to bounce back from a bad day after going through this last year? >> Um yeah, I mean, you're definitely going to have days that are better than others and worse than others. Um, but I think for me it's a lot of the times it's more about like how I go about the day and like did my did each rep start with the right technique, the right mindset, um, in terms of judging whether or not I had a good or a bad day. Um, and then if I do have a bad day, I think I am a lot better equipped in terms of, you know, coming back the next practice and having a quote unquote good day because like I mentioned before, like there's things that I have to do in order to be an NFL receiver, in order to have like an NFL receivers's technique. And those are the type of things that I revert back to when I have a quote unquote bad day. And I think a lot of times it just kind of I don't know, it's like I'm like, "Oh, okay. I just have to do this. I just have to do this. Like I it reverts back to the process or the technique. And so I do think I'm a lot better prepared than I have been in the past in that sense. when you go out and when you run your route, obviously out here you you could be with any of the three quarterbacks or four attendants out there >> and are you just a seab ball catch ball guy or do you are like if depending on what quarterback's in, you're like, "Okay, I may expect the speed to be different or the placement to be different and I've got to adjust." >> Uh, no. I don't really think about that too much. Just run my route how I'm supposed to run it. Um, and yeah, that's all. >> When it comes to a preseason game, what would you say you personally get most out of one? Like, is it just time on task or what's the most, I guess, effective result from preseason game experience for you? >> Uh, I think it's just, you know, getting more reps. Um, getting used to like a game environment, quote unquote. Um, yeah, like going against different DBs. Um, but not much more than that. Go ahead, Chris. >> Sure. >> Yeah. >> Okay. I was just going to ask like so like in the preseason game, you get through like the last one, you got three balls thrown your way >> um and didn't have a catch. Like what what do you learn about the experiences when the ball's not coming your way in those preseason games? >> Um uh I'm not really sure. Like I don't know. like just focusing on the play and like making sure you run your route, Chris, no matter where the ball's going and just >> play receiver like it's a dependent position >> like you know what I'm like you're not going to get 10 targets a game every game you know like even when you're the number one receiver you're not going to get 10 targets a game every single game. Um that's just the nature of being a receiver. Um so I don't know if there's much to learn other than that's just what it is what it means to be a receiver. Like, you know, when you play Oline, you just you're going against your guy every single play. Um, and that's what you're judged by. Um, but at receiver, it's a little bit different, right? Right. Like, the quarterback has to decide to come to you. You you have to win your route. Um, the ball has to be placed, you know, in a catchable position. Um, and that's just what it means. Like sometimes not all those things are going to go right. That's it is what it is. >> How much are you looking forward to just coming in here and what's kind of the focus for you for another short practice? Uh, I don't know if the joint practice changes too much of my mindset. I kind of try to up as just as much as I would in the joint practice. So, like it's pretty much the same. >> You probably you guess >> you get to talk to us. >> Hey, you ain't wor. >> How much uh how much you feel like you missed while you were out and how happy are you to be back? >> Uh, shoot. I mean, you know, the problem with any you miss one day in the NFL and it just kind of feels like you missed a Super Bowl and uh naturally it should feel like that. I mean, we put so much into this in the off season, we put so much into it each and every day, meetings, walk through practice, and so any little rep that you miss, like it just feels like the end of the world. Um, I'm I'm grateful. I'm thankful that the team has been behind me, had my back, let me kind of do my thing and um I feel a lot better. I'm excited. Um and just excited to be out here with these guys. But man, we're getting better each and every day. >> That said, how much do you empathize with guys that maybe miss extended time like a whole season or several weeks at a time knowing how hard it is and how much guys want it? Yeah, I mean, you know, again, it is a year round type of thing. And so, you you definitely understand, you feel for these guys who miss time, who have missed time. I've missed uh time in my past. And so, I definitely understand. And the best thing you can do is you can you can stay there for them. You can be there for them and make them feel included and welcome. And so, we do a good job of that here. I'm in every meeting. They make me feel like I've been in every practice. And so, man, I coach calls on me like like I've done every rep. And so I'm I'm extremely thankful. I'm extremely uh just grateful for the chance to be able to go out here today and and do my thing. I mean, it it it truly does sitting there or not being around the team during practice, it just, you know, it's just not the same. And so this this is the best game in the world. >> You guys got a pretty good interior defensive line duo coming in here for the joint practice this week. How much do you and Jeff relish the chance to win more battles than those two guys? Yeah, I mean I mean truthfully, you know, we we understand that uh there there's good players in the league in Seattle. I play with Leo and so extremely familiar. I mean and I I'm sure I I love Leo. He's one of my favorite dackles and so learn a lot from them. But um you know, our our battle is with each other and you know, it's with ourselves is making sure that what we do looks a certain type of way. We have a standard and and it has to be physical. It has to be violent. we have to play with, you know, the most effort in the NFL and and that's our standard and every other team may not have those same standards. And so that's why you can't compare um us to anybody else because we, you know, our stuff is just we we want it to look a certain way. >> What do you think about Kona, guy you've kind of gone up against in his practice? >> Oh, I mean, I was talking to somebody today. I mean, you know, you talk about a rookie stepping in and just owning a position. I mean, a guy that just shows up and works. And you know, the problem with rookies is, you know, it takes a second for you to feel like you belong or feel like you're welcome. And I mean, that's a guy that put the work in. He knew he put the work in and shows up to work like he did. And so, you could appreciate it as a rookie. Shows up. He wants to battle. He's he wants to go against me. He wants to go against Jeff. He wants to go against the best guys and and he wants to get better. He wants to pull you to the side, ask you the questions, maybe even take some extra reps if you're willing and able, um, depending on the day. And so again, you you can only appreciate, you can only value that because as a young guy, those are the things that matter. And you know, he's getting to go against um you know, two of the better guys in the NFL and interior in my opinion. >> A question he's asked you that kind of stood out of the way he processes the game. >> I think with him, I mean, he's trying to figure out what is his best set. And so based on width, based on alignment, maybe based on which foot, whatever his thing is, he's like, man, what is the best set for these type of things? And so again, I mean, as as a O lineman, you know, you can understand the run stuff is going to be the run. You got to be physical. The pass rush stuff is where young guys and old guys separate themselves in the NFL. And so once you understand that you're able to pass block, run block kind of it's one and the same. You know, you understand that you got to be physical to run block. Pass block. He asked all the questions in the world. And he's he's getting so much better. He's getting valuable reps. you've been in the league for a while now and had all kinds of experiences. I'm curious like as you play in this preseason game, what type of a measuring stick is that for you at this point? >> I think it's good. I mean, you know, you talk about measuring stick, it's hard because you don't know um who you're going against and and it doesn't truly it doesn't matter. You talk about guys who um these days, shoot, everybody has played in the league. If you're a rookie, I mean, they're expected to to play at the highest level possible. And so, um it doesn't matter for me. It's getting out there. is putting the shoulder pads on. It's feeling the fans. It's the adrenaline. It's everything that goes along with playing a game because you can you can get so caught up in everything else that you make the game harder or you say, "Man, this is my routine. This is what I do." And then the game just is a normal day. And so I try to prepare that way, do the same thing for the games. But the first game, if you do it the first week of the season, you're like, "Oh shoot, man. I I got to figure out my process. We have three hours before the game instead of 30 minutes to get ready." And so what do I do with three hours? What do I do with, you know, and so you figuring out your process? That's what the preseason is for. And um the older you get, the more you appreciate it. >> Play. Do you want to or you think maybe they roll you out Friday for the practice and hold you out Sunday? >> Uh I'm I'm know and I really don't care, man. I'm I'm a I'm a football player. I do this and there ain't nothing else that I We here. You know, if we put me out there, don't you going to think I'm playing regardless. I'm here to I'm here to support [laughter] talked about making these practices and actually giving the coaches the freedom to, you know, make the drills apply to the game. How much have you seen that with uh White Cotton and Tanzel Smart? >> Yeah, I mean, so I mean, crazy part about Tanzel um is as I I played with Tanzel, Tanzel got me ready for the games. He was I talked pass rush with him. I went through drills. I watched film with him every single day. And so he was like the guy that I bounced all my hey how my rush look, what could I do better? And so ironically, three years later, he's my coach. And so now you kind of see the the carryover and it's just like nothing nothing ended. It's showing up. It's learning. He's sitting next to me. I'm Hey man, what what did I do? What can I be better? And White Cotton, man, he he's evolved so much. He he does such a good job. Again, X and O's is one thing, but now you see the drills. I mean, the correlation. We're doing uh retest trace drills. We're doing swipe to counter drills. We're doing, you know, we're learning pass rush moves. And so, um, man, he's he's teaching us, you know, what wins in the NFL cuz we all want to work all these cute moves and all the time cute looks good and cute doesn't win. And so you understand that physicality wins, you understand effort wins, and then from there, man, it's just about going out there and doing your 111th. And I could appreciate what he does for us because you see the drills, you turn the tape on, and you see the resemblance and and that's all you can ask for. >> How familiar are you with uh I guess with Chris Johnson, Tim Shaw, who's in the building, I guess Steve Leon, a former player, and how meaningful is to do the I guess the ice bucket challenge to kind of pay tribute to some of those guys? Um I'm not extremely familiar with those guys. Obvious I mean Chris Johnson probably the most out of all those guys. Um but I mean you talk about humans one um but man I mean these are these are young young men that are that are experiencing I mean something just extremely traumatic and you can only feel for them. You can only want the best for them. You can only say look man I want to do whatever I can to help these guys. I want to do whatever I can to raise money to raise awareness. Anything in the world to help these people because you don't know. I mean, I don't know the the situation, but you know, maybe it's one day you wake up and you don't know what's going on with you. And so, life is so short. You got to appreciate the little things and you got to be there for everybody. I mean, you don't know when anybody's last day is. Um, RP to OJ. Um, I know that happened recently and just an example of just man, loving each other, one, loving one another, and being there for your people. >> You got to know Darnold early on in OL's career. Seeing him come back through what he's gone through and now being a Super Bowl champ. What does that tell you about the league in general that he's persevered this way, >> man? I mean, you know, much like life, you know, it's it's so short, but but it's unexpected and and you know, Sam Darnold is an example of making the most out of your opportunities. And, you know, all you could ask for is opportunity. He he took one after another. I mean, I think he was the backup in Carolina or something and nobody like you look at his situation now, you don't even remember that, but that's a part of his story. That's a part of his life that was extremely valuable, extremely important for that time of his life. It got him to where he is now. And I see Sam, we seen it then. He was a hell of a quarterback and and nothing has changed. I mean, he can make every throw. He can run the ball. He's smarter now. He's more confident, man. Super Bowl champ. And man, I'm I'm so happy for him. I couldn't do nothing but smile when I seen it. But, uh, you know, he's he's opposition uh here in two days and in four days and then he got to get it just like everybody else. >> I'm excited, man. Uh, you know, I love going up against my teammates. I love obviously going up against JFM, Jeff, and all those guys. Uh, I get great work, but it's nice to hit some other people and, uh, you know, put the power onto them. >> You mentioned going against Jeff. How has that experience? See, you win some, see you lose some also. How's that been? >> Yeah, it's been awesome, man. Uh, you know, coming into this league, being a rookie, like you want to go up against the best. And knowing that I'm going up against Jeff here, I know when it comes Sunday time, you know, it's going to be that much easier. And so, uh, it's a true blessing to have him on our team. And then, you know, him to go up against me every day in practice, it's a true blessing. >> I saw him I saw him walking off the field with you uh after Monday. Was there just kind of recap in practice, some some pointers and things in the game? >> Yeah, just some things that he's seen with me and just, you know, just helping me out. Uh obviously being a rookie, there's, you know, a lot of things I need to grow on and he sees a lot of those flaws in me and uh it's just awesome having that veteran leader being able to tell you, you know, what he sees and how I can improve my game. How's that communication with you and JC been so fluent so far on the right side? >> It's been awesome, man. Uh, you know, being the rookie, he's been, you know, that veteran presence for me there and, uh, it's awesome playing with him. Uh, I feel like I don't have to do much when I'm working in combo blocks just cuz he does most of the work, but uh, it's awesome having him next to me and, you know, his mindset day in and day out, he's he's an alpha and he's trying to get after so it's a lot of fun playing next to him. We may have talked about it draft time, but Duke many weather recirculated a video of you training. >> Yesterday. What kind of impact did he have on you getting ready? >> Man, uh Worth can't explain what he uh did for me and my football journey. Uh he's helped me out a lot and uh he he pointed out a lot of the flaws I had in my game going into the pre-draft process. And those three to four months I was with him, we attacked it a lot. And uh I think I became a better football player in those four months. and I think it's paying off here now. >> What were some of those falls that you guys tackled? >> Yeah, just some stuff with my stance. That was like the biggest thing. Uh stance and then hands and being able to strain. Uh those were like kind of like the three main things that he seen in me that I had to work on and we attacked it day in and day out and I feel like it's translated well coming into the league now. >> We hear you guys talk about strength a lot. How do you practice that? How do you get better at that? It sounds like it's effort from our end. Like what is strain on your end? Yeah, it it's a lot of it is effort, but uh it's hard to explain, man. It's, you know, you're getting into your stance. It's like this brace. And I really don't know how to explain it, but it's like really just like sucking sucking everything up, just squeezing yourself and just fighting and it's like you said, a lot of it's just effort and it's a mindset. You >> your coaches teammates been very compliment complimentary of you uh in recent weeks. How how you think you're doing so far in camp and what are some things you feel like you still got to get better at? Yeah, I think I'm doing all right. Uh there's still a lot of things I need to work on. Uh I mean it's awesome that they're giving me praise, but I know and I mean I'm hearing it in the film room. There's a lot of things I need to work on and uh I'm going to continue to improve and grow. >> What's the biggest jump going from college to to [snorts] pros? >> Uh I think the biggest thing is just the speed off the off the ball. Uh especially with Jeff, you know, he's a big, you know, time up the snap count. And so those little details matter and it was something that really didn't matter that much in college because you could just beat him with, you know, natural talent, but here, you know, those little details, if you're not getting off the ball, you know, it's a sack. >> What are some things you think that helped you stand out and made you start to get some of those first teams? >> Uh, you know, I I just always contribute contributed to me working hard and that's just kind of been my mindset going into college. Uh, you know, when I got to San Jose State, I'd only played one year of football and I just put my head down and I I just worked hard and that's all I really know how to do. And I know that'll just carry me a long way.

title: Robert Saleh on Anthony Hill, Carnell Tate & Seahawks Week | Press Conference
text: today. Uh woke up feeling some lower half stiffness. Hopefully we get him back on Friday. Uh nothing to be concerned about. Um other than that, uh we're evaluating a couple of guys for some injuries. Uh I know Kendrick came out there in that two-minute drive or that move the ball drive. Uh he's getting evaluated for a shoulder. Uh we think it's just a stinger, but we'll be we'll know more tomorrow. >> How's Martin? >> What's that? >> He was good. Uh uh he went through some practice. He feels good. Uh was active. Uh, he came out clean. >> Yeah. Yeah, he's good. He's in good shape. >> I like the way Anthony Hill seems to be showing up around the football a lot, especially today. He's seemed like four or five different times had his hands around the football. >> Yeah, every day is going to be a new experience for him, you know, and all and all the rookies really, but um but he's starting to grasp the middle linebacker position. Um, >> we ask a lot of that group, but uh but he's doing a good job handling it. with the ice bucket challenge there. Can you just talk about what it meant for you guys to come together as a team and do that and then obviously call out >> uh you know what, give credit to the to the guys. You know, Morgan, Cam, and uh >> uh Jeff put that one together for the team. Um, I think anytime you can you can stand up for your I mean there it just seems like there's a lot of athletes uh not just in football but all over that are being affected by this thing and to get a group of guys together and and bring awareness to it I think is always special. >> How polished he is as a prospect now that you've seen him now. How do you feel his transition? >> Who's this? >> Cornell Carell. uh he looks real good, you know, like uh and there's still a lot of uh things that he has to learn with the game with regard to the game within a game that's happening out there at the uh on the perimeter. It's different than than college where, you know, I always tell people in college, you know, from from here to that pole is covered, but from here to this pole is wide open. You know, it's just a a a different mentality on how tight coverage is in this league and and how precise you have to be with regard to attacking leverage. um winning on negative leverage, winning on positive leverage, and creating separation for the quarterback and winning and being strong at the point in tight tight uh windows. So, he's learning every day. Uh he's doing a really nice job. He's only going to get better. >> Started out initially, I asked how we're starting to see move him across the formation. Was that plan or >> that that's uh Daval's offense is built in a way where he can move his guys anywhere that he needs to uh needs them. >> And then how about what you've seen from him against press? >> No, that that's still ongoing. you know, we we haven't pressed as much and uh you know, he got some action against San Francisco. Hopefully, we get a little against Seattle. I know we'll get some versus Chicago. Um but that's going to be a year-long evolution. >> Looking forward to having Seattle in here. What What's the challenge there compared to maybe last week? >> Uh you know what, they're not to compare the two. I mean, they're they're two elite organizations. Uh both teams sitting there in the second round of the playoffs a year ago. Uh shoot we were playing for the for the one seed uh in the very last week of the season. So uh another great football team, another great organization. Um a lot of great players on on in all three phases in that uh on that Seattle roster and and I'm sure they're they're excited to get out and stop playing one another. I mean they they had to get to camp a week early and they haven't seen anybody except for themselves and so I'm sure they're they're looking forward to it as much as we are. >> What would you like to see from your guys in this one that you maybe didn't see last week? What's the message to you guys? >> Um, you know what, like the the message last time was just to to try to establish the identity of of violence and I and and and I know that it may may not seem like it from the sideline until you get to the tape, but I I do feel like both offensive and defensive lines really handled the line of scrimmage all week last week. Um, especially in the run game and and the expectation is that we continue to try to establish our identity and who we're going to be. Were the secondary struggles connected at all to the pass rush last week? And what do you want to see particularly from the secondary? >> Uh, we we've got to get um from from a from a secondary standpoint, everything's just got to get tighter. You know, a lot of the um issues last week were in one-on-one situations and and that's what we're trying to evaluate. Sure, we can play zone and we can keep underneath help and all that stuff, but at the end of the day to to win in this league, and we had a a good talk about it today, you've got to win in man coverage. You've got to win at the line of scrimmage and one-on-one. So, it's all one-on-one. Third and four, got to have it. Um, and that's the mentality that you've got to have at all times. And, uh, so for us, it's about getting tighter in our coverage, uh, cleaning up our press techniques, cleaning up our off techniques, and understanding what each, uh, um, each technique is is being asked out of the guys. >> Some place for plot at least where he was close and didn't. >> Yeah. Is that a different kind of problem than better problem? No, it's it's uh for him and and really for uh in in the game last week just speaking for Flot, everything started at the line of scrimmage when you when you really go back and look at it and uh I know there was a couple plays where there was off coverage and there's there's awareness. You're not game planning, but when you're at the line of scrimmage, um a lot of the issues that happen downfield actually end or start at the line and that's where he's got to improve. you want people generally like what's the general rule about >> you when you're out there impress there there's so that that's part of the game right like if you're saying in a perfect world you want to end a guy at the line of scrimmage that rarely ever happens um you know so you're you're trying to create disruption at the line of scrimmage to to mess with the timing of the quarterback just enough to give your D line a chance to get home uh but at the same time you're trying to be disciplined to make sure that you're not giving up a go ball so there's a lot being asked out of the corner at the line of scrimmage but uh the Last thing you want to do is give free access release where you're in chase mode, which is what ended up happening to him uh on his on the one rep on the gold ball to stribbling. >> As this has played out, how much have you found yourself being involved in the offense more than you thought less than you thought having someone like does that put your mind at ease knowing there's little he hasn't seen? >> Uh it's it's about what I expected. Um there's always uh to to steal from our good friend in Houston, uh Matt Burke, the duality of coaching where you're where you're you're trying to give awareness to both sides of the ball to make sure that we're all coaching in a way that's educating everybody. But, but what happened last week in in San Francisco to me was nothing. >> Oh, yeah. I was just going to say, so I mean, fair fair to say that as long as you take it to the brief and give your guys the green light to do that. >> Yeah, we're we're always going to push the envelope with regards to towing the line of violence, uh, that doesn't mean you go out there, play cheap. It doesn't mean that you're you're you're creating personal or you're you're getting personal fouls called on you. Ideally, you're agitating and getting personal fouls called in your favor, but um, we want our guys going from the snap to the echo of the whistle, period. Are there times where you're meeting the guys for the first time on the field? How do they learn plays and dynamics so quickly? How do you treat these guys like they are on the team and they've been here for three hours? Um well that's part of it you know like um every every position room has two coaches and uh you know so you have your your senior assistant and then you have your young assistant and the young the young assistant's job is to get those young men up to speed as quickly as possible. But we've also you know put the light the work in in the beginning of uh when we first got here. you know, all the voiceover tapes, all the all the uh the teach tapes, the the like the little short films that we make with with our voices to help them so they can go home and just watch these little five minute short clips on what is a hook drop, what is a uh what is whatever technique uh we're trying to teach in all three phases. title: Trevon Diggs: "This Feels Like Home" | Seattle Seahawks
text: Welcome to Seattle. What's what made this a good fit for you? >> Um the history. Um seeing what these young guys what this uh team has been doing. Uh seeing a lot of young guys just coming together and just being a great football team. Um I know a lot of familiar faces here. Uh Josh Job, D-Law. Um just those guys talking to those guys. They saying it's a great fit, you know, just everything that they have going here and you know, I would love to be a part of it. >> What did the coaches tell you about what they want you to to show or what they think your role would be? >> Um yeah, I just come here to compete, you know, I just want to come here compete, you know, earn my keep. Um you know, just do everything I can just to, you know, earn a spot here and you know, help this team win. >> When did this come together? >> Um yesterday. >> Is that the first time they showed an interest in uh yeah, they've been talking to my agent for a little bit. Um and then they he told me they were going to come down here give me down for a workout. Uh I came down here. I worked out. Um you know, and then the rest is history. >> Did you have a visit with Detroit as well? Like were there some other teams interested, too? >> Yeah. Uh I had a visit with Detroit. Um I was supposed to see a a couple other teams, but you know, it's I like the here a lot. Like this feels like home, you know, I I got a lot of familiar faces. Coach Scott, um uh AD, you know, so just being a part of those guys. Those guys knowing me, knowing, you know, where my heart is, knowing how how I want to compete. So, you know, it it felt right. >> What was the biggest driving factor for you? Was it just the fact that you knew so many guys here particularly in the secondary? >> Yeah, most definitely. Um you know, you got to have someone that, you know, you can relate to, can talk to, you know, guys going to help you out and you know, push you to to be your best, you know, and that's what I want for myself and that's what I want to do. >> What was the plan for sort of summer? Was your plan to be picky and wait through the summer and find a situation you really liked or what was your plan there? >> I was just finding somewhere that, you know, felt like home, you know, finding somewhere, you know, that I'll have opportunity to compete, um have a opportunity, you know, to play and just, you know, if it felt right, you know, that's what I wanted to do more than make the right decision for me. >> What do you feel like your strengths are as a corner and where are some places that you're wanting to improve? >> Um, my strengths as a corner, I got great ball skills. Um, you know, I I I have a great knack for the ball, just understanding, you know, offenses, understanding routes, understanding, you know, what receivers want to do, you know, I think that's my strongest abilities. >> Do you feel like the defense that they play here and, you know, having some familiarity with Karl and Josh from college and having them here, how does it translate for for what you're doing here? >> Uh, it's a lot of uh similarities. Um, just talking to Josh, you know, earlier today, he was telling me there's a lot of similarities. Um, you know, he he said he'll help me out, you know, get the playbook down, you know, I'm going to be in my playbook every day just to get the whole defense down and, you know, just be being able to give myself a chance, give myself an opportunity to come out here and compete and, you know, help win. >> And do you feel like you're fully healthy? You feel fully recovered? >> Most definitely. Uh, it's my first off season that I've been able to uh just not rehab and actually do off season training. So, you know, um, a lot of trainers put the work in, helped me put the work in to get to where I'm at today, you know, I'm truly thankful for that and, you know, it's a blessing from God on it from God, honestly, just to be able to, you know, come out here again. >> What are you looking to show? Obviously, you have a tough run of injuries there. Now that you are healthy, like you said, what are you looking to show here? >> Uh, I want I'm looking to show that I'm still the best, you know, I'm looking to show that uh I just want to win, you know, be there for my teammates, be a great teammate, you know, uh be a great player. >> Now with Josh and Karl, what's it mean having them as teammates? >> Uh, it's really good, you know, like I said, just having someone that you're familiar with or that you can talk to, you know, ask questions with, um, it helps out a lot. >> Was last year tough for you with the injuries and the concussion? Did you ever dealt with anything like that, concussion related? >> Uh, no, that was my first concussion ever. Uh, it was different, you know, um, but just overcoming uh injuries, you know, just adversity, overcoming adversity period is always tough, but, you know, if if you did it before, you know, you can do it again, You know, it's just I just want to be able to play healthy, you know, this year the full season um and hope. >> What was it like trying to deal with those knee injuries coming one after another and just kind of feeling like you're repeatedly in the same spot trying to work back? How was that to handle mentally and all that? And then what was the process of getting to back where you feel like you miss it in that area you're you're back on the field? >> Yeah, it was tough. Um it was tough, but just keeping good people around you, you know, my family was a a great support system for me. Um keeping my mental straight uh just keep going, you know, you know, I love football, you know, uh I I just love football. I love to play. So, this being a part of football, you know, it's kind of like it's part of my job. It's a part of your job. You going to get hurt. You going to have things that happen. You going to get traded. You going to get cut. Things happen, but you just got to keep going. >> Marcus Lawrence came here from Dallas, won a Super Bowl last year. And now you got Dante Fowler here and you here. Adam Gase is here. It's like Dallas uh a lot of guys coming here from from that organization. >> Yeah. >> What are your thoughts on on the kind of that transition and obviously uh the different places you played? >> Um just being with those guys, you know, the things that that we were doing and the the family aspect of it, you know, I I I see a lot of similarities. Just uh how close the guys are, you know, how how tight the group is, you know, uh that that's very important with a football team. Just, you know, being together, you know, being one, making sure your locker room is straight. And you know, I I see a lot of similarities there. >> The concussion, was it Is it true that you were mounting a television? >> It fell on your face or your What happened? >> Yeah, fell on my head. >> And then you were affected for a couple months from that, right? >> No, it was it was only um I was out of concussion protocol in like a week, but I was dealing with some other injuries. >> Timing-wise, do you like that you're joining the team and you're going to get on the road for a little extended trip to kind of start forming that bond with the team? >> Yeah, for sure. Um you know, just want to get in with the guys um you know, vibe, you know, get familiar with them, get familiar with new faces, um, and just go out there and help. >> What have you kind of admired about Mike McDonald's defense watching it from afar and kind of >> Amazing. >> seeing what what they do and and jumping into it, how big of a factor is that for >> It is it looks amazing. You know, they get to the quarterback, you know, they get create turnovers, you know, they do all the right things. So, you know, I'm excited to, you know, hopefully be a part of it, um, go out there, compete, and just try to help this team win. That's all I want to do. >> Do you have a play in a minute? Could you play by the final preseason game next Friday? You think you'd be in shape to do it by then? >> Uh, possibly. I got to put in the work, you know, get practice reps, um, and maybe. >> For all the things you had to go through to get here to have this opportunity to be the one that works with the defending champions. Your position is a position of need for them. I mean, almost like meant to be in a way, right? >> Yeah, most definitely, um, it's it's just it's been a long journey, you know, and I'm just extremely thankful, you know, it's been a blessing, you know, from God, you know, I thank him the most, you know, uh, and I I'm just thankful for the opportunity. >> You played some in the slot, is that right? Or have you mostly been on the outside? >> I've been on the outside. Uh, I I played in the slot, too, um, whatever. >> All right, thank you, everyone. >> Thanks for coming. >> Thank you.

title: Brady Russell: "The Biggest Thing I Pride Myself On Is Multiplicity" | Seattle Seahawks
text: Good afternoon. >> Congratulations. >> Yeah, thank you. >> Congrats. How's first few days of parenthood? >> Yeah, it's great. It's uh it's fun. She's super cute, so. I never thought a newborn was cute until I saw my own. >> What was Saturday like? >> Uh Saturday was cool. It was eventful. The um night before we like kind of thought she was in labor, having contractions and stuff. So, it was like don't know if I'm going to be at the game, don't know if I'm going to have to be home, and then contractions held off and stuff. So, I was like, "All right." And she was like, "Go play. Like, go have fun." And so, uh went, and then halftime checked, and she was back having contractions again and stuff. So, I was like, "I better hit the road." So. >> Were you on alert the whole time? Like, was there a plan somebody was going to tell you if it was going down? >> Yeah, so I gave her our security guy's number, George, and they had like a car and stuff ready in case I needed to get out of there quick, but it wasn't super urgent. Um I had time to go home and get her, and yeah. >> How How How or how and weight, and what's the what's the name? >> She was 20 and 1/2 inches. She's 9 lb 4 oz. She's a little tank. Uh her name's Hadley. Yep. >> Have you ever had to leave a game early before? What was it kind of like going out of a stadium when the game still going on? >> Absolutely not. Yeah, that was fun. That was uh I love the guys that work security at the garage there. So, they were all pumped up for me, giving me fist bumps as I left the stadium, and directed me out, getting me through quick, so. >> Show up, make a hit, get out. >> Yeah. Yeah, absolutely. >> That's your first, right? >> Uh yes, sir. >> How uh in retrospect, how good was it that you've been with the team now three going on four years that you had inroads that you could connections that you could arrange all that? >> Yeah, that's super helpful, for sure. And just everybody wanting to help me out and not feeling like a hindrance that my wife's giving birth, you know? That they're all supporting me and and loving me, and just excited for me to go have my first child. >> What kind of perspective does that give you? You know, you talked a little bit about having a child. What did you get out of that? >> Yeah, I think the I had the perspective probably ahead of time cuz I had 9 months to prepare, if you will. Not that I'd ever really feel prepared, but um just the perspective of that now it's like when I got into the NFL, I'm just a single dude that's out there having fun playing ball, but um it really does turn into a provision for your family, so um it's pretty [music] cool being able to like feel like I'm actually making a difference in someone's life just by just by going out and executing plays. >> Who have you talked to with uh you know, football side or family side to kind of give you some perspective on you balancing the football side and family side as well? >> Say that again, sorry. >> Anybody you talked to in football or family to kind of give you more perspective on how to kind of you know, handle fatherhood and going forward now? >> Uh I don't think I really I mean, I got a billion people to give me advice, I guess. Uh but no, I wasn't in particular seeking a bunch at that point. I feel like I'd done all the I'm never going to be prepared right for fatherhood. No one ever feels totally prepared, so I guess just being content in the fact that I can only control the things I can control and and letting everything else fall into place. >> When it comes to football, we've seen you all over the field. What do you like about Kory, his offense, and how he wants to use you this year? >> Yeah, I love the multiplicity and just the all the different things we get to do. Um and it's fun. Like we're all everybody's giving their best shot to try to like I want to prove that we move the ball best in base. I'm sure the receivers want to prove that we move the ball best in 11 personnel and tight ends want 12 personnel. Some of us want 13 personnel, 14 personnel, so uh it's just fun competing with everybody and trying to prove that you're the guy that should be one of the best 11 on the field. >> We saw you and Jared Ivey involved in a big hit on special teams. That's something you really can't do out here in practice. How valuable are those kickoff reps and punt team reps in the games to get that full contact in? >> Yeah, it's super valuable cuz obviously, like you said, we don't want to go running over our under turners or or putting our own guys blocking in harm's way or something. You'll have to pull up early, so it's fun when you actually get to go unleash it on another team. >> First one, how does that feel? First one of the >> Yeah, it felt great. It felt great. >> As as sort of the de facto captain of the special teams, how how much pride did you take last year in sort of that was such a key part in every game? I mean, the kickoff return and then the divisional game, what happened in the championship game, Jason Myers, some people thought he'd be MVP in the Super Bowl kind of thing. I mean, it was that everybody seemed to really do something on special teams down the stretch there. >> Yeah, absolutely. We took a ton of pride in it and and just treating our roles like it's an offensive and defensive role. And like we're running our own plays out there and we have our own calls and every time you go in the game like something different could be called, so you got to be totally prepared and know, all right, this is the play that's called, this is what my guy's going to try to do to me. Um and Jay puts us in really good situations to be prepared, um which I love. >> There's a lot of babies now in that locker room. Uh is there like a community of Seahawk babies now in and off the field that they kind of makes things a little different? >> Uh it don't make it too different. The moms are all um our wives, I guess, are all super close here, so it's cool that group just how they rally and support each other and love each other and I don't think the babies have changed anything, but they definitely added some new responsibility to the group. >> Were you able to see Hard Knocks outside where they showed the scene where you had to leave at halftime and everything? >> Mhm. I'm actually not watching the Hard Knocks till till after. I got too many things going on already. >> They did show a little clip like your teammates, you know, congratulating you when you're leaving. What was that moment like of like you're leaving locker room, your teammates are all giving you love in the middle of the game there? >> Yeah, it was super kind of them. The it's like such a unique thing cuz it's like I'm like, holy cow, I'm about to go have a kid. I'm freaking out in my head trying to get ready to get in the car and uh everybody come show me some love was very sweet of them. >> Are you pretty much uh like exclusively working at fullback now or you still doing like stuff in the tight end rooms? >> Uh the the probably the biggest thing I pride myself on is multiplicity. So, I want to be able to do everything a tight end does and everything a full back does and I want to prove that I'm capable of that, too, cuz it is a lot of responsibility. So, um no, I think I'm I want to do a little bit of everything still. >> Brady, with Robbie's injury, you're number one up on that spot now. Like, how comfortable do you feel with full back in totality? Obviously, you did that last year, too. Like, taking that role now and running with it. >> Yeah, I definitely feel a lot more comfortable this year after having a year of of learning and just understanding what it looks like to play that position in the Rebel. Um so, it things feel a lot uh I don't know if easier is the right word, but my mental process pre-snap is a lot smoother this year in understanding what the defense is showing me and what I need to do on that play. >> The joint practices, just the benefits of that as you guys hit the road, kind of bonding and all that sort of thing? >> Yeah, it's awesome cuz there's a lot like most all the time in practice, you're not wanting to finish your own teammates to the ground and and get pancakes and stuff. Like, you want to take care of each other, so it's fun when you go against another team and you get to truly kind of unleash and and just open up that extra little notch, if you will. >> Anything else? >> Thank you, Brady. Thank you, Brady. >> Yeah, thanks, guys.

title: Grey Zabel: "We Love Going Against Competition And We Don't Stray Away From It" | Seattle Seahawks
text: Good afternoon. >> How are you doing? >> Good. >> When you were a rookie last year, you guys went on the road for joint practice. What did that kind of extra time on the road with the team do for you in terms of bonding and getting to know everybody as a newcomer to the team? >> Yeah, I mean, when we went to Green Bay last year, that's kind of when we realized how special of a team that we had. Went there, I thought we had a fairly good joint practice versus them, and then you obviously get to have their rookie talent show to kind of bring the team together and and have fun and and have the joys of being a football team, and then just kind of brought us together and showed us kind of our first road trip together to to kind of how things work and and how to operate and what to expect. >> What's your best memory of the rookie talent show >> Man, I I think Fed's mariachi band has got to be up there. That was that was very impressive [snorts] and brought the whole scene and everything with it, so probably that. >> What did you do again? >> Just [snorts] spit some bars, sang some Future. Got after it, you know. Day one install. >> Future one of your favorites? >> Yeah, it's just KYP, know your personnel, and go out there and and do your best. >> Last night on the tractor back home? >> Yeah, yeah, sure. >> Where do you Where do you feel like you you guys' running game is right now when you're out there on the field and the practices and everything? obviously there's a lot to improve across the entire board, but I think it showed really good signs of how we're kind of projecting and and getting better every single day. And when you're going against a front like ours, it's you you find out your deficiencies and what you need to get better at a very rapid rate in practice. So, at the end of the day, you can always improve and never finished product. >> How do you think this joint practice will help you guys improve on that? >> Yeah, I think it just maybe a different scheme, different front, different type of defense and how they play certain formations and certain run games and stuff. So, it'll kind of give us a different view on things and then obviously it just kind of shows you a little marker stick of where we're at and how we need to improve and and and give us a good kind of spotlight on what to expect come the season. >> Did it I was going to say you guys obviously you guys you guys go against the best in the NFL all the time here, but Jeffery Simmons is really good, too. And you'll be going up against him, too. I just Getting getting that kind of experience in something like this, how would that be? >> Yeah, I mean it'll be awesome. I mean he's one of the best to ever play three tech. So, he's a guy that it's one of those deals we we'd love going against competition. We don't stray away from it. We want to be the best we can be. So, you got to go and compete against the best and I think it'll be awesome to go out there and compete Friday and and possibly Sunday against him and then go and and and kind of see what you're up against and and improve and get better and compete. >> A few of your line mates have talked about John Benton having kind of that old school coaching approach, but away from the field having some different ways that he reaches players. Google Earth in particular is something that he had mentioned like What what have you learned about him over the course of the last year plus in terms of away from the field and how he is able to approach you guys? >> Yeah, I think the best way to describe it is there's a method to his madness. The stuff we do to to bond and get to know each other and take breaks from meetings and get back to learning and all that stuff and how he coaches is there's a method to to everything that he does. I mean he's one of the best offensive line coaches that I've been around and in the NFL to say the least. So, he's done a super high level and and taken us to places that we didn't even think were possible. Um so it's one of those deals where you just got to keep your nose to the grindstone and just trust him and trust his process and and understand that he's coaching you cuz he loves you and he wants the best out of you and and and you got to understand that. >> Looking back, what did he do for your rookie year? To have him as your coach in particular your rookie season, how did that help? >> Yeah. Um if you'd have saw me during OTAs my rookie year, you you would have said, "What is this guy doing?" At the Seattle Seahawks. And then just him coaching me and helping me understand the game in a different lens um and just staying on the the process of of process over results and um ended up being a okay rookie year and but there's a lot to build on and he's understood that and he continues coach me every single day and you got to give where credit is due to to the unbelievable coach, person, leader um just is the best. >> How were you a mess your rookie year in particular? >> Yeah, I mean when you're going against some of the best and you're you're new to the the NFL, it's uh you uh you get get taken to the woodshed quite oftenly. So that uh yeah, but at the end it's it's what uh during the week doesn't have to look pretty. You just got to be there on Sunday. >> Do you remember any one moment Mike talks about rookies in the fog last year when that fog lifted at all or was it any certain game or is just a continued improvement process for you? >> Yeah, I think I think you said it perfectly like just continue to improve day after day, week after week. And then you get into the regular season and then the game every single week starts to slow down a little bit more and more and then by the end of the day you're you're thinking you're out going out there on Sunday and playing some of your best ball cuz you gotten every look uh throughout the week and you understand what what the opponent's going to do, the the looks, the the blitzes, the the types of coverages that kind of show things and then when you get there on Sunday the fog kind of lifts and you can play fast and free cuz you know you've kind of put in the work and the preparation for it. >> What are you learning about Brian Flores as a coach or as a person? >> Just seems like the man.com. Uh He's a good dude. Unbelievable coach. Love his his run first mentality and we're going to enjoy it. He's doing an unbelievable job so far and I know he kind of demands excellence and I love that out of a coach and he's going to hold us to a standard and and not waver. >> You mentioned the bond that you guys have in the offensive line. The the fine system that you guys have in place. How have you seen that change this year being in year two? I saw Jaylen Sundell was taking a video, so I'm wondering if that may have been a part of your guys' system there. >> Yeah, no. Um Yeah, it's It's one of those deals we It's uh we have a fine system and and obviously talking to guys, that'll be a fine. Um but at the end of the day, it's it's something we do to have fun, keep it lighthearted in the O-line room, um and and kind of keep everything happy-go-lucky. And then at the end of the year, you normally take an O-line trip. Last year, I think we just kind of donated throughout staff, throughout the team and stuff cuz it was middle of February and we weren't really looking to schedule an O-line trip. Everyone wanted to go home after Super Bowl, so it's one of those deals I'd gladly do that year after year and this year, I'm not getting fined as much not being a rookie, but yeah, we still get Yeah, Port Bow. >> break cuz he's the only rookie. You're not doing Port Bow. >> [laughter] >> No. The Bow Show does not get a break. >> How did he grade out on his hype man duties? >> Lot to improve, but it's it's you got to get through the storm. You got to get through the fog in the in those duties and and luckily, there's I don't think there's any more fan practices, but uh it's one of those deals you just got to wear it on the chin and it's never going to be good enough. >> How do you think he'll do in the rookie talent show? >> Yeah, I don't know. Wasn't very promising the first one back in OTAs, but I try and give him pointers and help all that stuff and we'll go from there. >> Did the old lineman put him up to the MC gig or is that Did you guys >> No, last year it was JB's idea to to do the rookie hype machine for the fans and stuff and it was kind of one of those deals that first day of fan practice he told us in meetings and we're all kind of looking around and then it was just one of those deals you just had to take it and run with it and it was it was good from there. >> All right, guys. >> Appreciate you, guys. >> Thanks, guys.

title: Matt Hasselbeck breaks down Ty Simpson and Mendoza's debuts, Jeremiyah Love's injury | The Herd
text: And with that, Matt Hasselbeck is joining us. So, I got to start with this. As somebody who played in the NFL for 18 years, how do you view preseason? What does it mean to you? >> I I always thought it was really important. And I I understand that I was a sixth-round pick and a guy that needed preseason games. My first year in the NFL, I was with the Green Bay Packers. We actually played five preseason games because we played in the American Bowl in Tokyo against the Kansas City Chiefs. And I needed it. I mean, I needed those reps. I needed those opportunities to make the team. And the funny thing is is myself and a few of the guys in my draft class, we didn't even make the team. Um we were guys like me were put on the practice squad for a while and then eventually made the team. So, developmentally, I think it's really important. I would also say this that I don't I've never heard anyone say this this year. There's 21 new offensive coordinators in the NFL. These coaches need preseason. These coaches need to get the mechanics of who's on the headset, who's in the booth, who's on the sideline. I remember Mike McDonald, who's an amazing head coach, had never been a head coach. Had never been with that group of coaches before. I remember after his first preseason game, it was a debacle on the headsets. They had to work out the [laughter] kinks. And so, like even the best of the best need preseason. Tom Brady was playing when I was playing. He loved the preseason. Uh my my dad played with Phil Simms. That dude Bill Parcells would have him in the fourth quarter of games in the preseason. I think there's value in it. Uh joint practices have kind of replaced it for coaches because you can keep them away from the quarterback, quote unquote. But uh but some some form of like the best versus the best in a game-like situation is really important for evaluation. >> No, I and I also thought as I was watching, you know, the Rams and I'm seeing Dean Connors, an undrafted running back, catching balls out of the backfield. I'm like, "God, if I was a general manager, I'm like, if McVay likes him, if he if he gets let go." I mean, do you ever remember playing with anybody in your career that maybe was undrafted or a late round pick, Matt, and you're like, "Oh my god, this guy's really good." >> 100%. I mean, really good. There were guys that were uncoverable. And and almost like, "Hey, let's let's hide him from from people. Like, we don't want them to know." Or a guy would have a great game against somebody and you know, pregame the scouts, what are they doing? They're just handing around talking to the other team's scouts and like, "Hey, we need an extra D-lineman." And they're like, "Uh you guys look like you need an extra wide receiver. Uh that guy looks good for you. This guy looks, you know, hey, let's do a trade." Or uh you know, maybe it's like you talk about him, you love him up, you trust your guy and then he's on the waiver wire and you sign the guy. 100%. That happens all the time. And and I think even coaches even say that, especially especially special teams coaches going into a preseason game like, "Hey, this is an audition for us. It's also an audition for the rest of the league." Um I don't want to say you're a mercenary like a hired gun that way cuz you're a team, but uh but it's a real thing. It it's a real thing that is talked about in in locker rooms. >> I thought Fernando Mendoza, again, it's a couple of drives. My take is he's big. Here's what I know from college. Big, smart, accurate, and he's not a dink and dunk guy. He almost at Cal threw the ball down the field enough to get interceptions. I like what I saw. Do you take anything from it? >> Yeah, I I I'm going to the conviction of Clint Kubiak is going to be tested because he looks the part. I mean, he the third and eights, third and eights, third and sevens, third he was so cool, so in control. Um I think there's so much to like there. Now, he's got to learn to protect himself a little bit more and I think that's one of the many reasons why why Kirk Cousins should be the starting quarterback this year. I mean, I said it to you a long time ago. Kirk Cousins is going to be the starting quarterback week one. And and they're going they're going to protect their investment of Fernando Mendoza. They know how good he is, but they're going to build the roster, they're going to get better as they go hopefully at wide receiver, they're going to solidify the offensive line. This This young quarterback's going to realize he's not at Indiana anymore. He can't just take off and run and take hits. He can't do the spin move on third down and and take an unnecessary hit. He's going to watch from Kirk Cousins who does it, in my opinion, does the little things as good as anybody. And uh I think it's a great thing for the Raiders if they if they stick to their conviction. >> By the way, he pats the ball a little bit and I was like, I got to ask Hasselbeck about that. I think you can get into habits. I think that's nerves. I saw him a couple of times pat the ball and I'm like, is that him or is that nerves? >> So, here's the thing on patting the ball. Sometimes it can be like a binky, a pacifier that you know as a toddler you think you need it and you really don't need it. It's just a comfort thing. But at the same time, it could be a bad habit, but it also can be a weapon that you use. Joe Montana, Tom Brady, some of the best, they would pat the ball as they would go through their progression and it would almost make it harder for the zone defenders that are watching their eyes and they're watching them take their left hand off the ball. So, if you're using it to your advantage, it's a good thing. Most young quarterbacks don't use it as an advantage. It's just the binky and you need to, you know, the binky fairy needs to come in the middle of the night and you need to lose the binky in most cases. >> Now, I think I didn't think the Giants looked great. They didn't play their left tackle. I actually think between Skataboo, I think Emeka Egbuka from Notre Dame at 6'4, I thought he was the best third round pick. If Neighbors comes back, I think the kid from Isaiah Likely from Baltimore, I think he's a real player, can be a volume receiver. I like them. But it does bother me. There's a brand now. There is a trend that uh once again Jackson Dart gets smoked and he's in the tent. Now, we can immediately say, well, the running back missed his block, but it wasn't a blind side thing. To me, I watched it and I'm like, "Okay, dude, you were in that five times last year. You got smoked again." I do feel like there are quarterbacks. I've seen this with Geno Smith. I'm like, "You get hit too hard, too often. Do some guys just not see it?" >> I I have no wish I love Jackson Dart. He's He's fun to watch. He plays a lot like Josh Allen to me. I I've no problem with how he plays the game. I have a problem how he lays on the ground. Dude, body language, man. Like you lay on the ground like you were you were dead. It was like a It was like a knockout punch. You wonder why you were in the blue tent. You were in the blue tent cuz you stayed on the ground like you were sleeping. That's why you were in the blue tent. Like they they probably called timeout. And so I I love him. I think he's got a bright future. I'm I'm a fan. But like don't let him see you sweat. Don't let the defense know like you're probably mad somebody missed their block, you know, I would say it kind of was a blind side block to the blind side hit to the right, but but get up. Like I always tried I always tried to get up and I hit like that. I always tried to get up before the guy that sacked me. Like that was like in my mind. You know, I watched Brett Favre do it. I thought it was I thought it was the greatest passive-aggressive move ever. Andrew Luck would get up and congratulate the guy. Hey, great that was a great hit. Good job. You know, like don't let him know that it bothered you. You laid out there like you know, you were going to stop the fight. So I you know, you want to solve that problem, just get up, man. Get up quick. That's that's all you got to do. >> Okay, so Arizona, two of their top four picks are already out for the season. So I felt I know with injuries and I kind of felt like they were trying to like win the day. Like Jeremiah Love, 23 snaps, 14 touches. I'm like, "Guys, I know you paid him 53 large in a signing bonus. I know everybody else is hurt. You're not winning the division. Do not get him hurt. It It I watched that game and I'm sitting there watching thinking, "Get him out of the game." Cuz he took a shot on a spin move, and I'm like, "Get him out of the game, or am I being overprotective here?" >> No, I mean, but some of it he's got to protect himself. You know, you mentioned the spin move. I mean, I'm I'm too old to know this. I think it's the B button when you're playing like video games now, the spin move. He was hitting the spin move way too much. I mean, everything is a spin move. It was like he was trying to do the uh the Saquon Barkley reverse jump. Like he was setting it up or something. So, some of it I think it's just like, "Hey, get downhill." You know, the the the You don't need to fight for that extra 1 in, you know, sometimes. Understand that it is a preseason game. We want you to get north and south. You know, I had a I was around a coach one time. He What would he say? He'd say, "Hey guys, we want to we want to be on 405 or I-5, not I-90. You know what I mean? Like, let's go this way, [laughter] not that way." Um there there's there's an element of that with the spin move. Um but yeah, you got to protect your investment. I would say this though, it's good that he got dinged up with the ankle early in the preseason rather than late in the preseason. Because this is something that you know, I don't think will will affect him going um once the regular season starts. >> So, I have I tend to believe when it comes to quarterbacks, your coaches will tell me what they think of you by what you can handle. Right? Like I mean, Mahomes in his prime, like Andy Reid's like, "If you throw 44 times, whereas in Philadelphia, you can tell they feel more comfortable if Jalen throws 26 times. I watched Ty Simpson. They threw it 25 times. Screens, seams, deep, like they just emptied the playbook with him. And I was like, "Well, that tells me either they wanted to see stuff or they trusted him, maybe." >> I It tells me that Sean McVay is the absolute best play-caller when it comes to being quarterback friendly. That dude is amazing. And Ty Simpson looked awesome. But it was turn your brain off plays in the whole first half. It was a naked bootleg, naked bootleg screen. Like for a quarterback, naked bootlegs are the easiest play you could mentally the easiest play that you could run. You We've all been doing them since high school, and that's what it was. High completion percentage, fits into the run game, to O-line friendly, you're on the road, you're backed up. That's what it was. Go watch his Go watch all of his passes early in the game, all naked bootlegs. And then in the fourth quarter, he's out there just playing ball. He looked like Dan Marino, slicing and dicing, like seeing balls and uh getting through his progression number five. Like it was really impressive, but he got comfortable. He like the game, he like got a lather going in his pads. He took a couple uh I wouldn't even say hits, they were like pushes. Um so to me, that was a clinic by Sean McVay of how to handle a young quarterback. So many coaches in the NFL get it wrong, they don't know what they're doing, they want to sound smart, they want to look Look how smart I am to all their peers. Sean McVay's like, I don't care. I'm going to run high school Harry plays over and over really, [laughter] really well. And and our quarterback's going to be comfortable, and everyone's going to be like, hey, we're not even We're not even talking about this dude. This dude's a rock-solid number two, you know, probably the heir apparent now. We're good. Aw- awesome job by Sean McVay and Ty Simpson. >> So there are there are I tend to really like players who are workmanlike and durable. And I like DJ Moore a lot, but I did think Chicago getting Rome Odunze, Luther Burden, Colston Loveland, and Caleb Young. I thought, you know what? Generationally, DJ's the veteran. Let's just grow with the kids. They got a young tackle at left tackle, young tackle at right tackle. It's a very young offense. It might take his DJ Moore's kind of aged out of this group. But he never misses a start, he's a total pro. You don't see him in trouble. He's just a a very durable guy. So when he goes to Buffalo, because his numbers had gone down slightly, and my argument is that's because Chicago's got so many good young weapons at, you know, tight end and running back, I watched him and Josh Allen and my take was they're just smart veteran guys. It'll It's not going to take that long. You tell me. When you got an older receiver, how long did it take you? >> I mean, you brought this up last week. I I I did not like seeing DJ Moore leave Chicago. I I think I mean, respect. I have two words that would come to mind when I hear DJ Moore's name. I think respect. Uh the defense respects that dude. They play off of that guy. They do not They They don't want to tackle him. They don't want to cover him. And then the other word is smile. Did you see the smile on Josh Allen's face when he gets asked questions about DJ Moore? He's like, "Yeah, this is the guy I want to get it to him early and often." Like he's a weapon. He's a problem for people. Uh they're they're going to be a really really fun offense to watch. I think DJ Moore is going to be great for Josh Allen. I also know, having been around it to answer your question about veteran receivers, they elevate the professionalism, the production, like all all the great stuff you're looking for of younger players in that in that room. Like you you see you watch the the Seahawks on Hard Knocks. Like it's it's impossible not to see the impact that Cooper Kupp is having on the room. >> Yeah. >> So to think that DJ Moore is not going to have an impact on Keon Coleman, like on when plays break down, like it's going to happen. I mean, it's it's such a good thing for the Bills. I think in a weird way this could be a win-win situation for the Bears and the Bills, but if I had to give the win to somebody, I like I like this for the Bills a lot. >> That was funny. I went I went to the Bears Cleveland game and I went downstairs on the field cuz I'm you know, VIP level guy. So I get down on the field and I was telling my producers, like I'm I'm I'm You're bigger than me. You're a pro athlete, right? I'm 6'2", buck 90, pretty ripped, but whatever. So I go on the field. I go on the field and I'm sitting there with a buddy and I'm like, "Every fan should go on the field." The size of defensive ends now and tight ends. I mean, the Stanford rookie for Chicago, this tight end is like 6'5, 250. He's like 22 years old and I'm like he looks like a lumberjack. >> [laughter] >> When you When you When you go on the field, do you ever think to yourself, you know what? I'm glad I retired. I think players are getting bigger. >> I You know, I remember at the end of my career I'd play in the preseason. Andrew Luck was the starter. So, I'm like 40 years old and I'm playing with the twos and you get these guys that you know, you mentioned the tight end from Chicago. Like they they look like a created player on Madden. Like their their biceps are like the everything looks like It's like, man, if that dude hits me on a blindside, I could be in trouble. Like I don't know how good these dudes are that are playing. I don't know if they're great football players, but they give you that like um I remember when Brock Lesnar came back into the NFL and it was like, whoa. What if he does one of those like WWE [laughter] wrestling moves on me and the like that would be bad news, man. That would be bad news. So, yeah, there's an element of that, but uh at the same time like I would just say um you know, there's some bad body dudes that are great football players, too. So, it takes all shapes and sizes and and and that's that's one of the good things, but total respect for the these guys are getting bigger, younger, and faster as they come out of college. >> impressive. Great seeing you, buddy, as always. >> Yeah, see you, Colin.
