text: Morning, how's everybody doing? >> Morning. >> All right. >> Hey, you guys have spent a lot of time and resources on both lines the last couple of years. Do you you feel like this is the year that it coalesces? And how important is it that this is the year it coalesces? >> Right. Uh we have we put a lot of resources into these players and draft picks. Uh we signed them in in free agency as well and uh we want to be strong there always, you know, you build through the line of scrimmage, you control the line of scrimmage, you got a chance to win a lot of games, you know. Um it starts up front. Uh we want to be big, we want to be strong. Um I said in my first year I got here we're going to be able to impose our will on people and be able to break them in second half of games. >> think you're better positioned to do that now, you think? >> so with the growth and development of what we have. Uh the players that we brought in here, we're bigger on our defensive line. We're excited about our depth. Uh we like our offensive line, the depth we have there. We're fired up guys, we've seen the growth out of some of our draft picks. So they got to continue to grow and continue to get better. And um you know, they're young. And uh we got a good mix of youth and veterans on defense as well. So um you know, we'll see how they do. We got another test coming up Friday night and next week and we want to see continued growth and development from those offensive and defensive linemen. >> On the topic of depth across the board, do you think the roster's deep enough that you can keep all four of the backs if that's what I want to do? >> That's that'll play itself out and that'll be up to Coach McCarthy. Uh Coach McCarthy, Omar, Arthur will make that decision on that. Um we'll watch that play itself out. So we got another test like I said Friday night coming up, next week in Buffalo. We'll see how these guys do today. The one thing that's great about training camp is you learn something about your team every day, something new. You see how guys handle different situations. Our coaches are doing a great job of putting players in different situations, different circumstances, see how they handle it, see how they react, and see how they perform. >> And then looking back to last year when you did draft Drew, what was the one thing that stood out to you that said this guy could be a starter this year? >> Well, I think you know, first of all you look at him, he's a big quarterback, right? He's got a strong arm. You go to practice at Penn State, you watch the ball, it jumps out of his hand. He could attack every part of the field with the arm power that he has. Then you get to know him, the intelligence he has. Uh that factored in with Coach McCarthy and his track record of developing quarterbacks. You know, personally, I saw firsthand in New Orleans when I was down there uh 26 years ago in 2000, Mike was our offensive coordinator. Uh him and you know, Frank Cignetti was on the staff, too, and I saw the work and the development they did with Jake Delhomme. And how Jake grew and developed there. And you know, he was able to leave in in free agency and then watch him go to Carolina and how he, you know, elevated Carolina, took him to Super Bowl. But Mike did a great job down there. I was stopped with the growth and the development of Jake Delhomme. >> Will Will Levis Will How How did you What stood out about him to you? >> I think Will, just how he handled, you know, he picked himself off the mat the after the Ohio State-Michigan game. Um you know, there was they lost at home and you know, he played his best football in the most important time of the year in the playoffs. He elevated his team, he elevated his play. Uh the moment was never too big. He was composed, he was poised, much like we saw the other night in the two-minute drill where he executed that, you know, to perfection. So, um you know, we'll see them play again this week. Excited to see those guys go out and handle a game situation and you know, it was a good start last week. We want to see them continue to grow and develop. >> And you guys have invested a lot in in defensive line depth as well. Right guys We've heard a lot about Rubio and how well he's done in camp. Elijah Black seems like he's one of your guys. What have you thought about the investment you guys have put in the depth of your defensive line? >> Right. Well, you know, the two the two places I've been where they won Super Bowls is we had two waves come in. Um Philadelphia, Baltimore, we had two waves of defensive line and you want it it it's nice to have that. It keeps your guys fresh so that when you get in December, January football, you're you're able to surge. You know, your guys are fresh. You can roll guys through and you're able to surge into the December, January football and hopefully into the playoffs, so that's why we invest there. >> Andy, you saw a lot from him when you drafted him out of Michigan. What What might be different with him? What What do you notice from him maybe any different this year than previous? >> I think you know, it's year two with Aaron, so the relationship, you can see the chemistry on the field. You guys have been up there to watch them. He's playing fast, he's playing with confidence. He's winning and I think physically he's grown, too. You know, he looks stronger out there, so it's been a good start for him and we want to you know, see him continue to grow and and develop and watch him Friday night, watch him out here today and and next week and you know, see see him keep elevating, so you know, we're excited where he's at, but we know we got a long way to go. >> You guys have a lot of players from Iowa on this roster. In other years it was Georgia or Ohio State. Is there something that keeps you going back to those schools year after year? Coaches or strength coaches or anything like that? >> Well, yeah, I think you know, Kirby Smart and the program he runs, you've been out to practice, they run there and the success they've obviously had in that in that program like you know, Daelin Everett, I two years ago I went to the Texas game and they they're playing there and it's a huge match up national game and you know, they went in there and won and they physically imposed their will and it started with Daelin Everett. I remember early in the game he hit a blitz off the edge and hit the quarterback, sacked, forced fumble, turnover and that really sparked it. He's always had a knack for playing big in big games, SEC championships, he played a lot of football there. But I think it's a lot of the way that you know, they they get guys in the program. You've come out of those programs, man, you're buying guys, you've been coached hard, physical, you're tough. Same way with Iowa, coach Ferentz is one of the best, you know, that ever do it all time winningest coach in Big Ten history. They have a history there of linemen, players, good football players that end up being good pros, so you know, it's just worked out that way, but you know, we acknowledge also the programs and Notre Dame, too. You know, what coach Freeman's doing up there with that program, man, it's exciting. So, you know, it factors in. You know, guys that come out of those programs, they've been coached well, they've been coached hard. They're tough, they're usually disciplined and buying guys. >> And as you've found this over the years, where have you, at the end of training camp, at the end of the preseason, where are teams still hunting the most? Is it secondary? Is it O-line? Where do you find teams at the end of the preseason still scouring the most to help before the regular season starts? >> I We always look at it and since I've been doing it, offensive line, people are looking for wide tight ends. So, you know, it's it's a league that we invest in the offensive line, so we're heavy there and we come in with good depth because I think offensive line offensive line, corners, defensive backs, they tend to suffer a lot of attrition during the year. Your depth is going to be tested. It's going to be tested at every position, but those in particular, you know, you want to make sure you have numbers. It's like like I said at one time, I heard it from Rex Ryan, if you have two corners, you need three. If you have three, you need four. If you have four, you need five. So, you can never have enough. >> With with Maxie on the tour, what do you remember about some of your early impressions of him and when you have a player like that that doesn't have a long history of playing football, how does that factor into your evaluation and in the projection of what they might become? >> That's a good question. So, he's an interesting case. Uh last year for me, I went out to the school visit and I saw them play uh TCU at home on a Friday night. I didn't go to Ireland. I did a a double header there and then came back here and watched Pitt and Louisville to see the the Bell kid, the receiver. But, I think you notice first and foremost his size and the movement skill. Um you see the background of it. He's he's relatively new to football. He started over 30 games at Arizona State, but like he's built different, he moves different. Um and you saw the composure he had in pass pro. You know, not being stressed, easy mover, the power he had. Then he goes down to the Senior Bowl and he gets better every day and we thought he was the best one down there. He competed. Um you know, again, it was just putting it all together and you saw the ascension and he kept rising and rising and then we did the the Zoom interview with him myself and coach Campion and just really impressive guy to talk to. You know, he he loves the brotherhood of the offensive line, running the football, pass pro, like he came across as a guy that you could connect with and and a football lover, so um you know, that was that was the process with him in short and and our scouts did a good job going in there, mining the the information, the background on him, so at the end of the day we we had a comfort level, you know, and we're excited to draft him and excited to have him here. >> Did he run into safety since the start of training camp? Would you say that's a position you're still hoping for some depth to establish himself? >> Yeah, I I think you just you never want to be short, you know, at a position. That's our job is to make sure that our coaching staff they have enough players and you know, when you have depth it breeds competition and competition brings out the best, so um as we say the cream rises to the top and we'll see how that that position goes, but it's a very spirited group, you know, bringing in in uh Jaquan Brisker, you know, he's brought a lot of energy to the group and it's been contagious and I think you guys have seen it at practice, they feed off one another, the DBs, the safeties. I mean, shoot, we don't even Jaylen Ramsey hasn't been out there yet. You know the player he is and the energy and intensity he brings, so um it's been good to see. It's a fun group. Um they're getting a lot of guys are getting a chance to play due to due to injuries and uh we're watching them grow and develop and coaches are doing a great job putting them in different situations and circumstances to see how they react to it. >> Speaking of bringing energy, Landon Roberts brought that in the first few days and >> I think familiarity and the depth and and more competition and uh when he played here, the guy was a warrior for us, he played hurt, um played physical, played downhill and uh you know, he he just just talking with him, we we always stayed in touch. Um you know, when he became a free agent we stayed in touch I should say. Um and just it was it was an opportunity, so credit to Omar uh pull the trigger on it and bring another guy in here and you know, having more depth at that position. >> And Andy, you guys recently just signed your fourth member of the 2023 draft class. Obviously, I'm sure there's priority to look to sign Joey Porter Jr. Just how much, I guess, of an emphasis are you guys trying to put on that right now, knowing what the market is in the >> So, you know, with regard to his contract situation, I'm going to defer to Omar. He handles He's the point guy on all contract um you know, extensions and any issues along those lines, but you know, it it's good. It's like we want to build through the draft, and you know, ideally you want to draft, develop, and resign. And um you know, credit to Omar and Cole getting the deals done with, you know, Keanu, um Nick Herbig, and uh Darnell, you know, to have those guys, and it's I think it's a good reflection on what we did there and our scouts and you know, the player development FY, and you know, the the three things that go into it is, you know, player acquisition is key, number one, right? It's critical. But player development and coaching absolutely matter. Those are the three pillars to really, you know, have a successful program, and um I think you're seeing them develop out here now and grow, and I think, you know, there's some more guys coming down the road, you know, hopefully, you know, keep adding, keep layering those drafts, and keep building, and you know, build building from within, so. >> How much Andy, how much >> Last two. >> How much of an emphasis do you guys put into that development part before scouting players to see who's coachable on top of like, you know, their raw skills, what they're doing in the game, etc.? >> We put a lot of emphasis. It's football character. I mean, football character matters. You got to have the talent first and foremost, but then it's it it's a football character, the ability to learn, ability to take criticism. You know, one of the things I I learned from uh Mr. Nunn when I was here a long time ago was, and it's it's universal, it's timeless, is it How does How do they handle criticism? Right? Coachability. Can he take criticism, let it roll you know, listen to the message, and get better from it, grow from it, you know, so. Um we think we've you know, we've we've emphasized that. Um the players we brought in, their football character has been a big priority along with their talent, so. We'll continue to do so. >> Andy, then you mentioned imposing your will. How does a fullback help you guys do that offensively? And has Riley been what you thought through this point? >> Yeah, I I think you're seeing Riley grow grow each day. You know, the development. Like I was I was with Kyle Juszczyk in in Baltimore and I saw him grow and develop each day. Took him a while to learn it. He was a He was a move guy as well at Harvard and you know, he had to learn the blocking and you know, what is it? Like six, seven Pro Bowls later. So, you know, Riley's out here. He's he's smart, right? He's really smart. He's versatile. He's got a strong frame. Shown up. I think he's getting a feel for it. You know, at the fullback, you know, he's versatile. Just seeing him at the Big Ten Championship against Ohio State in the in the the dirty work he did in that game, the conversion catches he made. He was a key part of their offensive offensive success that night. So, you know, it's it's good, you know, and hopefully he keeps getting better and better and better, so.

What did you see on the field that you might have seen as well during training? >> Uh, Mason has great command of the offense. I mean, just pure on the field game day. Um, he's he's very experienced. Uh, he's he's strong personality um in the in the locker room. I really like this command, understanding the offense. you know, he's he's been through a number of systems. Uh he's been asked to do things differently for how how we believe the quarterback position has played. He's done an excellent job. >> Mike Caleb Johnson hasn't had a ton of opportunities to run the ball. Will he get more and what do you need to see from him? >> I hope so. If the guy calling the plays, just would run the ball more. I think I'd help him out. Uh so, we'll just continue to work that way. Um but yeah, he'll I mean, he'll play I mean, he'll play, you know, he'll play Friday night and then hopefully play a bunch up in Buffalo. We do. We want We really want to focus on the younger part of our team uh and give these guys a chance to to make our spot. >> What is Eli Heiden shown you as far as you know? >> Sorry. >> What has Eli Heiden shown you so far? I know he was out for some time. >> Yeah, I mean I think the biggest thing for me with Eli, you know, he missed so much time with the injury so it was good to see him get out there and I just think he, you know, hopefully with this, you know, we had a little more rest than we anticipated, but you know, hopefully he'll benefit from that, get his legs back the way, you know, they were before the injury. So I just want to see him take a step get more com you know more comfortable particularly in the run game see see the burst that he he has shown in the on the practice field. So like to see him get more opportunities >> and testing more of the both Will and Drew will they get see both see like expanded parts of the playbook just to kind of further test them. >> Now our our playbook and in the way we're approaching this game is more about what's what what concepts are our players are most comfortable with. You know, there's I mean, we we watch the Jets, you know, their first preseason game, just have a general understanding of where they are and their install, but we're not putting a lot of energy into them, you know, because if be honest, I it doesn't matter. I've always approached preseason this way. I I really not concerned with the who the team is and what they're doing. I I I want to see our guys run the offense, especially the quarterbacks. You know, when we install concepts, everything's it's proactive adjustment. They have the tools to to to do what they need to do regardless of the defense. So, and you know, it's the same same same on defense. We we want to get our guys lined up. You know, we want to win the pre- snap. I want their eyes in the right place. You know, we want to play better fundamentally, and we want to, you know, run and go get the football. >> What did you want Will to work on the most up that first game? And where have you seen him perhaps improve even over? >> Oh, I think Will Will has taken steps, you know, throughout camp. I just, you know, just maybe get off to a little better start than he did last time and and and really, you know, a couple of those plays were weren't really his fault as far as what what happened, but you got to you got to react to to negative situations. Play preseason football is great for young quarterbacks on so many fronts. I mean, obviously, they get to play, you want to see them command the offense, take the play entry, you know, get up the line. if they get in trouble, they have a proactive reason that, you know, reasoning to to to do with it, but also if something goes wrong, if the route's not the way it should be or it's not doesn't happen or the right tackle doesn't do the right thing, to be able to react to that and and not be surprised by it. So, and I thought he did a good he had two plays in the game where something went wrong and he, you know, he he reacted accordingly and and throwing the ball away is a win. I mean, throw throwaways are, you know, uh when something negative happens, you throw the ball away. Second and 10 is fine. You know, we we can deal with punting is good sometimes, you know, in a game. So, just playing with that discipline. So, I I thought he definitely improved in that area. He didn't really I can't say he improved it because that's the first game he played in, you know. So, um so there were there was a lot of little things like that that were evident in both Will and Drew's play. >> Drew Dorilla talked about that too after the game, you know, play Drew Allen. Drew there was a play in the red zone where he said, >> "You got to speak up. They're grinding over here with the ball drills. You know, that that's going to happen in the game. You know, you know, there's a there's eight plays a game, you know, that statistically, you know, that a quarterback's going to have to move his feet, you know, in a potential extended play. Um, I think, you know, you you get these rookies, uh, you watch them go through the helmets and, you know, Shell's phase and, you know, through the, uh, you know, the offseason program, the mini camp, it it's so hard on the offensive lineman and the defensive line. title: QB Plan vs Jets REVEALED, Gennings Dunker, Daylen Everette injured, Metcalf update | Steelers Rewind
text: What's going on everybody? Welcome back to Steelers rewind here on pennlive.com. Nick Fairball here with you all. The Pittsburgh Steelers back on the Southside. No longer in Latrobe. Training camp though still going. It's just has switched modes and switched areas. Um but let's talk about today. Um the first big takeaway of today, the quarterback rotation against the New York Jets. Will Howard will start. Drew Aller will get to follow him. No Mason Rudolph. No Aaron Rodgers. Um Mike McCarthy noted that he has seen enough of Mason Rudolph who has praise since the spring. Um we will see more of the young quarterbacks. I wouldn't be surprised if it's flipped against Buffalo where we see Drew Aller get the start just to have all three of those quarterbacks facing um kind of the same level of competition. Um so I do think that'll be big. Talk with Howard. Talk with Aller. Both of them kind of talking about how the simplicity of the offense in the preseason allows you to maintain your drops, your footwork, your mental processes. It really goes to the basics. And if you can master the basics of playing the quarterback position in the National Football League, you can do a heck of a lot of good. And I think that's the big thing that both those guys are focused on. So let's see how they look. You know, Will Howard even admitted he thought he got a little antsy in the pocket. Sometimes Drew Aller said he thought his footwork got rushed but he auto-corrected. We talked about that. Auto-correcting your footwork, that feels like something both these guys are doing and that quarterback school is helping them. So that'll be the quarterback rotation. The other news is some injuries today. This This rookie class, you know, Maxi Hontour still not practicing. Probably not going to play. Um there were a lot of guys that didn't practice today. DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman. Did catch up with Pittman and Metcalf. Both will be fine for week one. Feels like uh I don't know what what Metcalf's injury is. Pittman has a minor hamstring injury. I don't think it's going to be too bad for either of those. Not really concerned with anyone for a week one miss. But the two rookies that missed today, Jennings Dunker and uh Daylen Everett. Those are new. Um Dunker did not practice. He was seen by a trainer on Sunday off to the side. And who knows uh exactly what injury it is, Um but not having him out there today signals he will probably not play. Same thing for Daylen Everette. Again, both these injuries undisclosed, do not do not know what they are, do not think they are serious, but could hold them out for a preseason game, which is a bummer. You know, when you think about how good of a game Duncker's coming off of of the summer Daylen Everette's had, I think, you know, you feel that that that's a tough one. There wasn't anyone else, you know, from the usual injury list, like Brandon Aiyuk, Tequon Brisker, Sebastian Joseph Day, Israel Mukuamu. All these guys still out, so so they're all really taking it easy. The Steelers seem like they are going to look to the younger roster throughout the next few weeks. Caleb Johnson, you know, that's someone that we asked Mike McCarthy about. He said, "Yeah, we're probably going to see more Caleb Johnson." So, Caleb Johnson only five snaps against Green Bay. Maybe we'll see more of him against the New York Jets. Maybe we'll see more carries, and he'll have that opportunity to prove himself. Also, a lot of praise for Roman Wilson. Andy Weidl and Mike McCarthy talked today, and they think he can play outside. You know, McCarthy pointed to some of the explosives he made on go routes and post routes on the outside, in addition to what he's done in the slot. And they feel like he can be someone that's big-time. Now, I think Jeremy Bernard is someone that's going to play outside if they have an injury out there to Pittman or Metcalf. But I do think, you know, he's had a really good camp. Roman Roman Wilson's done a nice job, but if anyone's in wait-and-see mode and skeptical of it, I totally get it. But the praise is natural coming in to all of this. All right, folks, make sure to like, comment, subscribe, turn on the notification bell for more, and thanks for watching.

title: The Steelers Have a Drew Allar Problem (And It's Not What You Think)
text: So, break down podcast, he's Penn Live Steelers beat reporter Nick Farabaugh. I'm John Lucy. We are live on YouTube taking your questions for Nick as we put Camp McCarthy in the rearview mirror and look ahead to the Jets on Friday at Acrisure Stadium where we hope to see one of the two young guns actually starting the game. Uh and my what a a difference a week makes. Uh before Nick and I were talking about, hey, you know, a lot of excitement, a lot of hype around these uh young quarterbacks, but maybe possibly most likely the franchise quarterback is not on this roster. Now, we we have people talking about a direct succession plan from Aaron Rodgers to Drew Allar and that the stage is set for uh a franchise quarterback in the making. We need to pump the brakes a little bit, give Nick the floor, and let him fill us in on this dramatic turn about, you know, and some rumors that they thought Drew Allar was a number one draft pick, and everybody said they reached when when he they took him in the third round. So, Nick, you got to straighten this out, and I'm going to pull up the chat while you're doing that. >> I mean, yeah, I mean, you are correct in the fact that uh that is exactly what Mike McCarthy said on the Pat McAfee Show last week that they had a first-round grade on Drew Allar after his junior year. Um so, before this past year. Um but it was it it was kind of interesting, the whole the whole kind of sequence of these quarterbacks. It's like, okay, Mason Rudolph comes in, gets pressured a lot, and leads a 99-yard drive. They don't finish it, but leads pretty good drive all all things considered, and had a few really nice plays where he looked like Houdini ducking in there, almost caught almost a crazy touchdown by Jeremy Bernard if he just had the one foot in and didn't get pushed out. And then you see Will Howard come in and engineer what I I it probably the most impressive drive of the entire game when we're talking about the two-minute drill. text: Brock, what you think of the day today? How you guys did? >> Um, honestly, I don't think it was our best day. Um, feel like fundamentals and stuff were just a little off and whatnot. Um, so, that's how I feel about it. I love all of our receivers and stuff. I know we've had some some grinders of some practices, uh, you know, last couple days and stuff. I don't know if that had any effect or whatever on them today, but um, you know, it's it was one day at practice and they're going to bounce back and we're all going to be good. So. >> Brock, you had a you had a pass deflected and intercepted and stuff. Like once I got to throw away pass, you You only had maybe one or two interceptions all of camp. I think, you know, one of the more slept on guys in the league. Um so, I'm extremely excited that we have him and every single play like he's he's almost going to sack me, it feels like. So, uh he's done a great job all camp. >> All right. Thanks, guys. >> Thanks, guys. >> Had a little bit of a challenge lately with the defensive backs today. What were they doing over there? >> Yeah, it's hard to tell, you know, when you're in the battle, right, what's exactly going on. It wasn't you know, me intentionally trying to go in and punch the ball out on him. It was just accidental. >> Which of the the young linebackers stood out to you in the game against the Titans? >> Um a lot of I mean all of them. You know, I think everybody had had good good things and things to work on throughout that game. Um you know, Doug did a lot of good things in that in that game as well. Wallow has been phenomenal all camp. He had a really good track tackle out in the out in space. You know, Nick Martin blowing people up. Unreal. You know, so there was a lot of guys that did a lot of good things. I'm sure I'm missing somebody, but I liked what I saw from the group. >> Fred, those young guys learn from you and [snorts] Dre quite a bit. Do you find yourself trying to be a little bit more verbal in the meetings to try to kind of show them the way a little bit verbally? >> Yeah, I mean I speak up where I can, but you know, at the end of the day I try to lead by example more so than just by words. You know, I think words are cheap. I think every day you got to go out there with something to prove. It doesn't matter what I've done in this league or what Dre's done in this league. I think what makes us great is this our hunger for the game and wanting to prove ourselves every single day. And I think that feeds, you know, the rest of the group. It's a hungry group and KJ's done a phenomenal job as our our linebacker coach and Johnny obviously overseeing stuff as well. So, we all still got a lot to improve on and I'm I'm looking forward to just continue to get be at our best for uh week one. >> [music] [music]

text: Scary, scary line from Kyle Shanahan on the 49ers left guard competition here in LA. >> Uh still competition, you know, no one's really um completely made it easy on us yet. >> No one has made it completely easy on us. Translation, all three of the 49ers competitors at left guard have failed to win the job and San Francisco feels that there is a hole at that position. Now, they can still hope that Carver Willis, the rookie, takes significant strides forward. He's have been out of the concussion protocol for about a week. They can still hope that Connor Colby corrects some of the errors that are part of this regression that has moved him to second team action. They can still hope that Robert Jones knocks off some rust. But Chris Forster was already very matter-of-fact in his appraisal of Robert Jones this off-season. >> His biggest thing he has to work on is pass protection. He's a absolute starter I mean, absolute. He's freaking awesome, you know, in the run game. But third down, pass pro, and things like that. I don't care what position you can't play on third down, it's hard to be a player in the NFL. Cuz third down's the money down. You got to be able to show up on third down. That's where Donald probably had some of his problems last year, and that's the place where Rob has got to make sure he improves cuz that was a problem for him in Miami. Now, I don't know if that'll be a problem here. We'll see how it goes. He's working his tail off. He's >> He needs to be a better pass blocker. And if the book on him is that he is a good run blocker, yet a deficient pass blocker, it's not likely to change. That's why the 49ers have wanted one of these younger guards to take control of that job. Jones is interesting. He played for the Miami Dolphins under Mike McDaniel. And I just ran into Mike McDaniel here in Manhattan Beach. I'm on the pier at sunset. 49ers practice with the Chargers just up the road. Mike McDaniel's now Jim Harbaugh's offensive coordinator and he worked with Robert Jones running a 49ers type of offense in Miami where Jones is a power blocker was able to pick up the movement blocking and develop the reputation of being a very good run blocker both through movement and power but still the pass protection is the issue. Ran into the 49ers brain trust including John Lynch at the place where I got an awesome burrito here in Manhattan Beach. The 49ers have to stay here for a relatively long time. They don't play until Thursday night. They don't play until 7:00 p.m. Thursday night. That means they don't fly out till about midnight which probably means because of the noise curfew at San Jose Airport they're going to have to land in the middle of the night at SFO and bus back down to the South Bay where all their vehicles will be waiting. Now, I have to emphasize that not all is lost at that left guard position. In fact, we saw a massive run from Keelan Black. Welcome back to the 49ers lineup over the left side. Trent Williams, you could see that epic block. Nice video from Matt Barrows but it's the rookie Carver Willis who's in at left guard on that play. So, there's obviously some capability for the 49ers here. They are just uncomfortable with the overall body of work that they've gotten from the three competitors at left guard. It does make me wonder if the 49ers, you know, we can talk about veteran options right now but the the best one up until a couple months ago was was Joel Bitonio. Somebody long time league fixture at left guard. Somebody who played under Kyle Shanahan back when he entered the league in 2014 and Shanahan was the offensive coordinator of the Browns but Bitonio retired. So, the 49ers are now looking at the three options on their roster plus maybe some old friends who are still on the street. Speaking of Mike McDaniel, Daniel Brunskill, played for the Dolphins, obviously with the 49ers before then, still available. >> I don't know how long the list is, but he's one of the players that can say they've started at six different positions in the National Football League. >> And somebody like Laken Tomlinson, whom I talked to a couple weeks ago, got the bone spur in his heel cleaned up. He's still available, but 34 years old this season. 49ers very clearly would love if somebody who is already on that roster would step up and grab that position. They might also have to go to outside help at defensive end. The ugliest part of the 49ers practice against the Chargers was the edge setting on run defense. And we all know that the 49ers are currently missing Nick Bosa. There is good news on Bosa's return, though. >> Yeah, he's making a lot of progress and he's a lot less lot less irritation, soreness, and tendinitis, whatever you want to call it, than he had last week. So, we think he's going in the right direction and we'll see him similar to Christian. >> And that's a relief because the 49ers badly need Nick Bosa. They were a borderline top-five defense with him over the first two-plus weeks of 2025, and then especially against the run, they dipped into a bottom-10 to 12 defense after Nick Bosa tore his ACL. So, they badly need him to set the edge. Not just the rush the passer, but to set the edge. They did get Keion White back at practice yesterday, but not yet in team drills. He's missed a couple weeks with an adductor injury. He's probably going to start at the opposite edge because MyCole Williams very likely will not be available for the 49ers in week one. And Williams' specialty is exactly where the 49ers I thought struggled most mightily against the Chargers. It's how Keaton Mitchell and Amari Cooper with some very, very successful early runs in the practice on Tuesday where the 49ers just did not set a firm edge. Something MyCole Williams, when he commanded all those double teams last year, extremely high rated as a rookie, did at a high level for the 49ers. There's a reason why their run defense fell off precipitously when MyCole wasn't available. And what happened against the Chargers on Thursday is as soon as the 49ers couldn't set the edge early in practice, the Chargers were able to run play action. That's faking run action. And when the run action is so so effective as it was for LA, well, that set the 49ers DBs up to get cooked and it put the 49ers pass rush on its heels. So that the 49ers just have to find a way to to bolster this edge. And right now, the hope is that it comes through returns from injury, but Kyle Shanahan himself said that MyCole Williams is likely not going to be back for week one. If you keep him on pup into the regular season, he's got to miss at least the first four games. And I think it's probably trending in that direction. So you've got Bosa, you've got Keion White, you've got a new scheme with Raheem Morris. You're obviously going to be trying to play some of those outside linebacker types in five-man fronts to take advantage of the current lack of depth at defensive end, but maybe you're going to have to be even more aggressive if you're the 49ers to solve the current issue. Now, I hate to isolate problems to one position group, or defensive end, outside linebacker, especially when these position groups are as amorphous and adaptable as ever for the 49ers. But I think that you've got to stretch the analysis out to the interior. And there's a reason why the 49ers have called the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Vita Vea. And that is because whatever happens on the inside of the defensive line has a domino ripple wave effect on the outside of the offensive line. And somebody like Vita Vea, at 350 lb, with his ability to stop the run and rush the passer, he occupies blockers because of that unicorn ability to do both at that size. And that allows guys on the outside to more easily set the edge, more easily get after the passer. I don't think that Alfred Collins has been good yet this training camp for this preseason. We're going to see on Thursday night if he makes market strides from the performance in week one of the preseason against the Tennessee Titans, then you can start to say, "Okay, he was just getting his legs back underneath him. Big tall 6'7" body. Obviously takes a little bit more to to play with the lower center of gravity that's necessary." What do you do while you're out not playing to just sort of stay on top of the playbook and everything else the signals to to keep that going? >> Really just uh whether I'm you know, couple days I got to be out here at practice making the IDs IDs from the sideline. Um seeing the game, seeing the pressures. Um if I wasn't out here when I'm watching on film, just making sure I'm making the IDs. Um that helps a ton. I mean the mental rep aspect it's a cliché but you really can get good work if you're locked in from the sideline or watching tape. Um, so just trying to do that as much as I can to keep myself locked in not cuz you can relax really easy and then come back out here and just a simple pressure can beat you. So, making sure that I was locked in and uh felt like I did a pretty good job at that. Was comfortable out there today. >> Are you on any sort of pitch count at this point? I mean, what's sort of the ramp up? >> Yeah, they had me on a pitch count today. Um, I'm not sure what the ramp up plan is, my plan is to push it push it as much as I can. Obviously trust them and I know it's still we're still in August, so we have time, just being able to get I think I had, you know, 15 16 reps today was awesome. Hopefully we push that up to 20 25 and hopefully cleared fully soon. >> Is this the type of injury just thinking logically with your position we have to do? Is that something that you have to worry about down the road or is it just >> You know, or is it knock on wood on that? I I hope not. Obviously all injuries, yeah. I'll continue to do some maintenance. Um, really that kind of is the case with any injury at this point. You at a certain point in your career you have an injury that kind of just gets added to your maintenance and it really doesn't come off the list at any point. So, the maintenance list gets long at a certain point, but I'll stay on that for sure. Yeah. >> [laughter] >> Um, Nick Martin told us about how great you've been to him especially when you obviously weren't able to be on the field as a leader and just giving him pointers. How important has it been for you to kind of take that leadership role? >> Yeah, absolutely. I mean, the the leadership role of center is probably the my favorite part of the position. Um, and then just a guy like Matt similar uh draft pick as myself. Um, so I know what he's going through. It's he he just knows he deserves to be here. There's probably some doubts in his head, you know, when he gets beat on a game or something like that, but it there's a lot of talented players out here. So, keeping his head up with stuff like that and then also he's a he he has a lot of tools in his bag that he's been able to use really early. Trying to add a couple of things. Uh trap hand is one that some guys like, some guys don't. So, trying to add that to his game. Um but he's done an awesome job. Really good communicator at a young age. Uh really excited to watch him. >> And Sam Cosmi said that he thinks as a group maybe you guys don't get enough credit and he couldn't explain why. Do you have an opinion and could you explain why? >> that? >> Sam Cosmi. >> Yeah. He uh that's his opinion. I don't want any more credit. Just just do our job. We're we're fine. We play the offensive line for a reason. >> You talk about the mental reps and things like that. Is that even more important for you getting in sync with the guys on either side of you especially as you're learning this new? >> Yeah, absolutely. And just getting the mental reps with the different groups too. And you know, if I see a certain game out there or certain pressure, you know, talking to Sam, CP, uh Josh, BC, Julian, talking to all the guys and seeing how they saw it so that not only I see it on the sideline, but I see what the communication was between them out there so that when I jump back in, I can keep that communication the same. >> Last one, Connor. >> When you look at like you guys want to be more of a run team this year. You've had a little change up front in this amount of time. Now, Brandon's out there. Could it take a little bit of time to get that cohesion in the run game that you guys want? >> Um yeah, obviously all of that stuff takes time, but we've been getting a lot of a lot of really good reps in training camp. Um the concepts, I think they're we're very clear on the concepts on what we want. I think probably the last step in that progression is probably the three-step kind or the the three-man combinations. Two-mans, that's kind of basic ball. Uh everyone's done it plenty. Um but just, you know, having a play-side shade that returns and, you know, bringing the backside guard with me even though he also has to work with the backside tackle. So, probably the three-man combinations are the thing that will take the longest. Um and then matching those up based on the angle of the run, whether it's the wide zone, the inside zone. Um same thing with gap scheme combos. Uh so, I think we're we're doing a really good job. The Staple chain, uh they've done an awesome job uh in stone those combinations, how we want to run it, the desired look, and then giving us the uh option to change it up when we need to. >> Thank you. Last one. >> You just You've had to put your opinion out there with Jayden Washington from the sideline. >> What's sort of your your opinion of how he's done for Miami? How's he looking? >> Uh awesome. I think really when we got back here in April, um the inflection in his voice was has changed a lot. And I think that's kind of a thing that comes with age, it's a confidence thing. cuz you you do become old quickly in this league. Your third year, you're at the average age of the league. Um and I think the confidence that he has in himself, his cadence has improved a ton, which is awesome. I think that's a huge skill that we can use as an offense. he see I don't want to say it's more comfortable cuz I think he's always been comfortable in his position, but definitely more confident. Expects more of not only himself, but willing to ask more of the guys around him, which is another huge step for a quarterback to lead an offense. Um so, he's been doing a great job. >> Awesome. Thanks, thanks. >> Thank you, guys.

title: K Drew Stevens Speaks To The Media After Practice | Washington Commanders
text: All right, so you got your starting kicker. How'd that feel? >> Good. >> Yeah? >> Yeah, yeah. I mean, it did it feel it I mean, honestly, it kind of feels the same that I have been feeling, you know, in terms of the way like I approach it. But I mean, I mean, it feels good. I don't really know how much more to say to that. >> Kicking in the first preseason game, what was that experience like? >> It was pretty good cuz it well, the lead-up to it is not like college cuz in college it's like you have multiple practices and you game plan for that specific team. And like I mean, we put in our like a few packages, but just like the lead-up to it, it kind of just like it's just there like pretty quickly, so a little different. >> So I wanted to ask you like what is it like when you guys are trusting the way you have your kicking coach and what are some of the things that they were kind of telling you as you were kind of leaning on them? >> Yeah, I want to take this opportunity to give Jake some flowers here because obviously we're competing. He could have done He could have had every right cuz we're competing for a job to just lead me in wrong directions and like not be a good guy to me, you know what I'm saying? But he was. He I mean, he he pretty much I followed him more than I followed anybody else in the building. Like he was like, "Hey, like we're going to lift this certain way. We're going to go and do stuff down during this time." And like he did not have to do that at all. So I mean, props to Jake because he's a great guy and he did not have to be. Uh but in terms of like Tress and I, obviously they're like I actually I told Tress during practice that um the difference between him and my dad is closer than the difference between me and him. Like so it's a it's crazy that I'm playing with like a a 36-year-old, but uh learning from him is is pretty cool. I I like to ask questions to a lot of guys like that that have been playing for a while at a high level. And so I mean it's it's fun to pick his brain and he's seen a lot of kickers. Like so, I can pick his brain on that, too, and like learn a thing or two here and there. Cuz you never know, like you never know when you learn that thing that's going to change your game for the better, you know? >> So, are you surprised they made the call this early? >> Yeah, kind of. I I mean, I don't really see why they wouldn't just let us play the next two, you know? But that's not my place. >> What was the conversation like when the coach just told you? >> Uh coach Izzo called me on the phone and then told me. Cuz it was it was yesterday, obviously, uh is when I found out. And it was crazy because I was not expecting it at all. Like cuz I thought we were going to play all three preseason games and then do it, but I mean, shoot, like it's my first rodeo. I have no idea. I'm just trying to play good on the field, you know? I'm not I'm not worrying about off off-field stuff. >> Now, just with the kicking series that you guys have had in practice, where have you seen the most improvement >> Most growth? I would say uh I mean, easy terminology, just getting adjusted to how good the operation is. Because I mean, I thought I had like probably one of the better operations in college, if not the best, a few of those years in there. Uh and it's still like it's insane. Night and day difference between here and there. Like I'm not even thinking about it. Like I have no like it's basically kicking off sticks, which is why like whenever I hit warm-ups, I was talking to DQ today, when I hit warm-ups and I'm hitting a good kick, and then he's like, "Yeah, it's off sticks, like whatever." And I'm like, it's basically off sticks when I'm kicking with them, you know? But I don't know. I I feel like the mental growth is no matter it's a good or bad day. Uh I think the best place that I've grown is I haven't changed anything. Like I'm still sticking to what I believe is going to work. I'm not like lacking conviction in certain areas. I'm just I'm I'm believing that my thing is going to be good enough, you know. Um I would say it's almost the most important thing. I I would say it is the most important thing because like how many kickers in the NFL have you seen just bomb one like perfectly dead straight, you know? Like that means you're physically capable of doing it every time. So where's the disconnect? It's It's up here. So I think getting your mind right is like 100% the most important thing in kicking and being convicted is is showing true belief in what it is you're doing. So I mean I would say it's the most important thing is being convicted like I'll give you an example. Let's say it's like a right to left wind, but it's like kind of gusting. So it's like sometimes it's really strong and sometimes it's barely moving right to left. Then let's say you're standing back in your stance and you just lined up to aim it like pretty much down the middle and then you hear you feel a gust. What's your plan? You don't want to be sitting back there like, oh, do I play it out right or do I think it's going to stop gusting? You got to pick one thing like, all right, I'm playing my line and I'm going to just hammer it. You You can't You can't be like You can't have questions in the back of your stance. You got to be okay if it goes wrong as long as you you stuck to your plan. Yeah, I mean it's definitely different, >> but it's it's also easier because it's it's really good. Like it's it's a really good operation. Like I I remember the first day I saw your aunt like snap the ball and the rotation was off. Like you know on rotation we do it like a clock. So like 12:00 is laces perfectly straight pointed at the uprights. He snapped one that was like 10:00. So it's like a little off or 9:00 and he'll be like pissed. He'll be like, "I know I know you're you're fine with it, but like I got to get that right." And it's like it's crazy that that's like the standard that he's operating at. So I mean it's pretty easy to adjust when guys are are good and have done it. >> Did you talk to Jamie since yesterday? >> Yeah, he I mean like I said, he's a he's a he's a really good guy. Like he's a really good human cuz he did not have to it's just all the things he does not have to do that he does cuz like pretty probably 2 hours after I found out, obviously he had found out and he he still texted me he's like, "Hey man, best of luck. I'm here if you need anything." And it he did not have to do that, you know? Like he could have just not said anything. Like I'm sure some other guys have been like that, but I don't know. It's just a huge character thing when you do something like that, you know? So >> All right. Thanks for >> Of course.

title: RT Josh Conerly Jr. Speaks To The Media After Practice | Washington Commanders
text: I'm good, how are you? >> Good to see you. >> I'm curious to feel like now you've gone through this year, curious what how you've assessed your camp so far and knowing where you want to be. >> Yeah, um I don't think it's anywhere I want it to be. Um but it hasn't been bad. Um definitely a lot better than my first one. Um still cleaning up stuff day by day and I feel like I've made a lot of progress in my position and where I'm at and I think the guys around me as well have progressed a lot, so. >> Where do you think you guys are at with just trying to get that run game going? I know there's like there's a there's a process, right? So, where are you at with that? Are you seeing what you need to see? Or what do you want to see? >> Um just want to see the guys flying off the ball. Um I feel like that's the biggest thing for us is getting up to the line, breaking out the huddle quick, getting the communication down the line and running, you know? Um I feel like that's I feel like that's the biggest thing. Um and I would say that I feel like we're we're starting to we're starting to get there, you know? It's not there's never going to be a perfect day and we understand that and as long as we just continue to grind and grind, we'll get get the results we want, so. >> Hey Josh, you just said that camp is not exactly where you want it to be. What what are you still kind of working on? What what's not up to your standard? >> Um just my hands. I mean, I feel like the set the set's coming along. The set's looking all right. Um it's looking good. Um but as far as like my hand my hand usage and placement in terms of when I punch, I feel like it's where it needs to and then obviously like when I can get up to the line where like if we're breaking out if we're like to break out fast, like getting into the into my stance the right way that I want it to be. I feel like it's another big thing for me. Um just making sure the stance is consistent, running past, not giving away any tells. Um I feel like just for myself watching, like I can tell when I'm about to pass block when I'm about to run block. Um So, I mean, fixing those little cues and um I mean, I feel like hands running past as well. Just hands hands hands. That's I feel like that's my biggest thing for real. >> And obviously losing Laremy on the line, huge deal, we all get that. Just for you personally though, a guy who's been your mentor, who's How tough was that when you heard that you might, you know, miss a lot of the time of the season? >> Yeah, um I mean, it sucks. I mean, obviously we spent about like 3 months together in this offseason working together. So, I mean, it really sucks to just see all his work kind of just go out the window, you know? Um and someone I care so much about this game and his career and everybody around him, um it was yeah, it would it definitely sucked. But, you know, Bitchy's going Bitchy's going to step in and he's going to do what he needs to do. Um and and LC will get right, so. For sure. >> Josh, kind of on that same note, how does the rest of the offensive line have to step up, you know, losing Laremy for, you know, for the foreseeable future? >> Um I mean, we all have our individual positions that we have to play. Um so, I mean, I feel like we all we all just need to go out there and put the best brand of football out there every week. Um so, I mean, I wouldn't I wouldn't say there's no specifics on like who needs to step up where, but at the end of the day, we all just need to go out there and put our best effort out there on the field every day, so. >> I know he's working back from injury, but you got Nick Allegretti working at center this year. How has that changed the communication along the the line? >> Um I mean, Nick Nick is a great communicator. Um so, I mean, I I feel like he's not a natural center. Um and he enjoy he enjoys doing doing that and I feel like that's one of the better parts is that he enjoys having the ball in his hand and snap snapping and let's go, so. Yeah. >> Josh, what specifically did you learn from Laremy when you guys trained this summer and how can he still help you even though he's not going to be playing for the next couple months? >> Um I mean, obviously just giving me little pointers like he always has. Um but I feel like one thing I learned um this offseason was just that like you still need to lift heavy, you know, to put out what you want to put out. Um and to see that day in day out, like day after day, even on our off days we get a little something in and I feel like that that was the biggest thing is that it's just lifting heavy, so it translates onto the field, so yeah. >> And you've had a whole season under your belt on the right side now. How much more comfortable are you at right tackle than maybe last year? >> Yeah, a lot more comfortable. >> [laughter] >> Yeah, I I definitely I definitely say I'm a I'm a lot more comfortable in my stance and getting out of my stance as well, so yeah. >> We've got time for two more. >> Josh, real quick. Um, can you give us some insight into what it's like going against this D-line every day? >> Um, obviously they give us a lot of different fronts and looks. Um, so that So I feel like that's one thing in its own and then, um, obviously the the skill of everybody across the board, ones, twos, and threes. Um, everybody has improved as well as we have. Um, I feel like that's the best part is there's not a whole lot of drop off. >> Uh, Josh, obviously you you dropped some weight. Can you talk about that, that discipline, that, you know, it needed that you needed to have to drop some weight? >> Um, I mean, I feel like I I've weighed the same, um, like 310, 315, kind of a little bit above that for the last year. It's just making it look different. I feel like it's the biggest thing. Um, so with that, we're just eating a little bit cleaner, um, and, you know, staying disciplined on the weekends I feel like is a big thing as well, so yeah. >> Awesome. Thank you, Josh. >> Absolutely, man. Appreciate you guys. Appreciate it. >> Josh, can you sign my glove? >> [crying] Can you sign my glove?

title: HC Dan Quinn Speaks To The Media Before Practice | Washington Commanders
text: I don't know. I don't know. I don't >> All right, get rocking today. We'll get a good padded big session today with the guys kind of like our peak of camp in a lot of ways for reps in some situations, but um first one man, it's been like an incredible training camp honestly with the fans. And so last day of them today, I wanted them to know uh how hard their team is, you know, working for them and like like we felt their energy as fans. So that meant a lot to the guys. So all that said, let's get rocking, John. >> Can we get an update on some of the guys who weren't out there? Yes, I think it was Odafe, Caleb on Jordan, and then Johnny Newton. >> Sure. Um let's start with uh Caleb on. So he um injured his knee in the joint practice. Not significant, but we are being smart in that spot. Um Johnny Newton injured his pec during the game. He's currently in New York um seeing a specialist there. So I'll give you an update tomorrow after you know, their meeting. Uh Oweh has a strained calf. Um kind of the early phase of that. We're again just being smart there. Uh Jordan McGee, I think was the other one you asked about. Uh injured his shoulder in the game. Uh we'll hold him out this week. Um but nothing that's going to like linger into, you know, the season or anything like that. >> Is there a long-term concern for Johnny? >> It could be. I I have an update today um about, you know, like anytime they go see a specialist, you know, with a pec. So um it could be. >> And then uh for me, um the defense, what have you seen from them so far and what do you still want to see as you move forward? >> Yeah. Well, I think yesterday and you know, like there's a couple opportunities to get the ball and we did. So there was a time in a two-minute at the end, a punch out by Owen. So that part is improving, John. Um our I think just the awareness to to practice it, the process of going through that. Um I like where I'm seeing the different packages and the people going in and out and the disguises that go with that. Drontae's got a good job of when it's you know, an all-out blitz, when we're back and having those two look alike and that in fact was some of yesterday's, you know, emphasis, can they look the same but play out differently? And uh those would be a few of the things that I seen. There's still a number of spots, you know, like we're at safety and you know, different spaces to say where we at. So, but I do like you know, our mindset for ball that's improving and the different packages now that we've gotten more reps at it. We're starting to get more comfortable there. >> Good morning, coach. >> When guys come back from being out for you know, extended period like Nick Allegretti or someone like that, do you let them gauge where they are in practice or or is there a ramp up period for them that you guys monitor? >> a little bit of both. We do a ramp up for sure. What you don't want to do is be susceptible to a re-injury. Not just to that body part, but you know, like something else based on not having enough training to go. So, they do a good job in like our return to play format. So, there's obviously like the treatment phase and the rehab and then the return to play the on-field work. But yeah, we definitely limit the reps and then ramp that up as it goes. So, Nick was maybe at 15 or so yesterday and few more into it, but that's kind of the process that we go through and then we take it day-to-day and listen honestly to the player about where they were, how to go and then make any modifications. >> As far as running back room with with Henry Jr. playing as well as he did in Miami, is it something you guys are looking for more from him coming up against Detroit? >> I like the competitive group of where we're at and like about Bills had a good camp as well. So, between him, Ke'Shawn, you know, we've added Craig Reynolds yesterday to it. But specifically with Rob, I was pleased to see pass protection. We know he's got good hands. You can you see him come return and that. So, you know, what else can he do for third downs? That's a big deal. You have to be able to nail the pass protection and as a running back, that can be the hardest space. So, I was pleased to see that part coming together early. He's got very good quickness and vision. But yeah, I'm excited to see him, you know, over the next couple weeks. >> Hey coach, >> Good morning. >> three weeks into training camp second preseason game what do you see this team overall as a whole what do you like that's standing out and what are some things that you feel that you want to see? >> Yep so first start off with the things that are standing out I like the competitive makeup of the training camp practices that the guys have had done I thought they've really pushed it against one another so like even in a practice like yesterday when I highlighted the film there was one-on-ones from o-line to running backs to linebackers you know down to the wide receivers and corners in the red zone so I like the situational football that the guys have done you'll see some more of that today on some two-minute and four-minute at the end of the game so those would be two of the things that I'm pleased with and then the things I want to see cleaned up is like pre-snap mistakes you know we've had ball starts you know in practice we've had them in the game I'm just talking specifically to offense defensively kind of the same thing like a communication has to be on point in every single play so those are the things I'd like to see you get rid of that some of the self-inflicted penalty you know and those ones I recognize like when you're moving fast mistakes will happen but those pre-snap ones like we've got to get rid of that. >> Dan I know you're already high on the defensive line from what you've seen throughout training camp so far but last week you know going against the Dolphins in joint practice and then in the in the game that was really the first time you got to see them you [snorts] know competitive against another team after evaluating the film what were some of your takeaways from the defensive >> Um I like the versatility so we have you know the ability to be like in three down or five down packages four down packages so that takes training I thought Eric Kendricks has done a nice job with the interior guys you've seen Payne and JK out on the edges which like that's a nice match up to see that type of size and strength you know playing over tight ends we still need a lot of work from a pass rush and games and stunts that takes timing Um so days like today in the padded days helps the most for that. It's not something that you can do on air and be effective, you know, like think about a receiver or you know, running a route. So, those would be some things that I'm looking to see more of. Um it was nice to see the guys work together in the practice um because most of it was unscripted. Just, you know, play ball and see the guys go. So, those are the practices I like the most cuz that's the best time to evaluate them. They don't know what's coming. How are they going to play? So, um I thought we're making progress there and uh I like the work that the group's putting in so far. Um and sometimes like you said, like for instance today with KC and OA out, like the lesson is like, all right, here's the opportunity for some others. And then the second lesson is, you know that's the opportunity. What are you going to do with it? And so, I like although I don't love injuries at all, I do like when people recognize there's an opportunity and like, what are they going to do about it? And so, I like looking for that. >> Hey, good morning, coach. >> Um you've brought up Jayden Daniels in the in the camp that he's having um so far. So, can you just share, I mean, this is year three with you all together? Just what have you really specifically seen from him in this camp that I mean, I know of course he's year three in the NFL, but what do you really love about him? >> Um I love that he's decisive, you know, as a quarterback. Um he's got like a unique ability to put the ball in the right location. And so, not just to like a what's his completion percentage, but like what's the accuracy? And that's even above the completion percentage. It could have been a drop or something, but it was in the right location. So, I like that he's in a system that he is now at the line of scrimmage working more things. And so, that might be the biggest difference, Kandy, between, you know, the last couple years and this year is like him at the line of scrimmage and working through. So, um he's done a good job with cadence. That's not something that we, you know, we've done here before. So, those are a few of the things that don't show up on the stat sheet that he's doing a really good job with. >> And in terms of whether he how much, or any of the starters, have you all had that conversation? Have you made a decision on that yet? >> No, no decision yet. Um, but we'll go through today and into tomorrow and then we'll hit on to those um after we see kind of the health of everybody and where we're at. But, um he's throwing a really good camp. I'm very pleased with what I've seen from him. Um new system, owning it, being in charge of it. So, he's off to a hell of a start. >> Morning, coach. >> So talking to the guys both on offense and defense, a lot of what they're talking about with Dorance Armstrong and the new defense is how difficult it can be to pick up all the different changes that they have, disguises beforehand. When you're learning a new defense like this, what are you communicating with the linebackers, specifically guys who could wear the green dot that's most important? >> I think you want to make sure like when in charge, be in charge. In other words, if there's a check that has to be made, often times you guys have seen an offense say, "I'm going to a kill. I'm going to an alert." to make sure it gets to all the people. And so, as a signal caller on defense, you want to have that same demonstrative effect to make sure not just these, you know, four or five guys in front of me get calls, but the people on all the edges. So, the communication hub is really the the linebackers and the safeties. They're the ones that just have to be able to like relay the information quickly, be on the same page. And so, that's the group that spends probably the most time together cuz they have to be in sync, you know, much like a quarterback and an offensive line. >> Hey Dan, um in light of the the Johnny Newton news, where do things stand with Tim Settle at this point? >> Yes, so sorry I couldn't hit Tim on that. Um, so he's making good progress, got big marker in that return to play today of like if he can hit all those and we're hopeful as he gets into next week that we could start ramping him back up into practice. So, if he hits all the good spaces, you know, that would be a good good thing for us. >> And you've obviously talked about a competitive camp throughout. Um, for some of the starters like today will be like the first time in in full pads since the joint practice. How do you kind of factored in the practices with the preseason games in order to determine the level of physicality? Has anything changed I guess over the course of camp? >> Uh can you repeat the last part, Ben? Sorry. >> changed over the course of camp in terms of the the planning with the physicality? >> Oh, no. Okay, good question. Uh it hasn't been a change of plans. So, like going into it you wanted to make sure where could we put those practices to have the highest, you know, return for that space. So, the joints are obviously one, today's one, earlier ones to go. And so, each of those practices features a little bit more line of scrimmage work and not the the loose downs of second and longs and third downs, but actually like today we have a a short yardage period that's that type of emphasis. So, when I lay it all out, you kind of look to those days and then make the specific emphasis for it. >> Morning, Dan. >> Um you mentioned how much you've liked the competitiveness of of camp and and everything like that. Yesterday, you kind of huddled them a few times seem more so than usual. I guess what was kind of the tone of what you wanted to tell them? >> Um I wanted to make sure like this is what I want to see. So, at the one after like a special teams break and a hydration, I didn't love how we came out of the second half for the second half in our preseason game as much. So, I reminded them of that. This is coming out of halftime right now. So, we use that tent like a halftime, get hydrated. But like there's a process to go into that. So, I just didn't want to miss the moment to hey man, this is a third quarter. Like how are you going to go enter it? Are we mindful to go take our shot? Are we getting a pass break up when it's there? Those are the things that I'm tracking on a regular basis, so it was nice to see in the second half of the game the rush and the coverage I thought was the real factor in getting the interception. Certainly one with Al Woods and with Malik Byron inside hitting the quarterback and other stunt. So like when I see that in coordination, that's when I know we're at our best. But we've got a ways to go to be a true ball-hawking unit, but the process of getting there is good. You know, we can't just talk about the outcome. It's got to be how much how often how many shots how much are we thinking about it? Those are the things that I think the years that I've had like really good takeaway teams, it was all the time. It was in practice. It was in the meetings. It was just a way of life that we thought about it. And so I'm seeing signs of that. It's not everybody, but that's what I'm building towards. >> It's been a few years, but you were a coach when there were four preseason games and now three preseason games. How has that changed the way you approach preseason? >> Yeah, it's it is different. I would agree. I'm in favor of it, you know, like the regular season games. As much I love the preseason games, I love it for the new players that we spend so much time developing to see what's next? How are they going to go? And they're the ones that usually like I haven't had like tons of rookies like in their first preseason game and I really nailed it. It's like anxious, nervous, mistakes, and then it gets better and better. So there's value to that for sure. Um I would say when you had four, you kind of timed it up a little bit little bit more. And then a lot of times with four, I didn't have other joint practices knowing that you had other preseason games. So, now that there's three having two seems the appropriate amount to do with the joint and then one without. So, I don't know if there's any set way that's best, but it's definitely different and I'm sure um, one day it'll go to 18 and two and that will have some adjustments that go with it, too, but um, yeah, I'm in favor of the less and then more in the regular. >> Last two, uh, Nikki and Kevin. >> Um, with the number of guys on the D-line, the front seven really banged up, do you plan to bring in any other guys and what sort of your concern level >> Um, no. Right now, um, we added Mo Hurst um, yesterday or two days ago and thought Byron did a nice job like in his first action, Nikki, of getting up and getting to speed. So, uh, we're hopeful that, you know, Tim's going to be back here soon and the other guys aren't long-term. So, no other plans in the group that we've had so far. >> And then going back to um, who was it? Kevin's question about um, Jayden. And you mentioned his accuracy. Could you tell if he changed anything in the off season? Was that something that you guys urged him to work on? >> He worked extremely hard, but that's that's him like in that way. Um, I just feel like the pocket that he's in, his routine is right that, you know, the team around him of getting everything organized and ready for him to play. Um, like saw him this morning early getting ready with Chad. Like he's got a good routine, a good process and I think what we're seeing like is some of the result of that, but also his connection with the players, this much depth, this much route. They've spent a lot of time together, so it's nice to see even early on like he and Stef. Like Terry and he have all these time now, so it feels good to add in Stef into that group. Um, that's been a big deal. He might have 10 or 12 targets so far, Stef does, and I bet he has 10 or 11 completions. So, that speaks to also Jayden in the right spot, in the right location and also to Stef, when do I sit down? When do I try to beat this guy? And so, it's been nice to see that relationship grow, too. >> Kevin, last one for me, Brandon Coleman working with Laremy over the off season and now moving to left tackle. Have you noticed anything as he's come back to that position where you're like, "Oh, he picked that up from Laremy." or any traits that you've seen from him? >> Um they definitely work together even like through the off season of some time where Brandon was working guard and tackle when he did do some of that. that'd be a better one for him on like the specifics of it. Brandon's got really good feet. We can always feel that part of him. So, I think he's definitely comfortable at tackle. Like it seems natural in a lot of ways for him to be in that space. Um I don't know if I feel a difference spat, you know, in between, but that'd be a good one for him. But they've definitely spent a good bit of time together and I would imagine if you spend much time with Laremy, there's going to be some some tips to learn and some insight to gain um offense or defense. >> All right. >> All right, thanks everybody. >> That was bad. >> Yeah. >> I know it. I heard something about everything I said earlier.
